Both delegate to the registered `AgentFactory` (the loop registers it via `setFactory`); both reject with `'no agent factory registered (load an agent-loop plugin)'` (`index.ts:217`) when none is registered. Note `create()` re-traces the factory through the **caller's** context (`const ownerCtx = this.ctx`, `index.ts:406-414`) — so the fiber that calls `ctx.agents.create()` structurally owns the agent.

`CreateAgentOptions` (`index.ts:80-133`) — full field set:

|---|---|---|

cancel(cause: AgentCancelCause, options: CancelOptions = {}): void {
  if (!options.keepInbox) {
    this.inbox.clear()
    if (this.phase.kind !== 'idle') this.phase.wakeRequested = false
  }
  if (this.phase.kind !== 'idle') this.phase.abort.abort(cause)
}
```

Idle cancellation is a no-op and does not arm later work. The cause surfaces durably as `turn/end` with `reason: { kind: 'aborted', reason: TurnEndCancelCause }` (`session/types.ts:150-158`). ### Which event records user input

**Two durable events, at two different times:**

1. **`agent/inbox/spliced`** — appended **synchronously at delivery**, from `Inbox.mutate` (`inbox.ts:186`: `const event = this.session.append('agent/inbox/spliced', splice)`). Declared in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/src/types.ts:19-25`:

```ts
'agent/inbox/spliced': {
  target: InboxTarget
  start: number
  removedCount?: number
  inserted: UserMessage[]
  outcome?: 'canceled'
}
```

2. **`user/message`** — appended when the claimed batch **enters a step**, not at delivery. `SessionEventMap['user/message']: UserMessage` (`session/types.ts:264`), documented as "A user-role message on the model-visible surface: a direct human prompt (the queued message claimed for this turn), a synthetic `agent.inject()` context …". Written at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:283`:

```ts
this.session.append('user/message', message, { surfaceOp: 'append' })
```

So: `agent.followup(msg)` immediately produces a durable `agent/inbox/spliced`; the `user/message` event only appears once a turn opens and the pre-step admits the batch. A rejected pre-step closes a `turn/end { reason: { kind: 'blocked' } }` with no `user/message` at all (`agent.ts:267-269`).

`Session.append` signature (`session/src/index.ts:604-608`) — `user/message` is a `SurfaceEventType`, so the `SurfaceIntent` arg is mandatory:

```ts
append&lt;T extends SessionEventType&gt;(
  type: T,
  data: SessionEventMap[T],
  ...opts: T extends SurfaceEventType ? [opts: SurfaceIntent] : []
): SessionEvent&lt;T&gt;
```

## 3. Presets — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` (`ctx.agentPresets`)

A preset is a **directory holding one `agent.cordis.yml`**, mounted once per process under a standing dsh-scope key; each session joins by parenting its agent scope key to the mount (`README.md:5`). Optional `preset.yml` beside it carries display `name`/`description` only. Id must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` (the directory name).

**Validate a preset exists by name:** `await ctx.agentPresets.resolve(id)` — throws `UnknownPresetError(wanted, availableIds)` naming the available ids (`index.ts:217-219`). Broken presets still *resolve* (deleting/reading needs the row); the private `resolveMountable` rejects them with `PresetMountError` at mount time (`index.ts:233-239`).

**What a preset controls:** everything the composition's plugin rows register into the preset's scope layer — tools and prompt sections primarily (`README.md:7,35`). Not the model: model/provider come from `AgentOptions` / `installModelSelection`.

**Where to reference it during creation** — the *only* supported call site is the factory's `setup(agentCtx)` (`README.md:29-31`). The canonical two-phase shape is `composeAgent()` at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:1168-1189` — resolve the id **before** create (because `meta` is snapshotted before async setup), mount **inside** setup:

```ts
async function composeAgent(presetId: string | undefined): Promise&lt;{
  agentPreset?: string
  setup: (agentCtx: Context) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;
}&gt; {
  const presets = ctx.get('agentPresets')
  if (presets === undefined) { return { setup: (agentCtx) =&gt; { installSelection(agentCtx); return Promise.resolve() } } }
  const resolvedId = (await presets.resolve(presetId)).id
  return {
    agentPreset: resolvedId,
    setup: async (agentCtx: Context) =&gt; {
      installSelection(agentCtx)
      await presets.mount(agentCtx, resolvedId)
    },
  }
}
```

…then `meta.agentPreset = composition.agentPreset` and `setup: composition.setup` (`api-proxy.ts:1610-1619`). Note `ctx.get('agentPresets')` — a rosterless deployment composes nothing and is not an error.

The durable record: `meta.agentPreset` on the header names the preset the session *started* with; a blank-session switch appends `'agent-preset/selected': { agentPreset: string }` (`src/session.ts:26`). Reconstruction must use `resolveSessionPreset({ header, events })`, never the header alone (`README.md:41-45`). There is also a non-scoped cordis re-emit `agent-preset/selected(sessionId, agentPreset)` (`index.ts:180`) declared by the client-safe `./types` export.

**There are no `agent/*` turn/step events.** From `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/README.md:59`:

&gt; Turn and step boundaries and the model token stream are durable `session/event` facts rather than mirrored `agent/*` notifications. Consumers read `turn/*`, `step/*`, and `assistant/chunk` from the session feed

The complete live `agent/*` vocabulary is declared in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts:146-291`. All are scope-filtered on `Scoped&lt;Agent&gt;`:

| event | mode | payload | line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent/created` | emit | `{ agent }` | :159 |
| `agent/disposed` | emit | `{ agent }` | :168 |
| `agent/status` | emit | `{ agent, status: AgentStatus }` | :178 |
| `agent/inbox/inserted` | emit | `{ agent, message }` | :186 |
| `agent/inbox/claimed` | emit | `{ agent, message, turn }` | :197 |
| `agent/inbox/discarded` | emit | `{ agent, message }` | :205 |
| `agent/session-start` | emit | `{ agent, source: SessionStartSource }` | :217 |
| `agent/pre-step` | waterfall | `{ agent, messages, turn, step, signal }` → `PreStepDecision` | :231 |
| `agent/request` | waterfall | `{ agent, turn, step, signal }` → `LlmCallConfig` | :244 |
| `agent/request-error` | waterfall | `{ agent, turn, step, provider, failure, retryPolicy, signal }` | :260 |
| `agent/turn-stopping` | serial | `{ agent, turn, signal }` | :278 |
| `agent/error` | emit | `{ agent, turn, step, error }` | :290 |

`AgentStatus = 'idle' | 'running'` (`runtime-types.ts:50`), emitted on every transition; `running` covers turn close, checkpoint, and consecutive queued turns — it is **not** proof a turn is open (README:75).

**Turn counting** therefore goes through the durable feed, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/session/src/index.ts:76`:

```ts
'session/event'(this: Scoped&lt;Session&gt;, session: Session, event: SessionEvent): void
```

(siblings: `session/created` :54, `session/disposed` :64, `session/flush` :85 — parallel/awaited.) Count `event.type === 'turn/start'` / `'turn/end'` with `event.data.turn`; payloads are `{ turn: number }` and `{ turn: number; reason: TurnEndReason }` (`session/types.ts:243-256`). Steps: `'step/start' | 'step/end'` = `{ turn, step }` (`:254-256`). Turn ordering is documented at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/docs/architecture.md:63-90`.

For the "did that turn actually consume work" question — needed so a budget doesn't charge for no-op turns — `dsh-agent` exports `foldConsumedWork` (`src/consumed-work.ts:68`):

```ts

// ConsumedWork = { readonly end?: SessionEvent&lt;'turn/end'&gt;; readonly droppedUnrun: boolean }

### Delivering into an existing long-lived session's inbox

Two production precedents that are exactly your case (b):

**`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:279-300`** — reacting to a runtime completion event, with a wake budget, choosing `followup` (wake) vs `inject` (non-waking) by agent status:

```ts

**dsh-scope does not answer "which agent caused the currently-running code."** It answers "which scope key does *this context* carry" — a lexical/registration relation, not an async-causal one. `scopeOf(ctx)` returns the `ScopeKey`, which for an agent scope *is* the `Agent` (the registry builds carriers with `scopeTarget(agent, agent)` — `agent/src/index.ts:479`, `dispatch.ts:95`).

Propagation across async boundaries (`runWithInitiator`, `:640-670`): the operation runs inside `initiatorRuns.run(run, () =&gt; this.initiators.run(agent, operation))`, so every continuation of that chain inherits the Agent. The **exact** synchronous value or Promise is preserved; when the result is a Promise the run is held open until it settles (`:654-666`), which is what makes the drain accounting work. Nesting is isolated: "a child driver's continuations carry the child, while the parent continuation regains the parent as soon as `withInitiator()` returns" (README:28). `AgentLoop` establishes exactly one boundary per driver lifetime — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:192`:

Teardown states are `'active' | 'closing' | 'disposed'` (`:261`); a new boundary during closing/disposed throws `'agent initiator scope is disposed'` (`:641`), and a nested chain that triggers its own owning fiber's unload is released from the drain (`releaseReentrantInitiatorRuns`, `:688-694`).

## 1. Durable domain storage

### The architecture note is under `proposed/`, not `implemented/`

The path you gave does not exist. The real file is `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md` (331 lines, plus `.zh.md` and `.i18n.yaml` siblings). Every package README links to it at that `proposed/` path.

### Package family (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/`)

Per `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/README.md`:

| Package | Role | ctx key |
|---|---|---|
| `storage/` | Connects registered backends with typed data forms | `ctx.storage` |
| `storage-json/` | Stores data in JSON files | registers backend `json` |
| `storage-sqlite/` | Stores data in SQLite | registers backend `sqlite` |
| `storage-domain/` | Provides validated domain-record storage | `ctx.storageDomain` |

Three layers, and **a plugin uses none of them directly except the domain form**. From `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/storage.md:5`: the hub performs no IO itself — "backends own media, data forms own semantics, and product packages never touch backends directly."

### The service a plugin actually uses: `ctx.storageDomain`

Not `ctx.storage`, not SQLite directly. `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:35-39` declares `Context.storageDomain: DomainFacility`, and `:29-33` merges it into `StorageForms` so `ctx.storage.domain` is the same object (`docs/subsystems/storage.md:24`).

### Exact APIs

**Declare a domain** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/spec.ts`:
- `defineDomain(spec)` (`:79`) — pins literal types, **fails loud at module load** on a name outside `UNIT_NAME_RE` (`:80`), a non-integer/negative `version` (`:83`), a bad table name (`:86`), or a global schema accepting `null` (`:91`). The null rejection rationale (`:70-76`): `null` is the medium's "never written" sentinel, so a nullable global "could not round-trip".
- `domainTable&lt;K, V&gt;(schema)` (`:63`) — phantom compile-time key type; `readonly __key?: K` is "never present at runtime" (`:31`).
- `DomainSpec` (`:35-44`): `name`, `version`, optional `global: { schema, initial }`, `tables: Record&lt;string, DomainTableSpec&gt;`.
- **Record schemas are zod, plugin `Config` is schemastery.** Stated at `:6-7`: "Record schemas are zod (`z.infer` keeps types un-duplicated and the same schemas later project to RPC wire schemas); plugin `Config` stays schemastery."

**Open** — `DomainFacility.open(spec)` at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:100-156`. Ordered failures: `already-open` (`:102`) → backend route resolution → `facet-unsupported` (`:110`) → backend `version-mismatch`/`malformed-medium` → zod validation of every stored record producing `invalid-record` with table+key (`:121`, `:181-192`).

**Lifecycle is caller-owned** (`:93-96`): "the CALLER owns the returned handle and closes it via `Domain.close()` (typically as its own `ctx.effect` disposer)"; leftovers are closed by `closeAll()` at unmount (`:175-177`, wired at `:208-215`).

**Read/write** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/domain.ts`:
- `KvTable` (`:42-90`): `get(key)`, `entries()`, `keys()`, `size` — **all synchronous from memory**; `put(key, value)`, `delete(key) → boolean`, `update(key, fn)`.
- `DomainGlobal` (`:19-35`): `get(): G` sync, `set(value): Promise&lt;void&gt;`.

**There are no transactions.** The write model (`:2-8`):

&gt; Reads are synchronous from memory; every write queues on the chain, awaits backend durability FIRST, then mutates memory, then emits `domain/changed` — a rejected backend write leaves memory untouched (no divergence between reads and the medium)

`update()` is the *only* atomic read-modify-write primitive (`:83-89`): "`fn` sees the value current at its queue slot, so concurrent updates never interleave." The `storage-domain` README's Known Limitations names it explicitly: "**No cross-table transactions, secondary indexes, or multi-segment keys** — each write touches one record."

Because there are no transactions, a multi-write mutation needs a **recoverable pending marker** — see the workspace pattern below.

**Change event** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/events.ts:46` declares `'domain/changed'(change: DomainChanged)`. Union of `put` (carries new value) and `deleted` (no value); global writes use `table: ''`, `key: ''` (`:14-17`). Emitted strictly after durability, in write-chain order. Listener exceptions are **swallowed with a warn** (`domain.ts:251-261`) because "the commit point has passed."

### SCHEMA_VERSION conventions (SQLite)

Two orthogonal version axes, and this matters for your provider:

1. **Physical layout version** in `PRAGMA user_version`, one constant per SQLite-backed package.
2. **Per-unit format version** from `DomainSpec.version`, stamped in a `units` row.

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-sqlite/src/schema.ts:14-20`:

## 2. Config

### Mechanism: three coordinated pieces

**(a) A TypeScript `interface Config`** — the documented shape, one JSDoc per field.
**(b) A same-named `const Config` schemastery schema** — `z&lt;Config&gt;` from `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`. TypeScript's declaration merging lets both share the name.
**(c) Validation in the vendored cordis fiber**, not in the plugin.

Validation site — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:50-62`:

```ts
export function resolveConfig(runtime: Plugin.Runtime, config: any) {
  if (!runtime.Config) return config
  // TODO: async validation
  const result = runtime.Config['~standard'].validate(config)
  if ('then' in result) {
    throw new TypeError('Async config validation is not supported')
  }
  if (result.issues) {
    throw new ValidationError(result.issues)
  } else {
    return result.value
  }
}
```

It runs through the Standard Schema interface (`vendor/cordis/src/registry.ts:104`: `Config?: StandardSchemaV1&lt;any, T&gt;`, "Standard-schema validator applied to config before the plugin starts"). Call sites: `fiber.ts:643`, `:655`, `:747`. Critically, `fiber.ts:740-747` defers resolution because "**Config resolution may access injected services**" — which is what makes `!!js` expressions in cordis.yml able to read `ctx`.

**Two declaration forms**, per `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/AGENTS.md:5`:

&gt; service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace

- Function plugin → `export const Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({...})`
- Service class → `static Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({...})`

### The rule

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md:113` (verbatim; `CLAUDE.md:113` is byte-identical):

&gt; - **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.

Paired with `packages/AGENTS.md:12`: "**Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default... otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice."

This is the one `docs/config-catalog.md:444` cites for the rule. Service-class form, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:239-247`:

The three-mode contract, verbatim (`:24-28`):

&gt; Replay is the keyless default: boot real subprocess paths from recorded model responses and diff assembled requests, normalized protocol or transcript output, and persisted-log expected outputs. `record` calls the real API and updates fixtures and expected outputs; `refresh` replays committed scripts and updates current expected outputs. Replay/refresh never load `.env`; only record reads a key from the environment or root `.env`.

Concurrency (`:55-66`): replay runs files in parallel bounded by `DSH_SNAPSHOT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default `min(5, availableParallelism())`); **record and refresh stay serial** — "record spends real API quota per scenario, and refresh write-back harvests volatile values from fixtures already on disk, so concurrent writers would corrupt goldens."

### `record` vs `refresh` vs real key

| Mode | API key | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `replay` (default) | **never** | nothing |
| `refresh` | **never** | expected outputs only, from committed scripts |
| `record` | **required** for `recorded: true` scenarios | fixtures + expected outputs |

`record` skips authored (non-`recorded`) scenarios — `packages/test-support/acp-snapshot/src/suite.ts:209`: `if (recording &amp;&amp; !scenario.recorded) return true`. Rationale at `:81-88`: authored scenarios are "a live model won't reproduce" and are "NEVER re-recorded."

**A real `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is genuinely required only for:**
1. `pnpm run test:snapshot:record` on `recorded` scenarios.
2. `pnpm run test:e2e` — every suite self-skips via `describe.skipIf(!process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)` (`examples/headless-agent/tests/full-loop.e2e.ts:28`, `coding-task.e2e.ts:47`, `resume.e2e.ts:33`, `todo-write.e2e.ts:26`, `compaction.e2e.ts:27`, `code-mode.e2e.ts:352`; `examples/acp-agent/tests/acp.e2e.ts:100`, `hooks.e2e.ts:38`, `escalation.e2e.ts:123`).
3. Web e2e record mode — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:326-327` throws: `'web e2e record mode needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (env or repo-root .env)'`.

Keyless smokes pass a dummy so boot succeeds without a call: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ?? 'sk-dummy-for-boot'` (`examples/acp-agent/tests/acp.e2e.ts:53`), `'keyless-smoke-no-call'` (`examples/jsonrpc-agent/tests/keyless-smoke.e2e.ts:82`).

Some scenarios assert *credential failure* with deliberately bad values: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ''` (`headless.snapshot.ts:439`) and `'sk-\u{1F600}pasted-from-a-chat-window'` (`:479`).

Per `examples/AGENTS.md`, each example ships **both** a keyless smoke ("boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit") and a with-key smoke.

### The resolver-manifest rule, concretely

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md:102` (and identically `CLAUDE.md:102`), final clause:

&gt; Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.

**What "resolver manifest" means depends on which tree the file belongs to** — three disjoint groups in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/scripts/verify-cordis-config.ts`:

| Config files | Resolver manifest |
|---|---|
| `examples/**` (except app overlays) | `examples/package.json` |
| `apps/cli/config/*.cordis.yml` + app overlays | `apps/cli/package.json` **or any bundle manifest** |
| A bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml` | **that bundle's** `package.json` |

Discovery: `scripts/cordis-config-files.ts:13-18` globs `**/*cordis*.yml|yaml`, excluding `.claude/`, `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `**/*.i18n.yaml`.

The enforcement function, `verify-cordis-config.ts:364-386`:

```ts
function missingPluginDependencies(
  references: readonly PluginReference[],
  dependencies: Readonly&lt;Record&lt;string, string&gt;&gt;,
  manifestPath: string,
): string[] {
  ...
  return [...requiredPackages].flatMap(([packageName, locations]) =&gt; packageName in dependencies
    ? []
    : `${[...locations].join(', ')}: ${packageName} must be declared in ${manifestPath} dependencies`)
}
```

References are collected by `recordPlugin` (`:222-224`) from every `name` field — including nested `insert:` arrays and `cordis-plugin-include` `config.patches` entries (`:206-220`). So a bare plugin buried inside a patch's `insert` still counts.

**Concretely for `goal.cordis.yml`**: it names `@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal`; both appear in `examples/package.json:35` and `:95`. Adding a new bare plugin to any `examples/*` cordis.yml without adding it there fails the gate.

**Second, coupled rule** — `validateExampleResolution` (`:226-248`) *also* requires the package be in the **root `tsconfig.json` project references**:

```ts

```

This matches `examples/AGENTS.md`: "declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`."

**Special cases:**
- `appOverlayFiles` (`:35-39`): `examples/web-cordis/cordis.yml`, `examples/web-schedule/cordis.yml`, `examples/mcp-memory/*.cordis.yml` resolve from `apps/cli` instead — "these example files are overlays consumed by the built dsh app."
- App resolution (`:251-267`) unions `apps/cli` deps with **every bundle's** deps, because `healProfilesModuleFallback` links them.
- Per-bundle patches (`:268-278`) must resolve from that bundle's *own* deps — "per-layer resolution anchors on the bundle package directory."
- `CHOOSER_BACKEND_PACKAGES` (`:52-57`) is a hardcoded mirror of packages mounted by runtime string, invisible to yml scanning, so keyless Linux CI can't hide a dropped `-native` dep.

`verify-cordis-config` also validates entry metadata (`:40`: only `id`/`name`/`group`/`inject`/`intercept`/`isolate` are static fields — an `!!js` expression elsewhere "remains truthy data and silently changes composition"), source-plane resolution, preset/plane separation, and client-half declarations. Failure prints one line per violation and sets `process.exitCode = 1` (`:81-87`); success prints `verify-cordis-config: N config files passed.`

- `exports["./invariant"]` must be `{ types: "./lib/types/invariant.d.ts", default: "./lib/invariant.js" }` if present
- `files` must **exactly equal** the computed list from `expectedDshPackageFiles()` (`scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts:171-214`):
```ts
return [
  'lib/index.js',
  'lib/invariant.js',
  ...manifest.bin ? ['lib/bin.js'] : [],
  ...manifest.exports?.['./worker'] ? ['lib/worker.cjs'] : [],
  ...exportDefault(manifest, './client') === './lib/client.js' ? ['lib/client.js'] : [],
  ...,
  ...usesEmittedTreeDefaults(manifest) ? ['lib/types/**/*.js'] : [],
  'lib/types/**/*.d.ts',
  ...
]
```
`usesEmittedTreeDefaults` (`:240-242`) returns true when *any* export's `default` starts with `./lib/types/` — this is exactly why `jobs` (via `./brand`) and `tool-todo` (via `./client`) carry `lib/types/**/*.js`.

Also enforced: `packages/&lt;group&gt;/&lt;pkg&gt;` shape — a group dir must not contain a `package.json` and packages sit exactly one level below (`checkHierarchyShape`, `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts:384-400`).

### 1.3 tsconfig setup

Every package tsconfig is identical in shape. `packages/jobs/jobs/tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "extends": "../../../tsconfig.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "rootDir": "src", "outDir": "lib/types" },
  "include": ["src"],
  "references": [
    { "path": "../../../vendor/cosmokit" },
    { "path": "../../../vendor/cordis" },
    { "path": "../../util/brand" },
    { "path": "../../core/agent" },
    { "path": "../../core/session" },
    { "path": "../../runtime-diagnostics/invariants" }
  ]
}
```
`jobs-local/tsconfig.json` adds `vendor/schemastery`, `core/scope`, `util/timeout`, `../jobs`.
`tool-jobs/tsconfig.json` adds `vendor/schemastery`, `util/output-retention`, `core/system-prompt`, `core/tools`, `../jobs`.

**Aggregate face configs** — there is no group-level or per-family aggregate. Only two exist:
- `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.host.json:277-279`
  ```json
  { "path": "./packages/jobs/jobs" },
  { "path": "./packages/jobs/jobs-local" },
  { "path": "./packages/jobs/tool-jobs" },
  ```
  (`tool-todo` at `:286`, `runtime-diagnostics/invariants` at `:250`)
- `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.client.json` for browser-face packages.
- `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.json` is the program-less solution file (`"files": []`, references the two aggregates). Its comment forbids ever adding include/files.

Path mapping in `tsconfig.base.json` is glob-based per group:
- `:107-152` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-*/invariant"` list, containing `"./packages/jobs/*/src/invariant.ts"` (`:126`) and `"./packages/todo/*/src/invariant.ts"`
- `:240-…` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-*"` list, containing `"./packages/jobs/*/src"` (`:261`)
- `:84` a per-package explicit entry: `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs/brand": ["./packages/jobs/jobs/src/brand.ts"]`

The comment above the wildcard (`tsconfig.base.json:~232`) says: *"adding a package under an existing group needs no edit here. The aggregates' project references … stay explicit — TS project references have no wildcard form."* **A new group `automation` requires adding `./packages/automation/*/src` and `./packages/automation/*/src/invariant.ts` to those two lists.**

`scripts/project-reference-faces.ts` enforces that a reference never crosses into the wrong leaf of a split Host/Client project.

### 1.4 tsdown / build, and how `lib/` is emitted

Two-stage build:
1. `tsc -b tsconfig.host.json` emits declarations **and** JS into `lib/types/` (`rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`).
2. `tsdown` bundles from that emitted JS. Root `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsdown.config.ts`:
```ts
workspace: ['vendor/*', 'packages/*/*', 'apps/cli'],
entry: client ? '' : ['lib/types/{index,invariant,startup}.js'],
outDir: 'lib',
format: ['esm'], platform: 'node', target: 'es2024',
fixedExtension: false, dts: false, clean: false,
plugins: client ? [] : [typertPlugin({ mode: 'workspace', faces: ['host'] })],
```
So `lib/index.js` and `lib/invariant.js` are the tsdown bundles; `lib/types/*.d.ts` + `lib/types/*.js` are the tsc output. Actual on-disk `packages/jobs/jobs/lib/`:
```
index.js  invariant.js  tsconfig.tsbuildinfo
types/{brand,index,invariant,types}.{d.ts,d.ts.map,js,js.map}
```
`jobs`, `jobs-local`, `tool-jobs`, `tool-todo` **have no per-package `tsdown.config.ts`** — the root workspace glob covers them. A per-package override (e.g. `packages/schedule/schedule/tsdown.config.ts`) is only needed for non-default entry sets, and `scripts/package-invariants.ts:130-135` requires any such override to bundle `lib/types/invariant.js`.

Scripts: **no `scripts` field in any of these package.json files.** All build/test/lint is root-driven.

## 2. The Service Definition pattern

### 2.1 Context declaration merging

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/jobs/jobs/src/index.ts:29-33`:
```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
  interface Context {
    jobs: JobRegistry
  }
}
```

### 2.2 How the service class is provided

The Definition is an **abstract `Service` subclass, default-exported** (`packages/jobs/jobs/src/index.ts:62-71, 179`):
```ts
export abstract class JobRegistry extends Service {
  constructor(ctx: Context) {
    // `abstract` erases at runtime, so a composition row naming this package
    // would register a ctx.jobs with no method implementations and fail far
    // from the misconfiguration. Fail loud at load instead.
    if (new.target === JobRegistry) {
      throw new Error('@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs is the abstract job registry seam; load an implementation such as @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local instead')
    }
    super(ctx, 'jobs')
  }
  abstract start(spec: JobStart): JobId
  ...
}
export default JobRegistry
```
`super(ctx, 'jobs')` is what registers the instance — `vendor/cordis/src/service.ts:32-43`: *"Calls `ctx.reflect.provide(name, this, this[Service.check])`, so the service is unregistered automatically when the owning fiber unloads."* No `ctx.set`.

The Provider is a **concrete subclass, default-exported** (`packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:91, 123-129, 534`):
```ts
export class LocalJobRegistry extends JobRegistry {
  static Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({ ... })
  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
    super(ctx)
    this.maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner = (config as Required&lt;Config&gt;).maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner
    this.selfCtx = ctx
    ctx.effect(() =&gt; () =&gt; this.disposeAll(), 'jobs teardown')
  }
}
export default LocalJobRegistry
```

The Consumer is a **function plugin with named exports and NO default export** (`packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:21-22, 205`):
```ts
export const name = 'tool-jobs'
export const inject = ['tools', 'jobs', 'systemPrompt']
...
export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void { ... }
```
`packages/AGENTS.md:5` makes this mandatory: *"service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace."*

An alternative provide path exists in tests: `child.provide('jobs', probe)` (`packages/jobs/jobs/tests/invariant.spec.ts:51`).

### 2.3 `register()` returning a disposer

Root `AGENTS.md:104`: *"**Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer."*

Three concrete templates:

**a) Scoped-layer registry** — `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:281-305`:
```ts
onJobDone(listener: JobDoneListener): () =&gt; void {
  return this.layers.effect(this.ctx, layer =&gt; layer.listeners.append(listener), { label: 'jobs.onJobDone()' })
}
attachController(name: string): () =&gt; void {
  const token = Symbol(name)   // duplicate labels stay independently disposable
  return this.layers.effect(this.ctx, layer =&gt; layer.controllers.append(token), { label: 'jobs.attachController()' })
}
```
`ScopedLayers.effect` (`packages/core/scope/src/store.ts:226-266`) wraps `ctx.effect(function*(){ … yield () =&gt; { undo(); … } })` and returns the exact synchronous disposer.

**b) Tool registry** — `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1031-1062`:
```ts
/**
 * Register globally or in the calling agent scope. Scoped tools shadow
 * globals; duplicates within one layer and the reserved `run_code` name fail.
 * @param definition - tool schema, execution, and optional finalization/presentation callbacks.
 * @returns the exact disposer that unregisters the tool.
 */
register(definition: ToolDefinition): () =&gt; void {
  ...
  return this.layers.effect(this.ctx, layer =&gt; layer.tools.insert(name, definition), { label: 'tools.register()' })
}
```

**c) Invariant registry** — `packages/runtime-diagnostics/invariants/src/index.ts:136-197`:
```ts
register(packageName: string, installer: InvariantInstaller): () =&gt; void {
  if (this.registrations.has(packageName)) throw new Error(`invariants: package "${packageName}" is already registered`)
  const ctx = this.ownerCtx   // explicit origin so registrations stay owned by the service
  ...
  registration = ctx.effect(async () =&gt; { ... }, `invariants.register(${JSON.stringify(packageName)})`)
  return registration
}
```

Disposal proof is a required test — `packages/AGENTS.md:17`: *"Registry contributions prove disposal through the HMR-safety test required by testing policy: dispose the fiber and observe removal."*

### 2.4 Typed events: declaration merging + `@mode`

Root `AGENTS.md:106`: *"**Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`."*

**Two distinct maps.** The `jobs` family declares **neither** — it uses plain callback registration instead. Here are the exact patterns from packages that do:

**(i) Cordis bus events** — `interface Events` inside `declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis'`. `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:137-209`:
```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
  interface Context { tools: ToolRuntime }

  interface Events {
    /**
     * Allow, deny, or ask before dispatch. `next()` delegates to allow; ...
     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent's calls.
     * @param exec - the pending call (name, parsed arguments, caller agent).
     * @mode waterfall
     */
    'tools/pre-execute'(this: Scoped&lt;ToolRuntime&gt;, exec: ToolExecution, next: () =&gt; Promise&lt;PreToolDecision&gt;): Promise&lt;PreToolDecision&gt;
    /**
     * Observe the frozen, lossless-JSON final outcome. Listener failures are contained.
     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): keyed by `exec.agent`.
     * @param exec - the execution object that traversed the pipeline.
     * @param result - a deep-frozen snapshot of the final returned result.
     * @mode emit
     */
    'tools/result'(this: Scoped&lt;ToolRuntime&gt;, exec: Readonly&lt;ToolExecution&gt;, result: Readonly&lt;ToolExecutionResult&gt;): undefined
    /**
     * A tool was registered or unregistered ... An UNFILTERED registry-subject
     * notification, deliberately not scope-filtered dispatch ...
     * @mode emit
     */
    'tools/change'(): void
  }
}
```
`@mode` values observed repo-wide: `emit`, `waterfall`, `serial`. `@dshScopeScan unsupported` example — `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:51-53`.

**(ii) Durable session-log events** — `interface SessionEventMap` inside `declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types'` (note: the **`/types`** subpath, not the cordis module). `packages/schedule/schedule/src/types.ts:213-221`:
```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
  interface SessionEventMap {
    /**
     * Versioned Schedule mutation. The owning package validates the complete
     * session-local transition stream before accepting a candidate event.
     */
    'schedule/change': ScheduleChange
  }
}
```
`packages/llm/llm-retry/src/types.ts:7` and `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/types.ts:204` follow the same shape. The base map lives at `packages/core/session/src/types.ts:236-337`; `SessionEventType = keyof SessionEventMap` at `:340`.

**(iii) Projection keys** — `packages/todo/tool-todo/src/types.ts:15-27`:
```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection/types' {
  interface SessionProjectionStateMap { todos: TodoItem[] | null }
  interface SessionProjectionMap {
    /** The agent's current whole todo list ... or `null` before the first write. */
    todos: TodoItem[] | null
  }
}
```
`packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts:20` re-exports it as `export type * from './types.ts'` with the comment that this "keeps the module edge in the emitted index.d.ts, so aggregate programs consuming the declarations still receive the SessionProjectionMap merge."

**(iv) Merge-extensible domain maps** — `packages/jobs/jobs/src/types.ts:19-29`:
```ts
/**
 * Producer-defined job kinds. Plugins extend this map by declaration merging;
 * the registry treats every value as an opaque id namespace.
 */
export interface JobKindMap { bash: 'bash'; subagent: 'subagent' }
export type JobKind = JobKindMap[keyof JobKindMap]
```
Consumers extend it from a *test* too (`packages/jobs/jobs-local/tests/jobs.spec.ts:12-16`):
```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs' {
  interface JobKindMap { workflow: 'workflow' }
}
```

### 2.5 Config validation — exact mechanism

Schema library: **`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`** (vendored at `vendor/schemastery`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml:29` overrides it to `link:vendor/schemastery`). It goes in `dependencies`, not peer.

Two placements, both picked up by the Cordis Loader:

**Service class → `static Config`** (`packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:30-37, 92-98, 123-127`):
```ts
/** Configuration for the process-local job registry. */
export interface Config {
  /**
   * Maximum `running` plus `stopping` jobs per exact owner or in the shared unowned bucket;
   * omission defaults to 10.
   */
  maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner?: number
}

export class LocalJobRegistry extends JobRegistry {
  static Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({
    maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner: z.number()
      .step(1).min(1).max(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
      .default(DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS_PER_OWNER),
  })
  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
    super(ctx)
    // Schemastery validates and fills the default before constructing the service.
    this.maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner = (config as Required&lt;Config&gt;).maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner
```

**Function plugin → exported `const Config`** (`packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:31-53`):
```ts
/** Configures bounded `job_output` waits and completion-notice delivery. */
export interface Config {
  /** Wait duration applied when `job_output` sets `wait` without `timeout_ms` (default 30s). */
  waitTimeoutMs?: number
  /** Hard cap on any single wait; ... (default 10min). */
  maxWaitTimeoutMs?: number
  /** Whether a completion opens a turn on an idle owner (default `wakeup`). */
  completionDelivery?: CompletionDelivery
  /** Turns one owner may have opened by completion wakes ... (default 3). */
  maxConsecutiveWakes?: number
}

export const Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({
  waitTimeoutMs: z.number().min(1).default(30_000),
  maxWaitTimeoutMs: z.number().min(1).default(600_000),
  completionDelivery: z.union(['quiet', 'wakeup'] as const).default('wakeup'),
  maxConsecutiveWakes: z.number().min(1).default(3),
})
```

**Required-with-no-default** (`packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts:41-43`):
```ts
/** Schemastery configuration for the todo tool consumer. */
export const Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({
  allowParallelInProgress: z.boolean().required(),
})
```

Cross-field validation that Schemastery cannot express happens at the top of `apply` and throws (`packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:215-222`):
```ts
if (waitDefault &gt; waitCap) throw new Error(`tool-jobs: waitTimeoutMs (${waitDefault}) exceeds maxWaitTimeoutMs (${waitCap})`)
// A budget is a count of turns. `Infinity` would leave the runaway chain this
// field exists to bound unbounded, and a fraction never names a turn at all.
if (!Number.isSafeInteger(wakeBudget)) throw new Error(`tool-jobs: maxConsecutiveWakes (${wakeBudget}) must be a whole number of turns`)
```

Governing rule, root `AGENTS.md:114`: *"**No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability."*

## 3. Runtime invariants

### 3.1 `packages/AGENTS.md` in full — rules for a new package

The file is `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/AGENTS.md` (27 lines; `packages/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it). Complete rule list:

**Plugin/architecture rules (`:5-18`)**
1. `:5` **Plugin exports** — service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name`/`inject`/`Config`/`apply` and have **no** default export. Mixing makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace.
2. `:6` **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.&lt;name&gt;` for declared injections — the property proxy is topology-sensitive, `ctx.get` reads the global store.
3. `:7` **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient; boot a test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process.
4. `:8` **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Keep `Agent`/`Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces.
5. `:9` **One asynchronous operation = one lifecycle controller or transaction.**
6. `:10` **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, provider-specific behavior in the Consumer/provider. *Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller.*
7. `:11` **Require a current owner and need** for each abstraction/state machine/option/defensive copy/compatibility path.
8. `:12` **Require evidence for public choices.**
9. `:13` **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** No UI/transport/implementation vocabulary; pin stable model-visible text verbatim.
10. `:14` **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it** — schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, listener order are not enforcement; test denial through the executor.
11. `:15` **Publish state only at its commit point.**
12. `:16` **Apply bounds to the complete result** — test tiny/exact limits, oversized single chunks, multibyte byte limits.
13. `:17` **Registry contributions prove disposal** through an HMR-safety test: dispose the fiber and observe removal.
14. `:18` **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Verbatim:
&gt; **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`].

**Layout/naming rules (`:20-27`)**
15. `:22` **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, references each workspace dependency **plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`**; registers in **exactly one** aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits.
16. `:23` **`src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.**
17. `:24` **Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.**
18. `:25` README + JSDoc are part of the change; altered config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields update them in the same commit.
19. `:26` Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the canonical Model Experience format.
20. `:27` Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; packages with none need a justified allowlist entry.

Also relevant (root `AGENTS.md:105`): *"**Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, **not** service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct."*

### 3.2 Machine enforcement (`scripts/package-invariants.ts`)

Discovery is by glob `packages/*/*/package.json` (`:38`) — new packages are found automatically. Checks:

- `exports["./invariant"]` must be exactly `{ types: './lib/types/invariant.d.ts', default: './lib/invariant.js' }` (`:85-94`)
- `files` must include `lib/invariant.js` (`:95-97`)
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants` must be a `workspace:^` **peerDependency AND devDependency** (`:99-112`)
- tsconfig references must transitively reach `../../runtime-diagnostics/invariants` (`:120-128`)
- any `tsdown.config.ts` override must bundle `lib/types/invariant.js` (`:130-135`)
- `src/invariant.ts` must exist (`:169-171`)
- must not contain `@generated` (`:174-180`)
- **exactly one** `ctx.invariants.register(...)` call, resolving to a **local string constant** equal to the package's own name (`:209-229`)
- second argument must be the identifier `install` (`:200-204`, `:216-222`)
- must named-export `name`, `inject`, `apply` (`:230-234`); must **not** default-export (`:235-237`)
- an **empty** `install` body must carry the literal marker `No runtime invariant:` inside the declaration's leading comment (`:11-12`, `:265-276`)
- a **non-empty** `install` must accept the failure reporter as its **second parameter** and actually use that identifier (`:278-285`)

### 3.3 Real invariant file examples

**Non-empty (`packages/jobs/jobs/src/invariant.ts`, complete):**
```ts
/** Package-owned background-job snapshot invariants. @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs/invariant */

import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
import type { JobSnapshot } from './types.ts'

const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs'
const TERMINAL_STATUSES = new Set(['completed', 'killed', 'failed'])

/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
export const name = 'jobs-invariant'
/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
export const inject = ['invariants']

/** Validate the cross-field relationships in one registry snapshot. */
function validateSnapshot(snapshot: JobSnapshot, owner: Agent | undefined, fail: InvariantFailure): void { ... }

/** Install checks over current unowned records and every terminal snapshot. */
const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) =&gt; {
  for (const snapshot of ctx.jobs.list()) validateSnapshot(snapshot, undefined, fail)
  ctx.jobs.onJobDone((snapshot, owner) =&gt; { validateSnapshot(snapshot, owner, fail) })
}, { inject: ['jobs'] })

/**
 * Register the job-registry invariant companion.
 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
 */
export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise&lt;() =&gt; void&gt; =&gt;
  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
```

**Session-stream flavor (`packages/schedule/schedule/src/invariant.ts:29-45`)** — note the `jscpd:ignore` fencing, since the replay + `internal/dispatch` plumbing is intentionally shared:
```ts
/* jscpd:ignore-start -- package companions share replay and dispatch plumbing */
/** Install replay and pre-append validation for the owned event stream. */
const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) =&gt; {
  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) {
    validate(session.events, session.header.seedLength ?? 0, fail)
  }
  ctx.on('session/created', (session) =&gt; {
    validate(session.events, session.header.seedLength ?? 0, fail)
  }, { global: true })
  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) =&gt; {
    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
    if (event.type !== 'schedule/change') return
    validate([...session.events, event], session.header.seedLength ?? 0, fail)
  }, { global: true })
}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
/* jscpd:ignore-end */
```

**Explained-empty companion (`packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/invariant.ts`, complete)** — the canonical shape for the Provider and the Consumer:
```ts
/**
 * Package-owned invariant companion for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local`.
 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local/invariant
 */

/* jscpd:ignore-start */
import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import type { InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'

const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local'

/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
export const name = 'jobs-local-invariant'
/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
export const inject = ['invariants']

/**
 * No runtime invariant: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs/invariant` owns per-snapshot identity, status,
 * timestamp, and owner checks. This provider's admission decision uses private configuration and
 * must fail before a backend starter runs; `LocalJobRegistry.start()` enforces it synchronously
 * for current producers. Repeating an aggregate after publication would expose private
 * configuration solely to this companion and would not verify the fail-closed pre-start guarantee.
 */
const install: InvariantInstaller = () =&gt; {}

/**
 * Register this package's invariant companion.
 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
 */
export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise&lt;() =&gt; void&gt; =&gt;
  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
/* jscpd:ignore-end */
```
`packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/invariant.ts:17-21` is byte-similar with the Consumer reason:

## 4. Tests

### 4.1 Location and naming

`packages/AGENTS.md:24`: tests live at **package level under `tests/`**, never `src/__tests__/`. Vitest include globs (`vitest.config.ts:86-91`):
```ts
const testIncludes = [
  'packages/*/*/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}',
  'apps/*/tests/**/*.spec.ts',
  'examples/*/tests/**/*.spec.ts',
  'scripts/**/*.spec.ts',
]
```
Other suffixes route to other configs: `*.e2e.ts` → `vitest.e2e.config.ts`; `*.snapshot.ts` → `vitest.snapshot.config.ts`.

Observed naming conventions in these families:
| file | purpose |
|---|---|
| `tests/&lt;pkg-short-name&gt;.spec.ts` | main unit suite (`jobs.spec.ts`, `tool-jobs.spec.ts`, `tool-todo.spec.ts`) |
| `tests/service.spec.ts` | Service-Definition contract suite over a stub subclass (`packages/jobs/jobs/tests/service.spec.ts`) |
| `tests/invariant.spec.ts` | drives the `./invariant` companion via a probe service |
| `tests/loader-composition.spec.ts` | the mandatory real-Loader composition test |
| `tests/integration.spec.ts` | full agent-loop drive with a scripted mock model |
| `tests/projection.spec.ts` | session-projection registration + HMR removal |

### 4.2 Test utilities

`packages/test-support/` contains (each a normal package with `package.json`, `src/`, `tests/`, `invariant.ts`):
- **`agent-loop-testkit`** — `mountAgentLoopTestDependencies(ctx)`; used in `packages/todo/tool-todo/tests/integration.spec.ts:7,19`
- **`loader-smoke`** — `src/index.ts` + `src/agent-turn.ts`, the shared subprocess/direct-agent harness for keyless real-Loader example smokes
- **`llm-mock-server`**, **`llm-replay`**, **`acp-snapshot`**, **`client-runtime`**

For plain Cordis contexts there is **no shared helper** — every suite builds `new Context()` and plugs directly:
```ts
// packages/jobs/tool-jobs/tests/tool-jobs.spec.ts:22-30
async function setup(config: ToolTasks.Config = {}) {
  const ctx = new Context()
  await ctx.plugin(SystemPrompt)
  await ctx.plugin(ToolRuntime)
  const agentsFiber = await ctx.plugin(AgentRegistry)
  await ctx.plugin(LocalJobRegistry)
  const toolsFiber = await ctx.plugin(ToolTasks, config)
  return { ctx, agentsFiber, toolsFiber }
}
```
Scope helpers come from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope` (`bindScopeParent`, `createScope`, `scopeOf`) — see `packages/jobs/jobs-local/tests/jobs.spec.ts:7,20-32`.

The real-Loader template is `packages/jobs/jobs-local/tests/loader-composition.spec.ts` — it writes a temp `cordis.yml`, mounts `Loader` + `Include`, stubs `context.loader.internal.import`, then `await context.loader.await()` and asserts `context.jobs` is a `LocalJobRegistry` and that the yml-supplied `maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner: 1` actually bites.

### 4.3 The 100% per-file coverage gate

`pnpm run test:coverage` = `vitest run --coverage`. `vitest.config.ts:171-296`:
```ts
coverage: {
  provider: 'v8',
  include: ['packages/*/*/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
  exclude: [
    'packages/*/*/src/types.ts',
    'packages/*/*/src/bin.ts',
    'packages/*/*/src/worker.ts',
    ...  // long list of client/GUI-debt files
  ],
  // 100% or it doesn't merge (docs/testing.md: excessive tests are welcome).
  // Per-file so a well-covered big file can't subsidize a bare one.
  // Every v8 ignore comment must carry a reason — see the quality-gates Agent Note
  thresholds: coveragePartitionMode ? undefined : {
    perFile: true, statements: 100, branches: 100, functions: 100, lines: 100,
  },
  reporter: ... ['text', uncoveredLocationsReporter] ...
}
```

How existing packages reach 100% per file:

1. **`src/types.ts` is globally excluded** — this is exactly why `packages/AGENTS.md:23` insists `src/types.ts` contain only types. `packages/jobs/jobs/src/types.ts` and `packages/todo/tool-todo/src/types.ts` cost nothing.
2. **`/* v8 ignore next -- &lt;reason&gt; */` with a mandatory reason.** 600 occurrences under `packages/*/*/src`. Examples:
   - `packages/schedule/schedule/src/invariant.ts:23` — `/* v8 ignore next -- foldScheduleEvents normalizes every rejected stream to ScheduleLogError. */`
   - `packages/schedule/schedule/src/domain.ts:159` — `/* v8 ignore next -- successful fixed regexes always provide every requested group. */`
   - `packages/schedule/schedule/src/domain.ts:610` — `/* v8 ignore next 3 -- decodeScheduleChange returns a closed operation union. */`
   - The `jobs`/`todo` sources use **zero** v8 ignores — they are covered outright.
3. **Named `exclude` entries** in `vitest.config.ts` for platform-gated or GUI-debt files, each with a comment.
4. **`scripts/coverage-exempt.ts`** — heavy suites run *uninstrumented* in a parallel gate. Membership rule: qualifies only when every coverage-measured file it executes in-process is already fully covered elsewhere.
5. **`scripts/coverage-uncovered-locations.cjs`** — custom istanbul reporter printing exact `path:line:col` for every uncovered statement/branch/function, because "the built-in threshold ERRORs name only the file."

`docs/testing.md:10` on interpretation: *"An uncovered line is often dead code the gate is correctly flagging for deletion, not a missing test to bolt on. Line coverage is necessary, never sufficient."*

### 4.4 Other required tiers (`docs/testing.md`)

- `:9` Unit — *"Every registry gets an HMR-safety test (dispose the contributing fiber, assert cleanup)."*
- `:33` *"Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test."*
- `:47-49` **Snapshot required**: *"Every non-trivial model-, protocol-, or human-visible change adds or updates a keyless scenario in the same PR through a runnable example's owning snapshot suite."* A new model-facing tool means new/updated ACP snapshot scenarios under `examples/acp-agent/tests/snapshots/`, and — because both SDKs project the loop — updates to `examples/jsonrpc-agent/tests/snapshots/` and `scripts/snapshots/python-sdk-single-exe/` if `SessionEventMap` changes.

## 6. Adding a tool

### 6.1 `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md` — exact steps

The doc has no numbered checklist; it is a contract reference. Distilled:

1. **Minimal shape** (`:9-36`) — named-export `name` + `inject = ['tools']` + `apply(ctx)` calling `ctx.tools.register(defineTool({...}))`. *"Registration is effect-based: disposing the plugin fiber unregisters the tool. Schemas flow into the system-prompt assembly automatically."* (`:38`)
2. **`execute()` contract** (`:42-49`):
   - Args are pre-validated against `ParameterSchemaSpec`; hand-check only what the DSL cannot express (non-empty strings, positive numbers, cross-field rules).
   - Registration borrows the readonly definition — never mutate schema or swap callbacks post-registration.
   - Execution identity is protected: `callId`, `name`, `arguments`, `agent`, `token`, `signal`, `parent` are immutable through dispatch.
   - **Declare and return one canonical JSON value.** `output.schema` may have object/array/scalar/null root. Never return content blocks from the body.
   - Throwing or returning an invalid value ⇒ `isError`.
   - Honor `exec.signal`.
   - Optional `output.presentationMeta(args, value)` for replayable card data.
   - `exec.agent.inject({...})` for async notifications (not a wake-up).
3. **Long-running work** (`:53-55`) — gate `run_in_background` with producer config; `ctx.jobs.start({ kind, label, owner: exec.agent, run })`; return a typed handle like `{ kind: 'background', jobId }`; after `start()` publishes the id, use a **job-owned** cancellation signal, not `exec.signal`.
4. **Execution policy** (`:59`) — prefer `tools/pre-execute` / `ctx.tools.guard()` / `tools/execute` / `tools/post-execute` / `tools/result` over baking policy into the tool.
5. **Code Mode is free** (`:63-65`) — every visible tool is `await tools.&lt;name&gt;(args)`; design `output.schema` as a real programmatic API.
6. **Verification** (`:94`) — repository testing policy + the owning package's test docs.

### 6.2 Render-intent requirement

Root `AGENTS.md:126`: *"**A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args`."*

From `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:71-90`, both methods return a **`card`-tagged render intent**:

`presentCall(args) → ToolCallView`:
- `{ card: 'generic', title, kind?, rawInput?, content?, locations? }` — the default. `kind` picks an icon (`read`/`search`/…); `locations: [{ path, line? }]` for **any file your tool touches**.
- `{ card: 'terminal', title, description?, cwd? }` — the call *is* a shell command (tool-bash).
- `{ card: 'diff', title, diffs, locations? }` — `diffs: [{ path, oldText, newText }]`, `oldText: null` for a new file (tool-fs `write`/`edit`).

`presentResult(args, { content, isError, meta? }) → ToolResultView`: `generic` | `terminal` | `diff` | `search` (`shape: 'matches' | 'paths'`, plus `truncated`/`total`) | `web` (`kind: 'search' | 'fetch'`).

**Hard rules** (`:86-88`):
- **Purity** — these run on live streaming AND on session-log REPLAY; pure functions of `args` (+result). No I/O, no session state, no clock/random. *"If you find yourself wanting the file's old content or the working directory inside `presentCall`, stop."*
- **UI-only formatting stays out of the model result.**
- **`defineTool` soft-validates the display path** — malformed/older logged arguments make the wrapper return `undefined` rather than throw.

Type definitions: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/tools/src/presentation.ts:15,23,42,45,52,84,108` (`ToolCallKind`, `FileLocation`, `FileDiff`, `ToolCallView`, `GenericCallView`, `TerminalCallView`, `DiffCallView`), re-exported from the package root at `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:112-135`.

```ts

`defineTool` (`packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:483-547`):
```ts
export interface DefineToolOptions&lt;S extends ParameterSchemaSpec, O extends ValueSchemaSpec&gt; {
  readonly name: string
  readonly description: string
  readonly parameters: S
  readonly output: {
    readonly schema: O
    render(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;, value: InferValue&lt;NoInfer&lt;O&gt;&gt;): ContentBlock[]
    presentationMeta?(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;, value: InferValue&lt;NoInfer&lt;O&gt;&gt;): JsonValue
  }
  readonly timeoutMs?: number
  isConcurrencySafe?(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;): boolean
  execute(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;, exec: ToolRunContext): Promise&lt;InferValue&lt;NoInfer&lt;O&gt;&gt;&gt;
  finalizeContent?(exec: Readonly&lt;ToolExecution&gt;, result: Readonly&lt;ToolExecutionResult&gt;): ContentBlock[] | undefined
  presentCall?(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;): ToolCallView | undefined
  presentResult?(args: InferArgs&lt;S&gt;, result: ToolResult): ToolResultView | undefined
}

export function defineTool&lt;const S extends ParameterSchemaSpec, const O extends ValueSchemaSpec&gt;(
  options: DefineToolOptions&lt;S, O&gt;,
): ToolDefinition
```

### 6.4 `todo_write` registration, verbatim

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts:128-225`:
```ts
export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
  const allowParallel = config.allowParallelInProgress
  // The unit child activates only when a projection registry is composed ...
  ctx.inject(['sessionProjections'], (projectionCtx) =&gt; {
    projectionCtx.sessionProjections.register&lt;'todos', TodoItem[] | null&gt;({
      key: 'todos',
      stateSchema: todosProjectionSchema,
      init: () =&gt; null,
      apply: (state, event) =&gt; {
        if (event.type === 'todo/write') return event.data.todos
        if (event.type === 'turn/start') return null
        return state
      },
      wire: { viewSchema: todosProjectionSchema, view: state =&gt; state },
      stateVersion: 2,
    })
  })
  ctx.tools.register(defineTool({
    name: 'todo_write',
    description: describe(allowParallel),
    parameters: {
      todos: {
        type: 'array',
        required: true,
        description: 'The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.',
        items: {
          type: 'object',
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            content: { type: 'string', required: true, description: 'What the task is — a short imperative line.' },
            status: {
              type: 'string',
              required: true,
              enum: [...STATUSES],
              description: 'pending (not started) | in_progress (now) | completed (done).',
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
    output: {
      schema: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        properties: {
          todos: { type: 'array', required: true, items: { /* … */ } },
          counts: {
            type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: true,
            properties: {
              pending: { type: 'integer', required: true },
              inProgress: { type: 'integer', required: true },
              completed: { type: 'integer', required: true },
            },
          },
        },
      },
      render: (_args, value) =&gt; [{
        type: 'text',
        text: `Updated todo list: ${value.counts.pending} pending, ${value.counts.inProgress} in progress, ${value.counts.completed} completed.`,
      }],
    },
    execute(args, exec) {
      const todos = toTodoList(args.todos, allowParallel)
      if (!exec.agent) {
        // The list is per-agent-session state; a non-agent caller (no owning
        // session) has nowhere to write it. Reject rather than silently no-op.
        throw new Error('todo_write requires an owning agent session')
      }
      exec.agent.session.append('todo/write', { todos })
      const count = (status: TodoItem['status']): number =&gt; todos.filter(t =&gt; t.status === status).length
      return Promise.resolve({
        todos: todos.map(todo =&gt; ({ content: todo.content, status: todo.status })),
        counts: { pending: count('pending'), inProgress: count('in_progress'), completed: count('completed') },
      })
    },
    presentCall: args =&gt; ({ card: 'generic', title: 'Update todo list', kind: 'other', rawInput: args.todos }),
  }))
}
```

Note the DSL-inexpressible constraints handled in `toTodoList` (`:91-111`): trimmed non-empty unique content, and at-most-one `in_progress` unless the deployment allows parallel.

The `tool-jobs` pipeline-hook variant is at `packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:232-257` — a prepended `tools/pre-execute` listener captures the caller-visible job before policy, and each definition's `finalizeContent` applies the producer cap:
```ts
const outputLimits = new WeakMap&lt;ToolExecution, number&gt;()
ctx.on('tools/pre-execute', (exec, next) =&gt; {
  const maxBytes = visibleOutputLimit(ctx, exec)
  if (maxBytes !== undefined) outputLimits.set(exec, maxBytes)
  return next()
}, { prepend: true })
const finalizeTaskContent: NonNullable&lt;ToolDefinition['finalizeContent']&gt; = (exec, result) =&gt; { ... }
```
and the system-prompt section at `:263-267`:
```ts
ctx.systemPrompt.section({ name: 'tool:jobs', order: 106, text: 'Track every background job id you start. ...' })
```

### 7.4 How `pnpm run hygiene` reacts

`pnpm run hygiene` = `tsx scripts/run-gates.ts hygiene` (`package.json:133`). Gate set (`scripts/run-gates.ts:254-260` + `hygieneLeafGates()` at `:620-639`):

knip
publint

dsh-package-licenses

Note `hygieneLeafGates()` is called **without** `artifactNeeds` in the `hygiene` aggregate, so `publint`, `built-package-invariants`, and `node-next-types` assume `lib/` is already built — the cookbook's `pnpm run build &amp;&amp; pnpm run hygiene` ordering (`docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:115`) is load-bearing.

Concretely, a brand-new `packages/automation/*` package fails `hygiene` until:
- `package.json` matches every `check-workspace-constraints` rule (version, type, main, types, exports, exact `files` list, cordis peer+dev, non-private + publishConfig.access + repository)
- `src/invariant.ts` exists with `name`/`inject`/`apply`, exactly one self-registering `ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install)`, no default export, and either a real check using the reporter or an explained `No runtime invariant:` empty installer

- `tsconfig.json` references reach `packages/runtime-diagnostics/invariants`
- built `lib/` exists and its declarations compile under NodeNext
- `knip` sees no unused files/exports/dependencies
- if the package appears in a shipped preset, `python/sdk-runtime/package.json` lists it

All five methods are mixed onto every context at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/reflect.ts:222`:

## 2. Scope semantics — does a root listener receive a child-scope emit?

**Yes, always** (unless the listener context itself carries a scope tag that is not on the dispatch key's ancestor chain).

The mechanism is *not* context-tree bubbling. There is exactly one `EventsService` instance, installed on the root context (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/context.ts:80`), and it holds one flat hook table:

```ts
export class EventsService {
  _hooks: Record&lt;keyof any, Hook[]&gt; = {}
```
(`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/events.ts:131-132`)

`dispatch` (same file, 165-175) is the whole filtering story:

```ts
  dispatch(type: string, args: any[]) {
    const thisArg = typeof args[0] === 'object' || typeof args[0] === 'function' ? args.shift() : null
    const name: string = args.shift()
    if (!name.startsWith('internal/')) {
      this.emit('internal/dispatch', type, name, args, thisArg)
    }
    const filter = thisArg?.[Context.filter]
    return (this._hooks[name] || [])
      .filter(hook =&gt; hook.global || !filter || filter.call(thisArg, hook.ctx))
      .map(hook =&gt; hook.callback.bind(thisArg))
  }
```

Consequences:

- **A bare `childCtx.emit('x', …)` with no `thisArg` has `filter === undefined`, so every registered listener runs regardless of which context/fiber registered it.** Contexts do not partition the bus.
- Filtering exists only when the producer passes a `thisArg` carrying `Context.filter` (`vendor/cordis/src/context.ts:46`). Harness producers pass a **scope carrier** built by `scopeTarget`.
- `{ global: true }` listeners bypass filtering entirely (`EventOptions.global`, line 116).

`hook.ctx` is the *registering* context. That works because `EventsService` is a tracked service: its tracker is `{ property: 'ctx', noShadow: true }` (events.ts:135-138), and the traceable proxy returns the reading context for that property — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/utils.ts:176`: `if (prop === tracker.property) return ctx`.

### The harness scope filter

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:170-185`:

```ts
export function scopeTarget&lt;T extends object&gt;(base: T, key: ScopeKey | undefined): Scoped&lt;T&gt; {
  const baseFilter = (base as { [CordisContext.filter]?: (ctx: Context) =&gt; boolean })[CordisContext.filter]
  const carrier = {
    [CordisContext.filter](ctx: Context): boolean {
      if (baseFilter !== undefined &amp;&amp; !baseFilter.call(base, ctx)) return false
      const tag = scopeOf(ctx)
      if (tag === undefined) return true
      for (let cursor = key; cursor !== undefined; cursor = scopeParents.get(cursor)) {
        if (cursor === tag) return true
      }
      return false
    },
  }
  carrierKeys.set(carrier, key)
  return carrier as unknown as Scoped&lt;T&gt;
}
```

`if (tag === undefined) return true` is the answer to your question: **an untagged (root / ordinary plugin) context is admitted for every scope key.** A tagged listener is admitted iff its tag equals the dispatch key *or is an ancestor of it* — events flow **up** the parent chain, never down.

Pinned by `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/scope/tests/scope.spec.ts:93-110`:

```ts
    ctx.emit(scopeTarget(ctx, keyA), 'scope-test/ping', 'a')
    ctx.emit(scopeTarget(ctx, keyB), 'scope-test/ping', 'b')
    ctx.emit(scopeTarget(ctx, undefined), 'scope-test/ping', 'none')

    expect(heard).toEqual(['global:a', 'A:a', 'global:b', 'B:b', 'global:none'])
```

and by the ancestor test at `:195-220`.

`scopeOf` reads a private symbol own-property inherited through `extend()` (`packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:154-156`, tag written at `:140`).

### `ctx.on` lifecycle and disposer

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/vendor/cordis/src/events.ts:288-302`:

```ts
  on(name: string | symbol, listener: (...args: any) =&gt; any, options?: boolean | EventOptions) {
    if (typeof options !== 'object') {
      options = { prepend: options }
    }

    // handle special events
    this.ctx.fiber.assertActive()
    listener = this.ctx.reflect.bind(listener)
    const result = this.bail(this.ctx, 'internal/listener', name, listener, options)
    if (result) return result

    const hooks = this._hooks[name] ||= []
    const label = `ctx.on(${typeof name === 'string' ? JSON.stringify(name) : name.toString()})`
    return this.register(label, hooks, listener, options)
  }
```

and `register` (254-260):

```ts
  register(label: string, hooks: Hook[], callback: any, options: EventOptions): () =&gt; void {
    const method = options.prepend ? 'unshift' : 'push'
    return this.ctx.fiber.effect(() =&gt; {
      hooks[method]({ ctx: this.ctx, callback, ...options })
      return () =&gt; this.unregister(hooks, callback)
    }, label)
  }
```

So: the returned disposer is **the exact Cordis effect disposer**, owned by the *calling* fiber; disposing the fiber removes the listener automatically. `assertActive()` throws `CordisError('INACTIVE_EFFECT')` on a dead fiber. `once()` (312-318) wraps `on` and self-disposes on first call. Note the `internal/listener` bail escape hatch: a non-null result **replaces** registration and is returned in place of a disposer (used only for `internal/update`, events.ts:140-146).

## 3. Runtime enumeration / validation of event names

**There is no runtime registry that enumerates the complete set of declared event names for the active composition.** Four partial mechanisms exist; none of them validate a durable rule string against "the events this composition can actually emit."

### (a) `ctx.typert` — the real runtime registry, but opt-in and sparse

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-registry` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/registry/`). API summary from its README:

- `register(contribution)` — returns the exact Cordis effect disposer; rejects duplicate package-face or schema keys (`src/service.ts:499`).
- `getPackage(packageName, face = 'host')` → `TypertPackageRecord | undefined` (`src/service.ts:568`)
- `listPackages(filter?)` → `TypertPackageRecord[]` (`src/service.ts:577`)
- `get(key)` / `resolve(key)` / `list(filter?)` for live Zod schemas (`:527`, `:537`, `:558`)
- `toJSONSchema(key, params?)` (`:587`)

The event reflection shape (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/registry/src/types.ts:52-72`):

```ts
/** Runtime reflection metadata for one Cordis event. */
export interface TypertEventModel extends TypertDocumentation {
  readonly name: string
  readonly mode?: string
  readonly signature: string
}
…
/** Generated business reflection for one package on one face. */
export interface TypertPackageModel {
  readonly services: readonly TypertServiceModel[]
  readonly events: readonly TypertEventModel[]
  readonly objects: readonly TypertObjectModel[]
}
```

A real generated record (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/goal/goal/lib/typert.host.js:812-841`) carries `name`, `mode: "emit"`, `signature`, `summary`, `description`, `jsDoc`, and structured `tags` (including `{"name":"mode","comment":"emit"}`).

**Coverage caveat, measured:** only 7 real packages export `./typert` today — `context/file-reference`, `context/session-reference`, `host/plugin-inventory`, `feedback/message-feedback`, `extensions/cordis-host-runner`, `interaction/commands`, `goal/goal`. So `ctx.typert.listPackages()` yields a handful of events, not the 59 declared. Discovery is host-face only and cached for the process lifetime (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/loader/README.md`). `ctx.typert` + `dsh-typert-loader` **are** in the default composition (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:30-34`) but **not** in `examples/headless-agent/cordis.yml`.

What typert CAN do (README `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/README.md`, generator README):
- `generator/` — `WorkspaceAnalyzer` builds compiler-independent `FaceModel` + `TypeGraph` from `tsconfig.host.json` / `tsconfig.client.json`; `FaceModelEmitter` emits executable Zod schemas plus a `TYPERT` contribution; `WorkspaceTypertGenerator` discovers contributors "by walking package public exports reachable from Cordis `Context` or `Events` augmentations".
- `loader/` — follows `internal/plugin`, imports each Loader entry's `./typert`, registers until entry or plugin unmounts.
- `registry/` — the `ctx.typert` store above.
- Also exports `projectCordisCatalog(root, policy, face?)` for build-time projection (`generator/src/cordis-catalog.ts:359-394`).

## 4. Causal attribution — which agent caused this event?

Three layers, in decreasing directness.

### (a) The payload carries the Agent (14 of 26 scoped events)

Every `agent/*`, `tools/*` (except `tools/change`), `approval/request`, and `goal/changed` payload has `payload.agent` / `exec.agent` — this is exactly what the generated resolver map records (`scoped-events.generated.ts:11-36`). `agent.id === agent.session.id` is enforced at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:476-478`.

### (b) The carrier's routing key

Any listener on `internal/dispatch` receives the dispatch `thisArg`, and `carrierKeyOf(thisArg)` returns the `ScopeKey` — which for the shipped loop **is the live `Agent` object** (`packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:201-204`; `agentCarrier` at `packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts:94-96` is `scopeTarget(agent, agent)`). This is how the scope invariant attributes dispatches today (`packages/core/scope/src/invariant.ts:17-32`).

### (c) Ambient initiator via AsyncLocalStorage — `ctx.agents`

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:259-260`:

```ts

  private readonly initiatorRuns = new AsyncLocalStorage&lt;InitiatorRun&gt;()
```

- `currentInitiator(): Agent | undefined` — `:309-312`
- `requireInitiator(): Agent` — `:322-326` (throws `no initiating agent is active`)
- `withInitiator&lt;T&gt;(agent, operation): T` — `:341-343`
- `withoutInitiator&lt;T&gt;(operation): T` — `:356-358`
- `get(id: SessionId): Agent | undefined` — `:583-585`

The single production boundary is the loop driver, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:192`:

```ts

```

Other call sites: `packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:67,130` (`requireInitiator`), `packages/goal/tool-goal/src/authority.ts:56`, `packages/web/web-search-deepseek/src/index.ts:118` (`ctx.get('agents')?.currentInitiator()?.session.append(...)`), and two deliberate clearing boundaries: `packages/schedule/schedule/src/runtime.ts:110` and `packages/goal/goal-round-driver/src/index.ts:215`.

Rationale and constraints: `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md` — *"Initiator methods provide same-process causal attribution only. Ambient presence is neither liveness proof nor authorization"*; ALS does not cross worker/process/HTTP/queue boundaries; after service disposal the methods throw `agent initiator scope is disposed`.

### Does emission preserve the ambient async context? — Verified: yes

Every `emit`-mode dispatch in the harness runs listeners **synchronously inside the emitter's call stack**, so the ALS store is intact for the synchronous prefix of each listener (and, since ALS propagates across `await`, for its continuations too).

- Cordis core: `events.ts:194-196` — `this.dispatch('emit', args).map(cb =&gt; cb(...args))`. No microtask, no queue.
- Agent events, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts:119-137`:

```ts
    emit(name, payload) {
      // Cordis emit invokes callbacks through Array.map: one synchronous throw
      // starves later listeners, and returned promises are discarded. Agent
      // notifications are non-vetoing, so resolve the same filtered callback
      // set ourselves and contain both failure modes independently.
      const args: unknown[] = [carrier, name, fused(payload)]
      const callbacks = ctx.events.dispatch('emit', args)
      for (const callback of callbacks) {
        try {
          const returned: unknown = callback(...args)
          void Promise.resolve(returned).catch((error: unknown) =&gt; { … })
```

- Session events, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/session/src/index.ts:377-399` (`collectSessionCallbacks` + `invokeContainedSessionObservers`) — same synchronous `for` loop; `append()` invokes it inline at `:636-654`.
- Tools, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1657-1676` (`notifyResult`) — same shape.
- Settings, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:728-745` and `:778-798` — same shape, with an extra `INVARIANT`-coded rethrow after all listeners ran.

`parallel` (`events.ts:183-187`) invokes each callback synchronously in the first tick of its `async` wrapper, so the store is also live there; `serial`/`bail`/`waterfall` run the first listener synchronously and the rest as awaited continuations of the emitter's context.

**Important asymmetry:** `internal/dispatch` fires *before* listeners are resolved (`events.ts:168-170`) and for **non-`internal/` events only**. It receives `(mode, name, args, thisArg)` with the thisArg and name already shifted off `args` — and for waterfalls, `args` still contains the trailing `next` (it is popped afterwards at `events.ts:236`).
