## 6. Binding rules a new `automation/*` family must follow

### From `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-11-microkernel-event-taxonomy.md` (Status: implemented)

Verbatim decision text:

&gt; Pure Cordis event taxonomy. The loop's extension points are typed events with deliberate dispatch modes:
&gt;
&gt; - **waterfall** (around-middleware) where plugins transform, short-circuit, recover, or wrap: `agent/pre-step`, `agent/request`, `agent/request-error`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `llm/stream`, `system-prompt/assemble`.
&gt; - **serial** (awaited in listener order) for ordered checkpoints such as `agent/turn-stopping`.
&gt; - **parallel** (awaited fan-out) where every listener must get an independent chance: the `session/flush` durability checkpoint.
&gt; - **emit** (synchronous fire-and-forget) for notifications: inbox transitions, lifecycle, errors, and the contained immutable `tools/result` observation. Durable session events own turn and step boundaries.
&gt;
&gt; The event vocabulary lives in contract packages (`dsh-agent` declares the `agent/*` events); `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` is the only concrete loop plugin and is itself swappable — nothing outside it may depend on it.

Consequences that bind a new family:
&gt; - Every MVP feature maps to a listener (the feature → mechanism map is the proof obligation, kept current).
&gt; - HMR and disposal come free: listeners and registrations are Cordis effects.
&gt; - Waterfall semantics (call `next()` or short-circuit) are non-obvious and must be taught — documented in AGENTS.md and covered by composition tests.

### The domain boundary rule — `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-30-event-domain-semantics.md` (implemented)

&gt; **The boundary rule:** a durable, replayable fact is a `SessionEvent`; a live interception or a transient/live-object signal is an `agent`/`tools` Cordis event. A turn or step boundary is a durable fact, so it lives in the session log and is read off the `session/event` feed — it is NOT mirrored as an `agent/*` emit.

All four boundary mirror emits (`agent/turn-start|turn-end|step-start|step-end`) were removed; consumers read boundaries off `session/event`. An `automation/*` family that wants "on turn end" must subscribe to `session/event` and test `event.type`, not add a mirror.

### Ownership and naming (repo conventions)

- Event family prefix = the owning contract package's domain; the vocabulary lives in the contract package, not the implementation (taxonomy note above; `docs/architecture.md:45-61`).
- `AGENTS.md:105`: *"**Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`."*
- `AGENTS.md:103`: *"**Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer."*
- `AGENTS.md:107`: *"**Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain."*
- `AGENTS.md:108`: *"**Model-visible ⟺ logged**"* — anything reaching a model request needs a `SessionEventMap` entry, not just a bus event.
- `docs/cordis-primer.md:26`: *"The dispatch mode is part of the event's public contract."*
- Mechanical gates a new family must pass: `verify-cordis-catalog`, `verify-cordis-api`, `verify-scoped-events`, `verify-export-jsdoc`, `verify-doc-graphs` (regenerates `docs/event-producer-consumer.md`) — all in the `doc-sync` gate group (`scripts/run-gates.ts:657-671`).
- Scope: if the event is agent-subject, declare `this: Scoped&lt;Agent&gt;` with the literal `Scope-filtered dispatch` prose, put `agent` in the payload, and dispatch through `agentEvents(ctx, agent)` / `emitAgentEvent(...)` (`packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts:107,158`) — the scope invariant fails a bare dispatch: *"is a scope-filtered event but was dispatched without a scope carrier"* (`packages/core/scope/src/invariant.ts:21-24`).

### `2026-06-16-typed-event-schemas.md` — note the status

It is at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/.agents/notes/**proposed**/architecture/2026-06-16-typed-event-schemas.md`, not `implemented/`. Its proposal is **"Defer."** Key verbatim points bearing directly on runtime name/payload validation:

&gt; The pattern is **compile-time only**. The types vanish at runtime: there is no schema object to validate an incoming value against, parse untrusted input with, or enumerate at runtime.

&gt; **a plugin cannot declaration-merge a Zod schema.** Declaration merging is a TypeScript compile-time mechanism; a Zod schema is a runtime value. To validate events with Zod you need a **runtime registry** that every event-producing package contributes its schema to (e.g. `ctx.sessionEvents.register('compaction/marker', z.object({…}))`), and every consumer reads from.

Acceptance criteria: *"Option C proceeds only through its own implementation Agent Note, never as a persistence side effect."* Option B (schemastery on closed header/metadata shapes) is the sanctioned proportionate step. Open question it flags: *"Does the `ctx.invariants` service already cover enough of the runtime-shape gap when enabled…"*

---

### One-line summary of the load-bearing facts

There is exactly one flat, process-wide hook table on the root `EventsService`; scoping is *only* a `Context.filter` predicate on the dispatch `thisArg`, and untagged (root) listeners are admitted for every scope key. Emission is synchronous for `emit`-mode, so `ctx.agents.currentInitiator()` is valid inside a listener. Event names are enumerable at runtime today only from `EVENT_API` (build-time-generated static array of all 59 declared host events, repo-wide, not composition-scoped) or from `ctx.typert.listPackages()` (composition-scoped and mode-carrying, but only 7 packages publish artifacts); nothing validates a durable string against the *active* composition.</result>

## Deviations from the spec (and why)

1. **Session ids are branded `SessionId`, not `string`** (in `AutomationOwner`, `AutomationTarget` deliver, `AutomationRunRecord`). The spec's sketch wrote `string`; the repo rule "opaque cross-boundary ids are branded", the jobs template (`ownerSession?: SessionId`), and the named zod template (`workspace/src/spec.ts` uses `z.string().transform(SessionId)`) all point the other way, and it removes casts at `ctx.agents.get(target.sessionId)` in C2. Durable bytes are unchanged.
2. **No `src/types.ts`.** Every public type is `z.infer`-ed from `src/records.ts`, so a types-only file would hold nothing. (Consequence: no file uses the coverage exemption; `records.ts` is at 100%.)
3. **`AutomationRuleInput` is the zod *output* type** — `filters`/`causal`/`coalesce` are required on the type and filled by `automationRuleInput.parse()`. This is what makes the spec's `AutomationRuleRecord = AutomationRuleInput &amp; {…}` a complete durable record. **C2 must parse model/tool arguments through `automationRuleInput` before calling `create()`; `create()` never re-derives defaults.**
4. **Added public `AUTOMATION_EVENT_NAME_PATTERN`** (the spec only gave the regex inline); C2's tool description and tests need it.
5. **Non-emptiness beyond the spec's literal text**: `.min(1)` on ids, `label`, `plugin`, filter `path`, each `input.paths` entry, `presetId`, `eventName`. I deliberately did **not** enforce the "first segment is the argument index" path format — documented in JSDoc only, matching the spec's silence.
6. **Error/order contracts filled in where the spec was silent** but a complete JSDoc contract was required: `setEnabled` throws for an unknown or contributed id; `listRuns` returns most-recent-first (otherwise `limit` is undefined); `contribute` registers enabled and is invisible to `remove`. C2 should change these deliberately if it wants other semantics.
7. **Minimal dependency sets.** `tool-automation` depends only on cordis + schemastery + invariants (its C1 `apply` imports nothing else) even though it injects `tools`/`automations`; `automation-domain` depends only on cordis + schemastery + invariants + `dsh-automation`. Declaring `dsh-tools`/`storage-domain`/`agent`/`session` now would leave unused devDependencies for knip. C2 adds them with the imports **and the matching tsconfig references**.
8. `automation-domain` declares **no constructor** (inherited `(ctx)` is used) so an unused private config field cannot trip `noUnusedLocals`.
9. `files` is the 3-entry form (`lib/index.js`, `lib/invariant.js`, `lib/types/**/*.d.ts`) — correct because no export default points into `./lib/types/` (brands live in `src/records.ts`, no extra subpath export, the spec's "simplest" option).

First-call-order binding is safe regardless of interleaving: A claims script 0 on its first call, B is the only other live session.

**How session B's completion is awaited:** a scenario-local fence plugin, modelled on `subagent-settlement-fence.ts`. It records the agent id from the `todo_write` `tools/result` (the same synchronous point at which the provider queues its match), then holds *that* agent's `agent/pre-step` until a `domain/changed` write shows a run whose outcome is no longer `started`. Keying on the triggering agent id matters — a naive fence would deadlock session B's own first pre-step. # Adversarial review: event-triggered automation family

## (a) Confirmed defects, most severe first

### A1. A rule may name a **waterfall** event; the provider's listener never calls `next()` and silently vetoes that chain
`packages/automation/automation-domain/src/index.ts:411-417` subscribes with a plain listener that returns `undefined`:

```ts
return on(eventName, (...args: unknown[]) =&gt; { this.onEvent(eventName, args) })
```

Event names are data validated only by format (`AUTOMATION_EVENT_NAME_PATTERN`, `packages/automation/automation/src/records.ts:50`), and nothing restricts them to `emit`-mode events. `vendor/cordis/src/events.ts:234-243` composes waterfall listeners around the built-in `inner`: "a listener that does not call `next()` vetoes the rest of the chain, including the built-in behavior." This also breaks the repo rule "Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`" (AGENTS.md).

13 waterfall events exist (`docs/event-producer-consumer.md`), several load-bearing. Concrete, model-reachable outcomes from one `automation_create_rule` call:

- `event: "tools/pre-execute"` → the gate resolves `undefined`, and `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1475-1479` immediately reads `gate.kind` → TypeError on **every** tool call in the process.
- `event: "agent/request"` → the resolved `LlmCallConfig` becomes `undefined` → every model request in the process breaks.
- `event: "fs/write-intent"` / `"fs/edit-intent"` → `packages/fs/tool-fs/src/write.ts:111` receives `undefined`, which is exactly the "no policy" value; `packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/src/index.ts:116-122` deliberately occupies that same single decision slot. Depending on which listener registers first, the automation rule either **silently disables the read-before-write observation policy process-wide** or is silently shadowed (never fires) — an order-dependent, silent security/safety degradation.
- `approval/request`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `tools/execute`, `llm/stream`, `agent/pre-step` degrade the same way.

`bail`/`serial`/`parallel`/`emit` modes are safe (returning `undefined` is not a bail). The `contained()` wrapper does not help: the veto happens by returning, not by throwing. No test names a non-`emit` event (every suite uses `demo/event`), and neither the tool description (`packages/automation/tool-automation/src/index.ts:92-107`), the READMEs, the subsystem page, nor the note mentions the restriction — the tool text actively encourages the model to pick names by format alone.

### A2. Any throw between the reservation and `commitRun` permanently wedges a `serial` rule (the default)
`evaluate()` takes the rate stamp and the live-run reservation at `index.ts:544-545`. The only releases are `commitRun` (`:603`, non-`started` outcomes) and `finishRun` (`:380`, tracked start runs). There is no `try/finally`, so every one of these leaks the slot forever:

- `await this.runTable.put(...)` rejects (`:602`) — a durable write failure.
- `this.selfCtx.emit('automation/dispatched', ...)` throws (`:604`) because **any** listener throws; `ctx.emit` does not contain listener errors (`vendor/cordis/src/events.ts:194-196`), and the package's own invariant companion throws by design (`packages/automation/automation/src/invariant.ts`, proven by `packages/automation/automation/tests/invariant.spec.ts:82`).
- `await this.selfCtx.get('loader')?.await()` rejects (`:650`); `defaultModel.currentSelection()` throws (`:672`).

Consequences, all silent (one `logger.warn` from `detached`): the rule records `suppressed-coalesced` for every later match forever — a misleading diagnosis that hides a write/loader failure. Worse for `start`: the emit at `:604` precedes `handle.agent.followup(...)` at `:709`, so a throwing dispatch listener leaves a **created, tracked, live Agent that never receives its trigger message**, never opens a turn, never settles (`onSessionIdle` returns early while `turns === 0`, `:355`), and holds the reservation until the provider unloads. `prune()` is also skipped on that path.

The existing write-failure test (`packages/automation/automation-domain/tests/dispatch.spec.ts:504-516`) uses `coalesce: { mode: 'every' }` and asserts only the excerpt, so it passes either way and does not cover this.

### A3. Contract drift: the `agentEvents: 'ignore'` drop records nothing, contradicting the Service Definition
`index.ts:518` returns `{ kind: 'drop' }` — no run record, no event — and the outcome vocabulary has no `suppressed-agent-event` (`records.ts:198-210`). But the seam's own JSDoc, mirrored verbatim into `docs/subsystems/automation.md:45` and the definition README, says: "Every dispatch attempt that is **not a self-causal-chain suppression** commits one run record" (`packages/automation/automation/src/index.ts:81-84`). The agent-events policy is a separate, later gate; the carve-out does not cover it.

This is not merely wording. `agentEvents: 'ignore'` is the **default**, and reacting to agent-caused events (`tools/result`, `session/event`) is the common case, so the single most likely authoring mistake produces zero evidence — directly falsifying the note's consequence claim that under-firing is "diagnosable from its recorded `suppressed-*` runs" (`…2026-08-26-event-triggered-agent-automations.md:49`) and the subsystem page's "absence of effect is observable" (`docs/subsystems/automation.md:17`). Behavior is deliberate and tested (`dispatch.spec.ts:236-252`); either the docs or the outcome vocabulary has to move.

### A4. The kill switch increases durable writes instead of stopping work
The kill switch is checked first (`index.ts:506-513`), before the self-chain drop (`:514`), the deliver-self drop (`:515`) and the agent-events drop (`:518`), and before the rate limit (`:527`). While dispatch is off, every filter-matching emission — including ones that would otherwise be silently dropped — commits a durable run record, publishes `automation/dispatched`, and runs `prune()`. With the shipped example rule (`tools/result`, `agentEvents: allow`), engaging the "stop everything" control turns every tool result in every session into a domain write. That is the opposite of what a kill switch should cost, and it is unbounded by the rule's own rate limit.

### A5. Suppression records are not rate-limited, and `prune()` is O(n log n) per commit at the cap
`suppressed-rate-limit` records are written for every match past the limit (`:527-535`), so `rateLimit.maxPerMinute` bounds dispatch but not durable writes or `automation/dispatched` publications. Each `commitRun` past `maxDeliveredRuns` materializes and sorts the whole run table (`:614-626`). A rule on a busy event with `agentEvents: 'allow'` (exactly what the tool description tells the model to set for tool results) therefore amplifies one high-frequency event stream into one durable write + one emit + one 500-entry sort each.

### A6. Started Agents are never disposed after their run settles
`finishRun` cancels for `budget-canceled` but never disposes; `this.handles` is only drained in `disposeAll` (`:753-769`). Every automation-started Agent — completed, canceled, or orphaned — stays live, registered, and holding its scoped world for the process lifetime. `budget.maxTurns` bounds each run's *work*, not its *residency*. The README discloses it (`automation-domain/README.md:55`), so this is a design call rather than an oversight, but for the desktop runtime the note motivates (hourly rules, long-lived process) it is unbounded growth and deserves an explicit decision.

### A7. Teardown window: a dispatch can wake an Agent with no run record, and its handle escapes the provider's disposal
`commitRun` early-returns when `stopping` (`:601`), but `dispatchStart` continues to `handle.agent.followup(...)` (`:709`); and `this.handles.add(handle)` at `:690` runs after `disposeAll` already snapshotted and cleared the set (`:756-757`). Result: an Agent started and woken with **no** run record and **no** `automation/dispatched`, outside the provider's own handle set — a direct exception to the "every attempt commits one record" contract with nothing documenting it. In real compositions the agent-loop's `ownerCtx.fiber.assertActive()` (`packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:461`) makes `create()` reject once the fiber unloads, which closes most of the window; the scripted factory in the test harness does not, and the covering test (`dispatch.spec.ts:518-545`) only parks on the *preset-resolve* path, which settles before any Agent exists.

### A8. README overstates the loader barrier
`automation-domain/README.md:9`: "Dispatch awaits `ctx.get('loader')?.await()` so a match during startup waits for full composition." Only `dispatchStart` awaits it (`:650`); `dispatchDeliver` (`:717-735`) does not, so a deliver match during startup can record a spurious `skipped-target-not-live` before the target's plugin has mounted. Unexplained asymmetry between two parallel paths.

---

## (b) Plausible, not fully verified

- **Invariant false-positive on a mid-dispatch rule withdrawal.** `commitRun` publishes for a rule snapshot captured at match time; `invariant.ts:22` fails when `ctx.automations.get(ruleId)` is undefined. A durable `remove()` or a contributed rule's fiber disposing between the emission and the microtask makes a legitimate publication fail the invariant. `remove()` is not model-exposed, so the realistic trigger is plugin unload/HMR. Cheap fix: re-read `this.rules.get(rule.id)` in `evaluate()` (which would also stop a removed/disabled rule from dispatching a queued match).
- **Sanitizer fan-out.** `sanitize` (`matching.ts:79-96`) has a depth floor of 8 but no node budget, and the byte cap is applied only after a path is fully sanitized (`:124-125`). A cyclic plain-object graph with branching factor *b* costs ~*b*⁸ nodes. Class instances short-circuit at the prototype check, so this needs a wide cyclic *plain* payload — unlikely, but it is the one place where a bound is not applied to the intermediate.
- **Bound vs. what the model actually sees.** `maxExcerptBytes` caps `JSON.stringify(excerpt)`, while `renderDispatchText` emits `JSON.stringify(excerpt, null, 2)` plus a fixed wrapper (`matching.ts:140-150`). The complete emitted value is materially larger than the tested cap — worth a sentence, given the "apply bounds to the complete result" rule.
- **Serial coalescing is inert for `deliver` rules.** A delivered run settles at `delivered` inside `commitRun`, releasing the reservation immediately, so "serial" never holds a slot. The model-facing text says serial "drops a match while an earlier run of the same rule is still working" (`tool-automation/src/index.ts:336`), which reads as flood protection for a live target session that does not exist.
- **Cross-session observation and injection are unenforced.** A model-created rule can project arbitrary own-property paths out of any event's arguments (e.g. `tools/result` → `0.arguments`) and `deliver` them into any live session it names. Class instances are marked unserializable, and I found no credential in an event payload (`apiKey` only appears on `LlmModelDiscoveryRequest`, not an event), so this is not a secret-exfiltration path today — but it is a standing cross-session data route created by one tool call, with no approval gate anywhere in the family and no principal enforcement (disclosed in the note's limitations). Relatedly, the kill switch is model-writable in *both* directions: a misbehaving Agent can turn automation back on after a human turns it off (`automation_set_enabled`, `kill_switch: true, enabled: true`).
- **Run stuck at `started`.** If a started Agent goes idle without ever opening a turn, `onSessionIdle` returns early (`:355`) and the run never settles, wedging the serial rule until the Agent is disposed. `turn/end` is appended in a `finally` (`packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:316-323`), so a *failed* turn does settle — the exposure is a start dispatch whose message never becomes a turn (see A2), or an errored turn counted as `budget-canceled` rather than a failure.
- **A terminal outcome can be pruned away.** `finishRun` removes the tracked entry synchronously but writes the outcome in a later microtask, so a concurrent `prune()` no longer sees the run as live and may delete it; `updateRun` then rejects with `missing-key` and is swallowed.

---

## (c) Polish / nits

- `static inject = [... 'sessions']` (`index.ts:147`) — the provider never touches `ctx.sessions`; the agent factory owns session creation. The README repeats the requirement.
- Defaults have two homes in the tool: schemastery defaults (`tool-automation/src/index.ts:38-41`) plus `config.maxListedRules ?? 20` (`:234-235`), asymmetric with the provider's `config as Required&lt;Config&gt;`.
- `automation_list` never reports the global kill-switch state; `renderRules` prints `[on]` for rules that cannot dispatch. The service has `dispatchEnabled()`; the model has no read path.
- `limit` is unvalidated below 1: `Math.min(0, 20) = 0` returns nothing, and a negative limit reaches `slice(0, -n)`.
- The `causal` map never evicts (`:171`); one entry per started run for the process lifetime.
- Three always-on listeners (`:320-330`), including `session/event` — one closure allocation + try/catch per session append process-wide, even with zero rules.
- `automation/dispatched` for a `start` run publishes *before* the Agent is handed its message, while the event JSDoc says it is emitted "after the dispatch attempt settled."
- `SERVICE_PAGE` insertion in `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts:58` breaks the surrounding key ordering.

---

## (d) Test gaps (file + missing case)

1. `automation-domain/tests/dispatch.spec.ts` — no rule naming a non-`emit` event (A1 is completely uncovered).
2. `dispatch.spec.ts:504` — the durable-write-failure case uses `coalesce: 'every'`; no serial-rule variant proving the rule can fire again (A2), and no case with a throwing `automation/dispatched` listener.
3. `dispatch.spec.ts:110/144/206` — `dispatch-failed`, `failed`, and `skipped-target-not-live` are asserted, but no follow-up emission proves the serial slot was released.
4. `dispatch.spec.ts:379` — `budget-canceled` is proven, but not that it frees the reservation (only the `completed` path is, at `:355`).
5. `rules.spec.ts:94` — a contributed rule is proven to register, list, and withdraw, but never proven to actually dispatch.
6. No test for `remove()`/contributed withdrawal racing an in-flight dispatch (the invariant lookup in (b)).
7. No test for a started Agent that goes idle with zero turns (run stuck `started`).
8. `tool-automation.spec.ts:464` — `limit` larger/smaller are covered; `0` and negative are not.
9. No end-to-end test that `maxExcerptBytes` bounds what the started session actually receives (only the pure `buildExcerpt` unit).

---

## (e) Areas I checked and found sound

Gate order matches the note, subsystem page, and READMEs exactly (kill switch → self-chain → deliver-self → agent-events → depth → rate → coalesce). Initiator capture is synchronous in the emitter's stack and dispatch runs under `withoutInitiator`, so a started Agent never inherits the triggering initiator. Publish-at-commit-point holds for `create`/`setEnabled`/`remove`/`setDispatchEnabled` and for the run write before the event. Teardown order (watchers withdraw first via cordis LIFO, then handles → subscriptions → domain close) matches the JSDoc, and `disposeAll` is properly memoized. Causal rehydration correctly excludes suppressed and `delivered` runs. `contribute()`'s use of `this.ctx` is right (cordis service tracker rebinds `ctx` to the calling fiber), and disposal is proven. The sanitizer is genuinely good: exact-cap, one-byte-under, multibyte, cycles, sparse arrays, sibling preservation, prototype and `hasOwnProperty` walls are all tested, and `snapshotJsonValue` returns `undefined` (never loops) on cycles. The keyless snapshot is real end-to-end evidence: durable rule with `owner: {kind:'agent'}`, `[AUTOMATION TRIGGER]` `user/message` with `plugin/notice` provenance in the started session's persisted log, run `completed` at depth 1 in `.storage/automation.json`. `193 tests pass` (matching the note's claim exactly); `verify-agent-note-format`, `verify-package-invariants`, and `verify-doc-budgets` all pass. Generated catalogs (config, tool, event matrix, capability seams, module graph, website nav) are consistently regenerated, and the empty-invariant justifications in the provider and tool packages are specific and honest.

---

## Verdict

The change is unusually well-built for its size — the seam decomposition, the durable run account, the sanitizer, the teardown ordering, and the snapshot evidence are all above the bar, and the note is an accurate description of what shipped. But it is not ready to merge as-is: **A1 is a model-reachable way to silently break the harness's core dispatch chains** (tool execution, model requests, and — order-dependently — the filesystem observation policy), and it has no guard, no test, and no documentation; **A2 turns any transient write failure or third-party listener throw into a permanently and misleadingly wedged rule, and can strand a live Agent that never receives its work**; **A3** is a real contract/doc divergence that also defeats the diagnosability story the design leans on. A1 and A2 want code fixes (an event-name policy or a `next`-aware wrapper; a `try/finally` around the reservation plus a contained emit), A3 wants either a `suppressed-agent-event` outcome or corrected prose, and A4–A8 want the maintainer's explicit decision. Everything else on the list is safe to land as follow-up.</result>

## What changed, by finding

**A1 — waterfall veto** (`automation-domain/src/index.ts` `subscribe()`)
The data-named listener is now transparent middleware: if the last dispatch argument is a function it is treated as the cordis waterfall `next`, filters/excerpt run against `args.slice(0, -1)`, the match is handed off as before, and `return next()` returns the chain's value unchanged. The mis-detection caveat is documented on the method. Tests (`rules.spec.ts` › event subscriptions): a test-only `demo/waterfall` `Events` member with `next` is declared in the spec file; one rule on it resolves the inner value and still dispatches; two rules on it resolve the inner value with `next` invoked exactly once and both matches recorded.

**A2 — reservation/rate leak + stranded Agent** (`automation-domain/src/index.ts`)
`processMatch` now wraps the whole dispatch path in `try/finally` and releases the reservation on every exit except a started run the provider went on to track (`dispatchStart`/`dispatchDeliver` return that boolean). `dispatchStart` reorders to create → (stopping? dispose, warn, return) → `handles`+causal → `trackedBySession` → `followup` → write `started` → publish. A `followup` throw untracks, disposes the handle contained, and settles `dispatch-failed`. `commitRun` catches the write rejection, `logger.warn`s and returns `false` (a started+messaged Agent stays tracked). Publication moved into a contained `publish()` that catches listener throws with a `logger.warn` naming the event. `prune()` runs in the `finally` of `commitRun`'s write path. Tests (`dispatch.spec.ts` › the live-run reservation): rejecting put → next match dispatches and the first Agent kept its message; throwing `automation/dispatched` listener → followup delivered, `started` recorded, later settle works, next match dispatches; scripted `failFollowup` → `dispatch-failed`, handle disposed, slot freed.

**A3 — silent agent-events drop, counted** (definition `records.ts`, provider, tool)
`AutomationRuleRecord` gained type-only `ignoredAgentEvents?: number` (zod schema untouched — a new records test proves the durable schema strips it). The provider keeps a process-local `diagnostics` map, increments on the ignore drop, and merges counters in `get()`/`list()` only when non-zero. `automation_list` projects and prints ` (ignored N agent-caused matches)`.

**A4 — kill switch is a silent drop** (`records.ts`, provider, tool)
`suppressed-kill-switch` removed from `automationRunOutcome`; the gate now drops silently and increments `suppressedByKillSwitch` (surfaced exactly like A3's counter, including the rendered ` (dropped N matches while dispatch was off)` suffix). `automation_list` returns `dispatchEnabled` and renders a first line: `Automation dispatch is on.` / `Automation dispatch is off; matches are dropped until it is turned back on.` `SET_ENABLED_DESCRIPTION` and `renderAutomationState(false)` corrected. Old test rewritten: no run record, no publication, counter visible in `get()`/`list()`, absent from the domain's rules table.

**A5 — every durable write bounded by the rate window** (provider)
`rateWindows` now holds `{ stamps, marked }`. `takeWindowSlot` returns `taken` / `marker` / `exhausted`; the slot is taken in `evaluate` right after the causal drops and before the depth and coalescing decisions, so depth/coalesce suppressions consume slots and a dispatch consumes one at record time. An exhausted window writes exactly one `suppressed-rate-limit` marker (taking no slot) and then drops silently — bound: `maxPerMinute + 1` writes/publications per rule per window. Prune amortized behind `PRUNE_BATCH = 24`. Tests: marker-once-then-silence; depth + skipped + marker all counted against one window; window-slide resume; prune-at-cap+batch in both `rules.spec.ts` and `dispatch.spec.ts`.

**A6 — dispose started Agents at settlement** (provider)
`finishRun` disposes the run's handle (contained, via `disposeHandle`, which also removes it from `handles`) after the outcome write resolves. Causal entries are kept after disposal; `forgetCausal` drops one when its run record is pruned and its session is not live. Test asserts registry lookup gone, `disposals === 1` after teardown (proving it left the owned set), self-chain suppression still holding for the dead session id, and a fresh match dispatching. A second retention test covers both `forgetCausal` outcomes (dead session forgotten, live delivery target kept) end-to-end via a depth-1 re-dispatch.

**A7 — stopping-window race** (provider)
After `create()` resolves, `stopping` disposes the handle, warns, and returns with no followup/record/publication; `handles` and the causal entry are set before the followup. Test parks the scripted factory's `create` (parked after registration, before the handle returns) while teardown is parked inside the first Agent's disposal, then releases: second Agent disposed, no followup, only the first run on the medium.

**A8 — loader barrier symmetry** (provider)
`dispatchDeliver` awaits `ctx.get('loader')?.await()`. Test uses a new harness `loader` stub: nothing delivered and nothing recorded until release.

**b-fixes**
Withdrawal race: `processMatch` re-reads `this.rules.get(...)` and drops when missing or disabled; `publish()` skips (at `debug`) when the rule is gone, record still written — both tested (synchronous `withdraw()` before the handoff; and a parked-loader dispatch whose rule withdraws mid-flight → `delivered` recorded, `dispatched` empty). Zero-turn idle settles `failed` with `the started session went idle without opening a turn` (tested, including slot release). Finish/prune race: the run stays tracked until the outcome write resolves (`finally`); the test arranges the racy window through the rate-marker write path, whose put/prune is enqueued before the settlement's update. `static inject` lost `'sessions'`. `maxExcerptBytes` JSDoc notes the compact-JSON cap vs. the rendered message. `coalesce` model-facing description now says serial never throttles a delivering rule. `limit &lt; 1` rejected via `validateLimit` (tests for `0` and `-3`). Tool defaults read once through `config as Required&lt;Config&gt;`.

Definition JSDoc updated for gate order, the five silent drops, publication timing, the rate-window rule, `dispatchEnabled()`, and the `automation/dispatched` event. The invariant companion was left unchanged (the publish-when-present guard keeps it satisfiable).

## Deviations from the spec as written

1. **Prune stop condition.** The spec said prune "down to `maxDeliveredRuns`" from a snapshot `excess`. A burst of writes makes several passes overlap, and snapshot quotas then delete past the bound (this actually failed a test). The loop instead re-checks `this.runTable.size &lt;= this.maxDeliveredRuns` before each delete. Single-pass behavior is identical.
2. **`TrackedRun.handle` is no longer optional.** Only started runs are tracked and they always carry a handle; the `undefined` arm of A6's disposal call was unreachable dead branch under the 100% gate.
3. **`finishRun` disposes on every settlement**, including the new zero-turn `failed` — A6 enumerated `completed`/`budget-canceled`, which were the only settled outcomes at the time.
4. **`suppressedByKillSwitch` is also rendered per rule** in `automation_list`, reading A4's "surfaced exactly like A3's counter" to include A3's rendering. A4 only explicitly named the global header line.
5. **`dispatch-failed` after a failed followup records no `sessionId`** (the session is disposed immediately); the spec did not say either way.
6. The tool test `applies the built-in listing bounds when apply() receives a bare config` was replaced — it asserted exactly the `?? 20` fallbacks the spec deletes.

## For the orchestrator

Ripples outside my scope that will need regeneration or rewriting: `docs/tool-catalog.*` (all three tool descriptions, `automation_list` output schema gained `dispatchEnabled` and the two counter fields), `docs/config-catalog.*` (`maxExcerptBytes`, `maxDeliveredRuns`), `docs/event-producer-consumer.*` and `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts` (`automation/dispatched` JSDoc), the three package READMEs (kill-switch semantics, the removed `suppressed-kill-switch` outcome, the rate-window rule, publication timing, silent drops, the counters, prune amortization), and the cordis/module catalogs (`static inject` lost `'sessions'`). `examples/headless-agent/tests/headless.snapshot.ts` and its expected outputs are likely to move: started Agents are now disposed when their run settles, the publication lands after the Agent has its message, and a kill-switched match writes no run. ### API

Module doc (lines 6–9) states why merges must target this entry module: *"SlotMap and the standard-kit interfaces live directly in this entry module: consumer `declare module` augmentation merges with declarations lexically in the augmented module, not with re-exports."* The same pattern is used for `LocaleNamespaceMap` (line 34), `SessionStandardProps` (184), `SessionMaybeStandardProps` (191), `GlobalStandardProps` (198).

**Axes.** `SlotKind = 'single' | 'list' | 'keyed' | 'chain'` (line 88); `SlotScope = 'root' | 'session-maybe' | 'session'` (line 91). One `SlotMap` entry is a `SlotEntryDef` (lines 100–122): `kind`, `scope`, optional `owner`, `keyProps` (keyed prop table), `hookContext`, `inject` (slot-level inject face).

**register signature** — two overloads on `SlotCore`, lines 741–786 (inject-free and inject-bearing), implementation at 787. Options (`BaseOptions`, lines 526–550): `name`, `children?`, `store?`, `locale?`, `registrant?` plus `KindOptions` (lines 480–509): keyed → `key` + optional `priority`; list → `id`, `order?`, `label?`, `priority?`; chain → `select` (mandatory) + `priority?`; single → `priority?`. JSDoc at 706–737 states load-time validation and shadowing:

&gt; *"registering into an undeclared slot throws; declaring an already-declared child key throws (one declarer per slot — the message names the first declarer); mounting one shared store handle under slots of different scopes throws… entries sharing one cell … coexist at distinct priorities … A second registration at an occupied cell's exact priority (default 0) throws naming the occupant"*
&gt; *"Lifecycle: the disposer removes the contribution AND collapses every declared child slot (child entries clear recursively; their stale disposers become no-ops)"*

**Keyed slots.** `EntryKeyOf&lt;K&gt;` (152) narrows the key domain from `keyProps`; `KeyPropsOf&lt;K, EntryKey&gt;` (158) supplies key-dependent owner props. Runtime check at line 806: `if (options.key === undefined) throw new Error(\`keyed slot "${options.name}" requires options.key\`)`.

**Owner data.** `OwnerOf&lt;K&gt;` (148) = `SlotMap[K]['owner']` or `object`. `PropsRuntime&lt;K, EntryKey&gt;` (211–221) = `OwnerOf&lt;K&gt; &amp; KeyPropsOf&lt;…&gt; &amp; SlotInjectFace&lt;…&gt; &amp; (session kit by scope) &amp; GlobalStandardProps`. `renderSlot(key, owner, opts?)` typed by `RenderSlotFn` (275–295); chain slots dispatch via `renderSlotChain` (357).


**Does it own `root`?** No — `root` is declared by the runtime and seeded by `SlotCore`'s constructor (`packages/client/ui-slots/src/index.ts:698–704`; SlotMap merge at `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:41`). ui-layout **registers into** it. The chain to the browser DOM:
- `packages/client/web/src/boot.ts:88–91`: `ctx.inject(['uiRenderer'], (scope) =&gt; { scope.effect(() =&gt; scope.uiRenderer.mount(this.container), 'web boot: application mount') })`
- `packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/index.ts:41` — `export const inject = ['slots', 'sessions']`; `:79` — `ctx.slots.install(createSlotRenderer())`; `:80` — `provide('uiRenderer', { mount … })`
- `packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/app.tsx:37` — `{ctx.slots.renderSlot('root', {})}`
- `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:252–260` — three fail-loud guards: non-`'root'` key, renderer not installed, `'root'` has no registration.

**The register call** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts:116–143`:
```ts
export function apply(ctx: ClientContext): void {
  const layout = new LayoutController()
  ctx.effect(() =&gt; {
    const disposeService = ctx.reflect.provide('layout', layout)
    const disposeRegistration = ctx.slots.register({
      name: 'root',
      children: {
        'sidebar': { kind: 'single', scope: 'root' },
        'conversation': { kind: 'single', scope: 'session-maybe' },
        'details': { kind: 'single', scope: 'session' },
        'shell.overlay': { kind: 'list', scope: 'root' },
      },
      store: createLayoutStore,
      inject: (actions: PanelActions) =&gt; {
        layout.attachPanels(actions)
        return {}
      },
    }, AppFrame)
    …
  }, 'ui-layout: service + root registration')
  // second effect: 'ui-layout: theme presenter' (lines 147–155)
}
```
`export const inject = ['slots', 'theme']` (line 108). Context merge at lines 26–31 adds `layout: import('./service.ts').ILayout`. Value exports (lines 23–24): `LayoutController` and `type { ILayout }`; plus the four owner-share interfaces `SidebarOwnerProps` (94), `ConvOwnerProps` (102), `DetailsOwnerProps` (104).

**Region structure** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/AppFrame.tsx`:
- `:21–24` — `AppFrameProps = PropsRuntime&lt;'root'&gt; &amp; PropsRenderSlots&lt;'sidebar' | 'conversation' | 'details' | 'shell.overlay'&gt; &amp; PropsStore&lt;ReturnType&lt;typeof createLayoutStore&gt;&gt;`
- `:164–172` — one grid div, `gridTemplateColumns: \`${cols.sidebar}px minmax(0, 1fr) ${cols.details}px\``, with `data-sidebar-collapsed`, `data-details-collapsed`, `data-dragging`
- `:173–183` — `&lt;div className={css.sidebarCol}&gt;{renderSlot('sidebar', { collapsed: sidebarCollapsed, width: cols.sidebar })}&lt;/div&gt;`
- `:190` — `&lt;CenterColumn&gt;{renderSlot('conversation', {})}&lt;/CenterColumn&gt;`
- `:191` — `&lt;DetailsColumn&gt;{renderSlot('details', {})}&lt;/DetailsColumn&gt;`
- `:193–195` — `&lt;div className={css.overlayLayer} data-shell-overlay&gt;{renderSlot('shell.overlay', {})}&lt;/div&gt;`
- `:197–198` — two `DragHandle`s (`side="sidebar"` / `side="details"`)
- `:94–97` — reads `useSessions(s =&gt; …s.current…)` to derive `detailsSession`; `:136–142` narrow/collapse derivation; `computeColumns` from `columns.ts`.

**Slots declared**: the four above. **Slots consumed/rendered**: exactly those four (nothing else — `root` is its own registration target).

**Config**: none. No `Config` export exists in `packages/client/ui-layout/src` (grep for `export const Config` / `export interface Config` returns nothing). No `cordis.patch.yml` config block for the `ui-layout` row.

**Store**: `createLayoutStore()` (`src/client/stores.ts:48–72`), exclusive factory passed at register; state `{ sidebar, details, narrow, narrowExpanded }`; actions `setSidebar/setDetails/toggleSidebar/setNarrow/openDetails/closeDetails`. Not persisted.

**Service**: `LayoutController implements ILayout` (`src/client/service.ts:33`), face = `toggleSidebar` / `openDetails` / `closeDetails`; `attachPanels(actions)` is called from the register `inject` hook; `#require()` throws `'layout: panel actions not wired (root entry not mounted)'`.

**Tests** — 6 spec files; the apply spec asserts `expect(register).toHaveBeenCalledWith('@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout', expect.any(Function))` (`tests/apply.client.spec.ts:120`) and `expect(slots.spec('sidebar')).toEqual({ kind: 'single', scope: 'root' })` (`:51`) / `toBeUndefined()` after teardown (`:102`). `tests/app-frame.client.spec.tsx` imports internals through the `./src/*` subpath (`:16–19`).

## 5. RENAME MECHANICS — everything a client package rename touches

**a. TypeScript path mappings — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.base.json`.** Client packages are *not* covered by one wildcard; there are three wildcards plus one explicit row per package:
- `:158` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*/invariant": ["./packages/client/*/src/invariant.ts"]`
- `:161` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*/client": ["./packages/client/*/src/client"]`
- explicit rows `:183–233`, including `:204` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout": ["./packages/client/ui-layout/src"]` and `:205` `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar": ["./packages/client/ui-sidebar/src"]`
- the catch-all `"@deepseek-ai/dsh-*"` list at `:241–291` ends with `"./packages/client/*/src"` (`:290`), so a client package resolves through it too — but the explicit row is what the file's own comment at `:162–167` says is required for the split-face and non-trivial cases. A **new** package under `packages/client/` needs no wildcard edit; a **rename** must update the explicit row (`:204`/`:205`) or resolution silently falls back to the group wildcard.

**b. `tsconfig.client.json` references** — one entry per client package, `:52–99`; ui-layout at `:65`, ui-sidebar at `:66`. Split-face packages reference `tsconfig.client.json` inside the package (`connection`, `api/gateway`, `api/remotes`). Gates: `scripts/project-reference-faces.ts` (invoked from `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts`, `pnpm run constraints`) and `scripts/client-tsconfig.spec.ts` (asserts the aggregate loads exactly the `packages/{client,extensions}/*/src/css-modules.d.ts` set).

**c. Bundle cordis rows** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml`. Rows carry BOTH a short `id:` and a full `name:`:
```yaml
    - id: ui-layout
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout'      # lines 188–189
    - id: ui-sidebar
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar'     # lines 194–195
```
plus `packages/bundle/web-app/package.json:67,77`. Gate: `pnpm run verify-cordis-config` (`scripts/verify-cordis-config.ts`) — per root AGENTS.md line 102, *"Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`."* The boot roster/order visible in `apps/web/tests/built-boot.snapshot.ts` and `packages/client/web/tests/boot-page.client.spec.ts:38,41` uses the full names.

**d. ## How the stream loop was split — the one significant design decision

It was **not** split. `ConnectionHandle.start` is documented one-shot ("a second call throws"), and whichever domain started it would trigger `onConnected` — and therefore each domain's baseline pull — before a later-mounting domain could receive it. Having a domain re-broadcast the stream inverts the dependency; having each domain inject the other deadlocks.

So **runtime keeps the single loop** and reaches the domains the same way `slots.ts` already reaches them — by service name, through structural faces (`contract/stream-pumps.ts`: `SessionsStreamPump`, `WorkspacesStreamPump`, which `SessionRuntime`/`WorkspaceRuntime` satisfy structurally). `apply()` gates the start on `ctx.inject(['sessions','workspaces'], …)` and resolves each pump per frame:

- ordering preserved exactly: `sessions.handleHostEnvelope` → `workspaces.handleHostEnvelope` → `remote.$dispatch`; `sessions.handleConnected` → `workspaces.handleConnected` → `ctx.emit('connection/reset')`
- `connection/reset` and `slots/changed` declarations stay in runtime (runtime owns the emit)
- late-bound pumps keep the loop alive across a domain reload; `loop ??=` keeps `connection.start` one-shot. Documented in runtime's README Known Limitations.

`ctx.typert.contexts.registerClient('agent', …)` moved to session-runtime; `workspaces.startInitialSelection()` moved to workspace-runtime, which injects `'sessions'` and narrows it to `SessionsPort`.

## Deviations from the spec, with reasons

1. **`chat` is `scope: 'root'`, not `'session-maybe'`.** Session-maybe would have (a) made the layout store *per-session* (`SlotRegistry.resolveStore` keys non-root scopes by session id), (b) dropped `useStore`/`actions` from ChatSurface's props entirely on the no-session page (`standardKit` returns `store: undefined` when `sessionId === undefined`) — an immediate crash, and (c) remounted the whole frame on every session switch. `root` reproduces today's `root`-scope AppFrame exactly, and a root parent may declare session/session-maybe children (that is precisely what `root` does today).
2. **`ctx.layout` is now provided *inside* the `chat` injection, after the `register()` call.** This is a real bug I hit and fixed: ui-chat-sidebar and ui-conversation both bare-`register` into the columns and both list `layout` in their cordis `inject`. Previously ui-layout provided `layout` and declared the columns in one synchronous effect, so waiting on the service implied the seats existed. With the deferred `chat` injection, publishing `layout` at apply time let ui-chat-sidebar resume first — the first full web run was **67/84 files failed** with `slot "chat.sidebar" is not declared`. Publishing the service only after the register call restores the original ordering contract through the existing service edge, without restructuring ui-conversation's 470-line apply. The ordering is documented at the apply and in both READMEs.
3. **CSS module file renamed** to `ChatSurface.module.css` (spec said "moves as-is"); the load-bearing part — the exported class names — is preserved, and lightningcss's `[hash]_[local]` pattern keeps `[class*="frame"]`/`[class*="centerCol"]` matching.

## 2. `packages/client/ui-chat-surface`

### How it occupies `chat` — and the ordering contract
`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/index.ts:119-146`

```ts
export function apply(ctx: ClientContext): void {
  const layout = new LayoutController()
  ctx.slots.inject('chat', () =&gt; {
    const disposeRegistration = ctx.slots.register({
      name: 'chat',
      children: {
        'chat.sidebar':      { kind: 'single', scope: 'root' },
        'chat.conversation': { kind: 'single', scope: 'session-maybe' },
        'chat.details':      { kind: 'single', scope: 'session' },
      },
      store: createLayoutStore,             // exclusive factory, not a handle
      inject: (actions: PanelActions) =&gt; { layout.attachPanels(actions); return {} },
    }, ChatSurface)
    const disposeService = ctx.reflect.provide('layout', layout)
    return () =&gt; { void disposeService(); disposeRegistration() }
  })
}
```

The **ordering contract** is spelled out at `:111-117`: `ctx.reflect.provide('layout', …)` must come *after* the `register()` call, because registrants of the columns declare `layout` in their cordis injections; publishing the service earlier would let a registrant's fiber resume and reach an undeclared slot, failing at load. Test coverage: `tests/apply.client.spec.ts:53-66` ("publishes ctx.layout only with the columns, and retracts both with the shell declaration") — with no `chat` declaration, `ctx.get('layout')` is `undefined`; declaring `chat` publishes it synchronously; disposing the shell declaration retracts both.

### How client packages declare `dsh.client` + host apply (the general pattern)
1. **Two halves in one package.** `exports["."]` → `lib/index.js` (host plane, loaded by the host Cordis Loader; for browser-only UI plugins it is an intentional no-op `apply`). `exports["./client"]` → `lib/client.js` (browser bundle).
2. **`package.json` `dsh.client`** (`ui-chat-surface/package.json:32-40`): `{ inject: [&lt;package names&gt;], platform: "web" }`; optional `external: string[]` for extra module-table specifiers. Field semantics at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/modules/src/client/manifest.ts:45-63` — `immediately` marks stage-one prefetch, `inject` is informational graph metadata, `external` carries real module-graph edges.
3. **Gate:** `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/scripts/verify-cordis-config.ts:104-117` — a `packages/client/*` package that exports `./client` without `dsh.client` (or vice versa) is a hard error; "its bundle is never served and no error is raised anywhere". The browser roster is discovered by *scanning composed packages for a `dsh.client` block* (`:90-102`).
4. **Bundle:** `tsdown.config.ts` calls `clientBundle(id, libEntry)` from `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/tsdown.client.ts:106-123`; the client half is emitted as a `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` closure (`:562-564`) with a **bundle purity gate** (`:486-497`) rejecting any cross-plugin `@deepseek-ai/*` *value* import not in the baseline/`dsh.client.external`/inline-safe wire layers.
5. **Boot:** `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/web/src/boot.ts:113-135` creates every manifest row through the Cordis Loader, then `assertEntriesActive` (`:138-158`) fails boot on any non-active entry. Mount at `:89-94` through `ctx.inject(['uiRenderer'], …)`.

## 3. Slot system: keyed slots, owner data, metadata, `inject` vs bare `register`

### Where `SlotMap` lives and how it merges
Declared **empty** at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-slots/src/index.ts:24` (`export interface SlotMap {}`), deliberately in the entry module — the file comment at `:6-9` notes that consumer `declare module` augmentation merges only with declarations *lexically in* the augmented module, not with re-exports. The runtime merges `'root'` at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:26-43`; each UI package merges its own keys.

### A `SlotMap` entry: the full type chain
`ui-slots/src/index.ts:100-122`
```ts
export interface SlotEntryDef {
  kind: SlotKind                             // 'single' | 'list' | 'keyed' | 'chain'   (:88)
  scope: SlotScope                           // 'root' | 'session-maybe' | 'session'    (:91)
  owner?: object                             // owner share at the parent's renderSlot site
  keyProps?: Record&lt;string, object&gt;          // per-KEY prop table (keyed slots only)
  hookContext?: unknown                      // opaque per-renderSlot-occurrence context
  inject?: object                            // slot-level face supplied by the DECLARER
}
```

Derived types: `SlotSpec&lt;E&gt;` (`:130-137`, the runtime dispatch literal validated against the map entry), `ChildrenDecl` (`:145`), `OwnerOf` (`:148`), `EntryKeyOf` (`:152`), `KeyPropsOf` (`:158`), `HookContextOf` (`:168`), `SlotInjectOf` (`:172`), `PropsRuntime` (`:211-221`), `PropsRenderSlots` (`:336-363`), `ComposedProps` (`:442-450`).

`PropsRuntime&lt;K, EntryKey&gt;` = `OwnerOf&lt;K&gt; &amp; KeyPropsOf&lt;K,EntryKey&gt; &amp; SlotInjectFace&lt;SlotInjectOf&lt;K&gt;&gt; &amp; (session kit by scope) &amp; GlobalStandardProps`.

### Does anything pass per-instance owner data today? Yes — three live patterns

**(a) Keyed slot with per-instance owner data + hookContext — `chat.conversation.chat.node`.** This is the closest existing precedent to `desktop.window.surface`.

Declaration: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts:116-123`
```ts
'chat.conversation.chat.node': {
  kind: 'keyed'
  scope: 'session'
  owner: ChatNodeOwnerProps
  keyProps: { [Kind in ChatNodeKind]: { node: ChatNode&lt;Kind&gt; } }
  hookContext: string
  inject: ChatNodeTurnDataInjected
}
```

Runtime declaration in the parent's `children` table, carrying a slot-level inject face: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts:386`
```ts
'chat.conversation.chat.node': { kind: 'keyed', scope: 'session', inject: CHAT_NODE_INJECT },
```
`CHAT_NODE_INJECT` (`apply.ts:77-88`) is `{ hooks: { turnData: (standard, hookContext) =&gt; useTurnData } }` — a `SlotHookFactory` whose second parameter is the per-occurrence `hookContext` (the node key).

N-instance render loop: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/chat/ChatView.tsx:432-447` maps `order` → one `&lt;ChatNodeSeat key={nodeKey} …/&gt;` each; each seat dispatches at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/chat/ChatNodeSeat.tsx:50-60`:
```ts
renderSlot('chat.conversation.chat.node', routedOwner, {
  entryKey: routedNode.kind,
  hookContext: nodeKey,
  fallback: &lt;JsonBlock … /&gt;,
})
```
So: **N `renderSlot` occurrences of the same key, each with distinct owner data (`routedOwner` including the `node`), a per-instance `hookContext`, and a per-instance `entryKey`.** Registrants are per-key components with no knowledge of instance count (`chat/register-node-renderers.ts:16-51`).

**(b) Keyed slot dispatched over a data list — `settings.plugin.item`.** `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-settings-plugins/src/client/ConfigurablePluginsTab.tsx:35-39` maps namespaces → `renderSlot('settings.plugin.item', {}, { entryKey: ns })` inside a `&lt;Fragment key={ns}&gt;`. Owner share is `{}`; the data is only the key. Declared at `src/client/index.ts:143`, registered at `:146-160` via `ctx.slots.inject('settings.plugin.item', function* () { … })` (generator form).

**(c) List slot with `only` filtering — `chat.conversation.view`** (`contract/slots.ts:114`), rendered one-at-a-time by the session body via `only: &lt;active id&gt;`.

`settings.general.item` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-settings/src/client/contract/slots.ts:88`) is a **`list`/`root`** slot with `SettingsGeneralItemOwnerProps`, occupied by `ui-theme` (`ui-theme/src/client/index.ts:408-409`) and `locale` (`locale/src/client/index.ts:426-427`); each registers with `{ name, id, order?, store, locale }` under `ctx.slots.inject`.

### Can `slots.register` carry arbitrary metadata today? **No.**

`BaseOptions` is a closed set (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:526-550`): `name`, `children?`, `store?`, `locale?`, `registrant?` — intersected with `KindOptions` (`:483-509`):

| kind | option shape |
|---|---|
| `keyed` | `{ key: EntryKey; priority?: number }` |
| `list` | `{ id: string; order?: number; label?: SlotLabel; priority?: number }` |
| `chain` | `{ select: ChainSelect&lt;Owner,M&gt;; priority?: number }` |
| `single` | `{ priority?: number }` |

Plus the inject-bearing overload's `inject: (...args: InjectParams&lt;K,H&gt;) =&gt; I` (`:768-785`).

What is actually **persisted** onto a `StoredEntry` is narrower still — `StoredEntry.options` is typed `{ key?, id?, order?, label?, priority? }` (`:557-559`) and the write at `:845-860` copies exactly those five plus `select`, `inject`, `children`, `store`, `locale`, `registrant`. `ErasedOptions` (`:591-608`) mirrors that. **There is no `meta`/`metadata` field anywhere in `ui-slots/src/index.ts`.** The nearest existing "carry data with a registration" affordances are:
- `SlotLabel = string | (() =&gt; string)` (`:474`) with `resolveSlotLabel` (`:581-583`) — a locale-following thunk for list entries, the only display metadata today.
- The *declarer*-supplied `SlotSpec.inject` face (`:120-121`, `:133-137`), which is common to every entry of the slot, not per-registrant.
- `keyProps` (`:109`), which types per-key *props*, not registration metadata.

The inspection surface that would expose any such metadata is `LiveSlotOccupant` (`:631-644`: `registrant?`, `key?`, `id?`, `order?`, `priority`, `active`) via `SlotCore.snapshot()` (`:979-1019`), re-exported as `SlotRegistry.snapshot()` (`runtime/src/client/slots.ts:309-311`).

### `ctx.slots.inject(key, cb)` vs bare `ctx.slots.register`
`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:144-206`. `inject` installs an effect **per declaration lifetime** of a slot key: it runs the callback synchronously if the key is already declared, otherwise inside the declaring `register()` call after the declaration commits; a collapse disposes the effect and a later re-declaration re-runs it. Keyed on `declarationEpoch` (`:167-180`), driven by `SlotCore.subscribeDeclaration` (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:1054-1058`, synchronous notifications). Callback may return a disposer or a generator of disposers (transactional setup, reverse teardown). Setup failures **retire the injection permanently** (`:152-162`). The controller rides the caller's fiber.

Bare `register` (`slots.ts:468-475`) routes through `this.ctx.effect(...)` on the **caller's** context — the prototype-method requirement is documented at `:120-127` (an instance arrow would freeze `this` to the service root and break per-plugin disposal). Registering into an undeclared slot **throws** (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:789-791`).

Current usage: 131 `slots.inject(` call sites in non-test source. `ui-desktop` uses bare register (target is built-in `root`); `ui-chat-sidebar/src/client/index.ts:41` and parts of `ui-conversation` still bare-register into slots they do not declare, ordered only by the `layout` service edge — recorded as a follow-up in the Phase 1 note (`2026-08-27-desktop-shell-owns-the-root.md:39`).

### Shadowing / cell semantics (relevant to "a Window entry vs. a fallback")
`SlotCore.register` JSDoc `:706-737` and the switch at `:799-824`: entries sharing a cell (single = the slot; keyed = same `key`; list = same `id`) coexist only at **distinct** priorities; ascending, **lowest renders**; a second registration at an occupied cell's exact priority throws naming the occupant. `entriesOfSlot` (`:936-952`) projects to the winning entry per cell, skipping abdicated entries.

## 4. GlobalStandardProps / store engine / scope keying

### `GlobalStandardProps`
Declared **empty** at `ui-slots/src/index.ts:198` (zero-dependency layer). Merged by exactly two packages:
- `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/index.ts:122-124` → `useSessions: SnapshotSelectorHook&lt;SessionListState&gt;`
- `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/workspace-runtime/src/client/index.ts:20-22` → `useWorkspaces: SnapshotSelectorHook&lt;WorkspaceListState&gt;`

Session kits merge at `session-runtime/src/client/index.ts:106-121` (`SessionStandardProps`: `useSession`, `sessionId`, `useProjection`; `SessionMaybeStandardProps`: maybe-variants).

Bound at render time in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/scoped-slots.tsx:344-381` (`standardProps`): a per-host cache whose `root` entry is `{ useSessions: observableHook(host.sessions.list), useWorkspaces: observableHook(host.workspaces.list) }`; session scopes extend it per provide-bundle identity with every `info.hooks` source bound to `use&lt;Name&gt;`, `info.props` spread verbatim, `sessionId`, and `useProjection`. Every hook is bound from a **bare host observable**, cached per source (`session-provider.tsx:58-66`), so re-spreading a fresh kit object never churns subscriptions.

### Store engine
`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/store.ts` — zustand vanilla + `subscribeWithSelector` + immer `produce` + optional rAF batching + hand-rolled localStorage persistence (`:127-147`, deliberately not the zustand persist middleware). `defineStore(decl)` (`:207-240`) returns an `EngineStoreHandle`; `create(scopeKey?)` builds the snapshot store, bakes the draft parameter off every action, and computes `persistKey = scopeKey === undefined ? decl.persist : \`${decl.persist}.${scopeKey}\``.

Contracts live in `ui-slots/src/store.ts`: `StoreSpec` (`:44-48`), `StoreInstance` (`:58-73`), `StoreHandle` (`:82-92`), `StoreFactory`/`StoreDecl` (`:102-106`), `PropsStore&lt;H&gt;` (`:123-125` → `{ useStore, actions }`), `BoundActions` (`:116`).

### How `ui-desktop` / `ui-chat-surface` get store props
- **`ui-desktop`: it does not.** No `store` in its register call, so its composed props carry no `useStore`/`actions`.
- **`ui-chat-surface`:** declares `store: createLayoutStore` — the **exclusive factory** form. `SlotRegistry._register` mints it into a per-entry handle at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:361`. `standardKit` in `scoped-slots.tsx:417-425` resolves the instance and puts `useStore = observableHook(store)` and `actions = store.actions` on the props. The same baked actions are passed to the registration's `inject` factory (`scoped-slots.tsx:102-111`), which is how `LayoutController.attachPanels` gets them.

### Scope keying — "store resolution keys non-root scopes by session"
`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:427-440`:
```ts
private resolveStore(handle, sessionId) {
  const record = this._stores.get(handle)
  if (record === undefined) throw new Error('store handle is not registered (…)')
  const key = record.scope === 'root' ? ROOT_INSTANCE_KEY : sessionId
  if (key === undefined) throw new Error(`${record.scope} store resolution requires a session id`)
  let instance = record.instances.get(key)
  if (instance === undefined) {
    instance = record.scope === 'root' ? handle.create() : handle.create(key)
    record.instances.set(key, instance)
  }
  return instance
}
```
`ROOT_INSTANCE_KEY = 'root'` at `:50`. `StoreAxisRecord` (`:59-66`) = `{ scope, refs, instances: Map&lt;string, EngineStoreInstance&gt; }`; `_acquire`/`_release` at `:443-461` drop the record with the last holding entry. Cross-scope mounting of one shared handle throws in the core (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:833-843`). Session-scope teardown: `pruneStoreScope(sessionId)` (`slots.ts:273-280`) materializes the instance if needed just to `clearPersisted()`, then deletes it; called from `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:764`.

Render-side pass-through: `scoped-slots.tsx:417-419` — `scope === 'session-maybe' &amp;&amp; info?.sessionId === undefined` yields **no store at all**; otherwise `host.storeOf(entry, info?.sessionId)`.

This is exactly the mechanism the Phase 1 note cites (`2026-08-27-desktop-shell-owns-the-root.md:27`) for keeping `chat` root-scoped: a non-root `chat` would fragment the layout store per session, strip store props on the no-session page, and remount the frame per switch.

## 5. Recovery / error-tile machinery for a failed client renderer

**A per-entry error boundary exists; the "tile" it renders is an empty marker div, not a recovery UI.**

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/scoped-slots.tsx:317-333`
```ts
class SlotErrorBoundary extends Component&lt;
  { slotKey: string; onEntryError: (error: unknown) =&gt; void; children: ReactNode }, { failed: boolean }
&gt; {
  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: unknown) {
    if (error instanceof SlotAssemblyError) throw error   // miswiring stays fail-loud
    return { failed: true }
  }
  componentDidCatch(error) { console.error(`slot entry crashed in '${this.props.slotKey}':`, error); this.props.onEntryError(error) }
  render() { if (this.state.failed) return &lt;div data-slot-error={this.props.slotKey} /&gt;; return this.props.children }
}
```

Mechanics:
- **Placement.** The boundary wraps the *entry element*, not its interior, so inject-factory and kit-synthesis failures land in the per-entry fallback rather than escaping upward (`:704-706`). Applied per kind at `:707-755` (`guarded`); strict-session entries get an inner boundary keyed by `sessionId` at `:632`.
- **Boundary remount key.** `entryKeyOf(entry)` (`:295-305`) keys boundaries by entry identity so a boundary that failed on entry A cannot black out a healthy entry B after re-election / shadowing fallback / HMR re-registration.
- **Abdication.** `onEntryError` (`:714-716`) reports with `abdicate: spec.kind !== 'chain'`. `SlotCore.reportEntryError` (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:1098-1106`) adds the entry to an `abdicated` WeakSet (one-shot), bumps the record version, and notifies `onEntryError` listeners. The registration itself **stays on the ledger** — raw `entries()` still lists it and its disposer still works.
- **Dry-cell face.** `deadCell()` at `scoped-slots.tsx:759` — `&lt;div data-slot-error={slotKey} /&gt;`. Used when a cell has registrations but every one abdicated: `single` (`:762-763`), `keyed` (`:767-771`), `list` dry rows (`:837`, `:848`). An **unoccupied** cell instead renders `opts?.fallback ?? null`, so "never registered" and "registered but all crashed" are distinguishable.

- **Supervision seam.** `SlotCore.onEntryError` (`ui-slots/src/index.ts:1118-1121`) → `SlotRegistry.onEntryError` (`runtime/src/client/slots.ts:324-326`) — synchronous, fires for abdicating *and* non-abdicating crashes, carries `(key, entry, error, { abdicated })`. One live consumer: `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/tests/runner.spec.ts:528-532` mirrors `{ slot, message, abdicated }` — i.e. the dynamic-plugin runner already surfaces contribution health through this channel.
- **Anchor.** Every outlet renders a stable `&lt;div data-slot="&lt;key&gt;" style={{display:'contents'}}&gt;` wrapper (`:654-680`, `ANCHOR_STYLE` at `:652`); fallback, crash face, and undeclared-empty all render *inside* it, so the anchor never flickers with registration churn.

Tests: `packages/client/ui-renderer/tests/scoped-slots.client.spec.tsx:343, 407, 413, 945`.

There is **no** existing UI that identifies a plugin/package, offers retry/rollback/close, or persists across a failed render — the recovery tile described at `2026-08-26-…-restructuring.md:164` does not exist today. 0  contract/            shared contract API (types + slot declarations)

Concretely it forbids: (a) a file in domain X importing a sibling domain Y (`domain "X" imports sibling domain "Y" (route shared API through contract/)`), and (b) a top-level non-assembly file importing into any domain (`only apply/index may assemble`). `CONTRACT_DIRS = new Set(['contract'])` (`:24`); `ASSEMBLY_FILES = new Set(['apply.ts','index.ts','index.tsx'])` (`:26`). ## 1. `ctx.storageDomain` — the Service Definition

### Ownership and layering

Three packages, split as a capability seam (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/storage.md:5`):

| Package | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage` | `packages/storage/storage` | Hub `ctx.storage` — backend registry + form mount table, **no IO** |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain` | `packages/storage/storage-domain` | The domain data form — `ctx.storageDomain`, also `ctx.storage.domain` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json` / `-sqlite` | `packages/storage/storage-json`, `packages/storage/storage-sqlite` | The two `kv` backends |

`ctx.storageDomain` is declared at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:35-39`; the same object is merged onto the hub as form `domain` at `:29-33`.

### Domain registration and declaration

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/spec.ts`:

```ts
export interface DomainSpec {            // :35
  readonly name: string                  // must match UNIT_NAME_RE
  readonly version: number
  readonly global?: DomainGlobalSpec&lt;unknown&gt;
  readonly tables: Record&lt;string, DomainTableSpec&gt;
}
export function domainTable&lt;K extends string, V&gt;(schema: ZodType&lt;V&gt;): DomainTableSpec&lt;K, V&gt;   // :63
export function defineDomain&lt;S extends DomainSpec&gt;(spec: S): S                                // :79
export function descriptorOf(spec: DomainSpec): KvUnitDescriptor                              // :105
```

`defineDomain` fails loud at module load (`:80-96`): name/table names must match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/` (`packages/storage/storage/src/backend.ts:10`), version must be a non-negative integer, and a global schema that accepts `null` throws — `null` is the medium's "never written" sentinel. `DomainTableSpec.__key` (`:31`) is a phantom compile-time key carrier; keys are plain strings on the medium.

### Opening

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:100`:

```ts
async open&lt;S extends DomainSpec&gt;(spec: S): Promise&lt;Domain&lt;S&gt;&gt;
```

Ordered failure sequence (`:101-155`): `already-open` name reservation → route lookup (`config.routes[name] ?? config.backend`, `:106`) → `backend-not-found` from the hub → `facet-unsupported` when the backend has no `kv` → `kv.open(descriptorOf(spec))` (backend `version-mismatch` / `malformed-medium` pass through) → `loadAll()` + zod-validate every record and the global (`invalid-record` carrying `{ table, key }`, `:181-192`). The caller owns the returned handle and closes it (`:93-96`); `closeAll()` (`:175`) is the unmount path; `get(name)` (`:165`) is the untyped diagnostic lookup the invariant uses.

### Tables and global

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/domain.ts`:

```ts
export interface KvTable&lt;K extends string, V&gt; {                        // :42
  get(key: K): V | undefined                                           // :48
  entries(): IterableIterator&lt;[K, V]&gt;                                  // :55
  keys(): IterableIterator&lt;K&gt;                                          // :61
  readonly size: number                                                // :64
  put(key: K, value: V): Promise&lt;void&gt;                                 // :72
  delete(key: K): Promise&lt;boolean&gt;                                     // :80
  update(key: K, fn: (current: V) =&gt; V): Promise&lt;V&gt;                    // :89
}
export interface DomainGlobal&lt;G&gt; { get(): G; set(value: G): Promise&lt;void&gt; }   // :19,:25,:34
export interface Domain&lt;S extends DomainSpec&gt; {                        // :97
  readonly name: string
  readonly global: DomainGlobalHandleOf&lt;S&gt;
  table&lt;N extends keyof S['tables'] &amp; string&gt;(name: N): KvTable&lt;TableKeyOf&lt;S, N&gt;, TableValueOf&lt;S, N&gt;&gt;  // :108
  close(): Promise&lt;void&gt;                                               // :118
}
```

Reads are synchronous from authoritative memory; `entries()`/`keys()` are snapshots (`:294`, `:299`). Returned records are the stored objects, **not copies** (`:38-41`) — replace via `put`/`update`.

### Transaction semantics — there is no transaction

- **Per-domain write chain, not per-record.** One `chain: Promise&lt;void&gt;` per `DomainImpl` (`domain.ts:149`), `enqueue` at `:263-270`. Every write of every table and the global serializes on that single chain.
- **Atomicity granularity is one record.** `KvUnit` guarantees each single call is atomic on the medium and durable once resolved, and explicitly does **not** serialize concurrent writes — ordering is the caller's job (`packages/storage/storage/src/backend.ts:57-65`).
- **No cross-table atomicity.** SQLite: "Each primitive is a single statement, so atomicity comes from SQLite itself — no explicit transactions, and no write queue" (`packages/storage/storage-sqlite/src/unit.ts:1-8`). JSON: whole-file atomic rewrite per call, with in-memory rollback on a failed publish (`packages/storage/storage-json/src/unit.ts:69-107`, `:133-140`).
- Documented gap: `packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md:35` — "**No cross-table transactions, secondary indexes, or multi-segment keys**". The deferred `domain.transact(fn)` idea is tabled in `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md:298`.
- `update(key, fn)` **is** the atomic read-modify-write: `fn` sees the value current at its chain slot (`domain.ts:332-346`), missing key → `missing-key`.

### Commit-before-publish is already the domain-layer rule

`domain.ts:1-8` (module doc) and `KvTableImpl.put` (`:307-313`): `await unit.putRecord(...)` → mutate memory → `emitChanged(...)`. A rejected backend write leaves memory untouched. `emitChanged` contains synchronous listener throws with a warn (`:251-261`) because the commit point has already passed. `delete` decides existence at its chain slot, not at call time (`:317-319`).

### Versioning / migration hooks — none

`DomainSpec.version` is stamped on the medium at first materialization. A mismatch throws `version-mismatch` at open with **no migration and no rebuild** (`packages/storage/storage-sqlite/src/index.ts:100-110`; note `2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md:47,161`). Existing precedent for version bumps: `workspace` is at v2 and `session_projcache` at v3 (cache semantics: a bump discards the medium, `packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts:61-70`).

### Errors

`DomainErrorCode = 'already-open' | 'facet-unsupported' | 'invalid-record' | 'missing-key' | 'closed'` (`packages/storage/storage-domain/src/error.ts:7-12`), with `InvalidRecordDetail { table, key }` (`:15-20`). Backend failures pass through as `StorageError` un-rewrapped (`:28-33`); `StorageErrorCode` at `packages/storage/storage/src/error.ts:7-14`.

### Config / routing

`packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:52-62`: `backend` (required, no default — no universally correct medium) + `routes` (domain name → backend name). `apply` (`:200-220`) injects `storageBackendServiceKey(name)` for every routed backend so activation cannot race registration, then mounts the form and `provide('storageDomain', facility)`.

### Backend contract surface

`packages/storage/storage/src/backend.ts`: `StorageBackend { kv?: KvFacet; close(): Promise&lt;void&gt; }` (`:17-27`); `KvFacet.open(descriptor: KvUnitDescriptor): Promise&lt;KvUnit&gt;` (`:42`); `KvUnitDescriptor { name, version, tables, hasGlobal }` (`:46-55`); `KvUnit.loadAll / putRecord / deleteRecord / setGlobal / close` (`:72, :81, :89, :97, :103`).
