## 2. `packages/automation/automation-domain/src/index.ts` — the newest exemplar

### Domain declaration ('automation' v0)

`packages/automation/automation-domain/src/spec.ts:40-51`:

```ts
export const automationDomainSpec = defineDomain({
  name: 'automation',
  version: 0,
  global: { schema: automationDispatchState, initial: { dispatchEnabled: true } },
  tables: {
    rules: domainTable&lt;AutomationRuleId, AutomationDurableRule&gt;(automationDurableRule),
    runs: domainTable&lt;AutomationRunId, AutomationRunRecord&gt;(automationRunRecord),
  },
})
```

The durable rule projection is derived from the service record by omission (`:20`): `automationRuleRecord.omit({ contributed: true })` — the lifecycle-owned field is never persisted. Global schema is a separate small zod object (`:30`).

### Service-class shape (this is the Config pattern)

`packages/automation/automation-domain/src/index.ts:181-235`:

```ts
export class DomainAutomationRegistry extends AutomationRegistry {
  static inject = ['storageDomain', 'agents']            // :182
  static Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({                  // :184-188  (schemastery, NOT zod)
    maxCausalDepth: z.number().step(1).min(1).default(3),
    maxExcerptBytes: z.number().step(1).min(1).default(2048),
    maxDeliveredRuns: z.number().step(1).min(1).default(500),
  })
```

Note the deliberate two-schema split (`packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts:5-6`, `spec.ts:5-7`): **plugin `Config` is schemastery; durable record schemas inside domain specs are zod** (so `z.infer` keeps types un-duplicated and the same schemas later project to RPC wire schemas). `Config` is a documented `interface` + a matching schema constant; bounds are read once in the constructor via `config as Required&lt;Config&gt;` (`:231`).

The service default-exports its class and nothing plugin-shaped (`:968`), per `packages/AGENTS.md`.

### Lifetime

`protected async [Service.init]()` at `:238-259`: open domain → capture `ruleTable`/`runTable` → register a **memoized** teardown effect (`:243`) → read the global kill switch → rehydrate rules and the causal map from `runTable.entries()` → subscribe. Teardown order (`disposeAll`, `:957-965`): stop dispatching → dispose owned Agent handles → withdraw subscriptions → `domain.close()`, "an Agent settling during teardown must still find an open domain".

### Durable write vs event publish ordering

This is the reference implementation of publish-at-commit. `commitRun` (`:727-742`):

```ts
private async commitRun(record: AutomationRunRecord): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {
  if (this.stopping) return false
  try { await this.runTable.put(record.id, record) }
  catch (error) { /* warn */ return false }
  try { this.publish(record) }
  finally { await this.prune(record.id) }   // retention is owed to the write, never to the publication
  return true
}
```

`publish` (`:751-766`) skips a rule withdrawn between match and write, then emits inside try/catch — a throwing listener must not reach run accounting, the reservation, or the message a started Agent already holds. The stronger ordering claim is in `dispatchStart` (`:818-822, :887-898`): the message reaches the Agent **before** the record is written, so a listener of the publication can never find a started Agent with nothing to work on. Later lifecycle transitions update the record **without** publishing again (`updateRun`, `:474-484`) — one event per match, not one per state change.

Class-level doc block `:157-180` states the three properties (Lifetime / Publication / Containment) explicitly.

### Where revisions are bumped

`create` writes `revision: 0` (`:292`); `setEnabled` bumps inside the chain slot via `ruleTable.update` (`:310-314`):

```ts
const durable = await this.ruleTable.update(id, stored =&gt; ({ ...stored, enabled, revision: stored.revision + 1 }))
```

`ruleRevision` is pinned onto each run record at match time (`:707`).

### Retention

`prune` (`:774-788`) is amortized: it runs only when `size &gt; maxDeliveredRuns + PRUNE_BATCH` (`PRUNE_BATCH = 24`, `:48`), never deletes the just-published run or a run this process still watches, and re-measures the table each iteration so an overlapping pass stops at the same bound.

### Invariant: `packages/automation/automation/src/invariant.ts`

The publish-at-commit check lives in the **Service Definition** package, not the provider, so it holds for every provider (`:13-17`):

```ts
const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) =&gt; {
  ctx.on('automation/dispatched', (payload) =&gt; {
    if (ctx.automations.get(payload.ruleId) === undefined)
      fail(`automation/dispatched names rule ${ruleId}, which the registry does not hold`)
    const run = ctx.automations.listRuns({ ruleId: payload.ruleId }).find(r =&gt; r.id === payload.runId)
    if (run === undefined)
      fail(`automation run ${runId} is not readable through rule ${ruleId} when its dispatch is published`)
    if (run.outcome !== payload.outcome) fail(...)
    if (run.eventName !== payload.eventName) fail(...)
  })
}, { inject: ['automations'] })
```

(`packages/automation/automation/src/invariant.ts:18-37`.)

### `spec.ts` request/spec split

There is **no** separate request-vs-record split file in automation-domain. The split is: `packages/automation/automation/src/records.ts` owns brands + zod record schemas (input, record, run) shared by registry, provider, and tool; `packages/automation/automation-domain/src/spec.ts` owns only the durable projection + `defineDomain`. `automationRuleInput` (input, defaults filled on parse, `records.ts:165-174`) vs `automationRuleRecord` (input `.extend`ed with id/revision/enabled/owner/createdAt/contributed, `:185-192`) is the request/record split you're looking for.

Other consumers worth diffing against: `packages/workspace/workspace/src/spec.ts` (global with `pendingMutation` two-write recovery marker, `:32-56`), `packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts`, `packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/spec.ts`.

## 3. Idempotency keys, per-key serialized queues, monotonic revisions — what exists

### (a) Per-key serialized mutation queue + version CAS — `message-feedback` (closest match, and it is over `ctx.storageDomain`)

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/index.ts`:

```ts
private readonly operationTails = new Map&lt;SessionId, Promise&lt;void&gt;&gt;()    // :160
private mutationAdmissionOpen = true                                     // :161

/** Queue a complete read/compare/write mutation behind this Session's prior mutation. */
private enqueue&lt;T&gt;(sessionId: SessionId, operation: () =&gt; Promise&lt;T&gt;): Promise&lt;T&gt; {   // :361
  if (!this.mutationAdmissionOpen) return Promise.reject(new Error('message-feedback: service is disposing'))
  const previous = this.operationTails.get(sessionId) ?? Promise.resolve()
  const result = previous.then(operation)
  const tail = result.then(() =&gt; undefined, () =&gt; undefined)
  this.operationTails.set(sessionId, tail)
  return result.finally(() =&gt; {
    if (this.operationTails.get(sessionId) === tail) this.operationTails.delete(sessionId)
  })
}
```

Compare-and-set on an **opaque uuid version** rather than a counter: `nextVersion()` at `:132` (`randomUUID()`), `request.ifVersion !== (existing?.version ?? null)` → `version-conflict` carrying the authoritative current item (`:236-237`, `:353-359`). A matching no-op returns the stored item **without** minting a new version (`:240-243`) — that is the repo's existing idempotence idiom. Teardown drains all tails before closing the domain (`:173-181`).

### (b) Per-id serialized chain with abort + settled tails — `session-persistence`

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/session/session-persistence/src/coordinator.ts:1002-1033`. Same shape, plus: `signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the slot, a `started` flag so `observeQueuedAbort` can distinguish queued-abort from in-flight, exact-tail deletion, and the documented deadlock rule at `:1005-1009` — "serialized public methods must NOT call each other; they call the unserialized `*Core` helpers instead." Quiescence at dispose: `while (this.chains.size &gt; 0) await Promise.allSettled([...this.chains.values()])` (`:1096`).

### (c) Single global operation chain — `settings-file`

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/settings/settings-file/src/index.ts:121-126` (`operations: Promise&lt;void&gt;`) and `enqueue` at `:193-197`. One document backs every namespace, so writes and watcher reloads share one chain (`:185-189`).

### (d) The domain layer's own chain

`packages/storage/storage-domain/src/domain.ts:263-270`. Note this is **per domain**, not per record — a per-record queue for Desktop/Window would sit above it.

### (e) Monotonic revision + stale-ref rejection — `goal`

`packages/goal/goal/src/types.ts:18-24`:

```ts
export interface GoalRef { readonly id: GoalId; readonly revision: number }   // "Positive revision; every durable mutation increments it."
```

`expectCurrent` rejects stale refs with code `GOAL_STALE_REVISION` (`packages/goal/goal/src/index.ts:401-411`); every mutation builds `revision: current.revision + 1` (`:285`, `:453`); `clear` emits a tombstone at `current.revision + 1` (`:380`). Fold-side enforcement that a change advances by exactly one: `packages/goal/goal/src/fold.ts:192-196`. Goal state lives in the session log, not `storageDomain` — but the CAS vocabulary is the precedent.

### (f) Opaque backend revision token — `session-persistence`

`packages/session/session-persistence/src/revision.ts:9-18`: `SessionPersistenceRevision = Branded&lt;'SessionPersistenceRevision'&gt;`, backend-owned, identifies both storage source and log revision; `readStoredRevision(id, signal)` (`coordinator.ts:152`) is the poll. `2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md:293` names "the revision pattern (copy session-persistence)" as the deferred route for cross-process change observation, and `:328` records that `domain/changed` is the repo's first push-mode persistence event.

### (g) Client-chosen id deduplicated across concurrent retries — `apiproxy`

`packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:1068` `const sessionCreations = new Map&lt;SessionId, Promise&lt;Agent&gt;&gt;()` ("Client-chosen identity creation/resume, deduplicated across concurrent retries"), used at `:1565-1636`. Also `presetSwitches` (`:1064`), `workspaceCreationChain` (`:1070`), `serializeImageAdmission` (`:1076-1080`). The wire-level contract "a same-id same-cwd retry is idempotent; a different cwd reports `session-conflict`" is recorded at `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-25-web-client-session-scope-and-provide-channel.md:111`.

### (h) Sentinel-abort no-op write — `workspace`

`packages/workspace/workspace/src/entity.ts:190-220`: one private `mutate` funnels every write through `table.update`, and an unchanged result throws `unchangedSentinel` (`:66`, `:211`) so a no-op "neither rewrites the medium nor emits a change event."

### What does **not** exist anywhere

No idempotency-key store, no request-id dedup table, no `Idempotency-Key` header handling, no monotonic revision counter persisted through `storageDomain` (automation's `revision` is per-rule and never checked on write). `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-30-continuable-subagent-report-tool.md:51` records the absence explicitly as deferred work.

## 4. Typed events: declaration, docs, dispatch

### Rules

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md:105`: "Typed events use declaration merging and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`."

- The map is `interface Events` inside `declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis'`. `@mode` ∈ `emit | waterfall | parallel | serial` (`docs/cordis-primer.md:12,26`).
- The generated matrix `docs/event-producer-consumer.md` lists every declaration site, mode, dispatchers and listeners — regenerate with `pnpm run gen-doc-graphs`.
- **`ignorable` is a different mechanism.** It is a `SessionEvent` *envelope* field (`packages/core/session/src/types.ts:426`, validated at `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:226,239`), used when a build meets an unknown `SessionEventMap` type; it has nothing to do with Cordis `Events`. Only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION`.
- **Scoped emission** is `packages/core/scope`: an event opts in by declaring `this: Scoped&lt;Base&gt;` (e.g. `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:76`, `packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts:159-290`), and `scripts/gen-scoped-events.ts` derives the resolver map from real `scopeTarget(base, key)` calls; zero matches require `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. `ctx.agents.currentInitiator()` (`packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:309`) is a *separate* facility — ambient causal attribution, paired with `withInitiator` (`:341`) / `withoutInitiator` (`:356`).

### The requested complete example (`automation/dispatched`)

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/automation/automation/src/index.ts:43-66`:

```ts
declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
  interface Context {
    automations: AutomationRegistry
  }

  interface Events {
    /**
     * One automation rule matched and its run record was committed, emitted
     * once per committed record, after the write resolved and after a started
     * Agent already holds its message. A later lifecycle transition of the same
     * run updates the record without publishing again, and a match a gate
     * dropped silently publishes nothing. Payload carries plain ids so
     * listeners read records through `ctx.automations`.
     * @param payload - rule id, run id, matched event name, and the outcome recorded.
     * @mode emit
     */
    'automation/dispatched'(payload: {
      ruleId: AutomationRuleId
      runId: AutomationRunId
      eventName: string
      outcome: AutomationRunOutcome
    }): void
  }
}
```

Emitted at `packages/automation/automation-domain/src/index.ts:757-762`. Note the payload deliberately carries **plain ids**, not records, so listeners resolve through the service — which is exactly what makes the `./invariant` cross-check in §2 possible.

A scoped counterexample (agent-scoped, with the required doc line): `packages/goal/goal/src/domain.ts:104-116`.

The domain layer's own event: `packages/storage/storage-domain/src/events.ts:36-48` (`'domain/changed'`, `@mode emit`, closed union discriminated on `operation`, put-only `value`, never the old value; `table`/`key` are `''` for a global write). Current listeners per the matrix: `apiproxy`, `storage-domain` (its own invariant), `workspace`.

### Consumer-side initiator use

`packages/automation/automation-domain/src/index.ts:541` reads `this.selfCtx.agents.currentInitiator()` **synchronously in the emitter's stack**, then hands each match off via `queueMicrotask` + `detached(...)` which wraps the continuation in `agents.withoutInitiator()` (`:566-574`) — a started Agent must not inherit the initiator that happened to trigger it.

## 5. The `./invariant` companion convention

### What `packages/AGENTS.md` requires

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/AGENTS.md:18`:

&gt; **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail `verify-package-invariants`.

Reinforced by `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md:104` ("Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence…") and `packages/AGENTS.md:15` ("Publish state only at its commit point").

### Mechanically enforced by `scripts/package-invariants.ts`

Every `packages/*/*/package.json` is an owner (`:36-53`); the gate checks `src/invariant.ts` for:

- no `@generated` marker — companions must be hand-owned (`:174-179`)
- exactly one `ctx.invariants.register(&lt;own package name&gt;, install)`, name resolving to a local string constant, installer identifier literally `install` (`:190-235`)
- named exports `name`, `inject`, `apply`; **no** default export (`:236-246`)
- an empty `install` body requires the literal marker `No runtime invariant:` in the declaration's leading comment (`:12`, `:265-277`)
- a non-empty `install` must accept and **use** the bound `fail` reporter (`:278-286`)

Runtime side: `InvariantInstaller` and `InvariantFailure` at `packages/runtime-diagnostics/invariants/src/index.ts:24-42`; `InvariantError` at `:49-66`; the installer's own `inject` list rides on the function via `Object.assign(fn, { inject: [...] })`.

Manifest wiring: `"./invariant"` export + `lib/invariant.js` in `files` (`packages/automation/automation-domain/package.json:21-32`), and the package tsconfig references `runtime-diagnostics/invariants` (`packages/automation/automation-domain/tsconfig.json`, last reference).

### A real check

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/invariant.ts:24-59` — event-stream ↔ mutable-data agreement, and directly relevant to a Desktop provider:

```ts
const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) =&gt; {
  ctx.on('domain/changed', (change: DomainChanged) =&gt; {
    const domain = ctx.storage.form('domain').get(change.domain)
    if (domain === undefined) return fail(`domain/changed for '${change.domain}' emitted while that domain is not open`)
    if (change.table === '') {
      if (domain.global.get() !== change.value) return fail(`domain/changed global value for '${change.domain}' differs from the in-memory global`)
      return
    }
    const current = domain.table(change.table).get(change.key)
    switch (change.operation) {
      case 'deleted': if (current !== undefined) return fail(...); return
      case 'put':     if (current !== change.value) return fail(...); return
      default: change satisfies never
    }
  }, { global: true })
}, { inject: ['storage'] })
```

Second real check, cache↔medium divergence: `packages/workspace/workspace/src/invariant.ts:27-49` (fails when a `workspaces` put lands with no cached entity, or a delete lands while the cache still publishes one — "some write path bypassed `ctx.workspaceRegistry`").

Third, the cross-provider one: `packages/automation/automation/src/invariant.ts:18-37` (quoted in §2).

### An explained empty

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/automation/automation-domain/src/invariant.ts:17-26` — the model for a *provider* whose Definition already owns the check:

```
/**
 * No runtime invariant: the relation between a published dispatch and its committed run record
 * belongs to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-automation/invariant`, which checks it for every provider. What is
 * left here is pre-dispatch policy — the kill switch, the causal map, the sliding rate-limit
 * window, and the live-run reservations — decided synchronously against private process-local
 * state before any Agent exists. A companion sees only published events and service reads, so it
 * could observe neither that state nor the ordering that makes the gates binding; a suppression
 * it could confirm has already been recorded as a run for consumers to read.
 */
const install: InvariantInstaller = () =&gt; {}
```

Other explained empties in the same family, each with a different reason: `packages/storage/storage/src/invariant.ts:17-23` (pure registration table, enforced synchronously at call sites), `packages/util/brand/src/invariant.ts:17-21` (pure type utility), `packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/invariant.ts:14-18` (private typed writer is the sole authority). Note the `/* jscpd:ignore-start */ … /* jscpd:ignore-end */` wrapper on the boilerplate-only companions.

## 6. Brand convention

### Where the primitive lives

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/util/brand/src/index.ts` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand`) — type-only, no runtime code, no harness dependency:

```ts
declare const BRAND: unique symbol                                       // :24
export type Branded&lt;B extends string&gt; = string &amp; { readonly [BRAND]: B } // :27
```

Stated policy (`:11-19`): "a package brands the ids it owns… This package owns ONLY the primitive — no concrete id, no runtime code beyond the (erased) type — so the brand vocabulary stays dependency-free."

### The type + same-named factory idiom

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/automation/automation/src/records.ts:15-41`:

```ts
/**
 * Identifies one automation rule. Durable rules take a provider-minted id;
 * a plugin contribution supplies its own. Ids are predictable, so ownership —
 * not secrecy — fences a rule.
 */
export type AutomationRuleId = Branded&lt;'AutomationRuleId'&gt;

/**
 * Brand a string as an {@link AutomationRuleId}.
 * @param id - the raw rule-id string.
 * @returns the same string, branded; no validation is performed.
 */
export function AutomationRuleId(id: string): AutomationRuleId {
  return id as AutomationRuleId
}
```

Type and value share one name (declaration merging), the factory is a plain cast, and both are re-exported from the package entrypoint as *values* (`packages/automation/automation/src/index.ts:16`) alongside the schemas (`:17-29`). Minting: `AutomationRuleId(\`rule-${randomUUID()}\`)` (`automation-domain/src/index.ts:291`), `AutomationRunId(\`run-${randomUUID()}\`)` (`:548`).

Identical shape elsewhere: `SessionId` (`packages/core/session/src/types.ts:22-30`), `GoalId` (`packages/goal/goal/src/types.ts:16`), `MessageFeedbackVersion` (`packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/types.ts:13`), `AttachmentId`/`ImageVariantId` (`packages/attachment/attachment/src/brand.ts:6,18`), `CompactionId`, `TeamId`/`TeamTaskId`/`TeamMessageId`, the five `cordis-host-runner` ids.

### How zod parses into brands

Two variants coexist. **Preferred — `.transform(Factory)`**, `packages/automation/automation/src/records.ts:55-62`:

```ts
/** Rule ids at the durable boundary; branding has no runtime representation. */
const ruleId = z.string().min(1).transform(AutomationRuleId)
const runId  = z.string().min(1).transform(AutomationRunId)
const sessionId = z.string().min(1).transform(SessionId)
```

used in the record schemas at `:186` and `:241-246`. **Inline cast** where the owning package exports no factory: `packages/workspace/workspace/src/spec.ts:14` (`z.string().transform(value =&gt; value as WorkspaceId)`), `packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/spec.ts:21-22, 28`.

Caveat already hit in the repo: zod infers transformed branded fields structurally, so a record schema whose fields brand cannot name the public interface — `message-feedback` resolves it with `as unknown as z.ZodType&lt;MessageFeedbackItem&gt;` and an explanatory comment (`packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/spec.ts:25-39`).

The brand reaches the domain layer only as a phantom: `domainTable&lt;AutomationRuleId, AutomationDurableRule&gt;(automationDurableRule)` (`automation-domain/src/spec.ts:48`) types `KvTable`'s keys while keys stay plain strings on the medium (`storage-domain/src/spec.ts:22-32`).

### 1e. The single connection stream loop and the structural pump faces

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/index.ts:69-112` is the one owner of the Host stream:

```
export const inject = ['connection', 'remote']                      // :64
const sessions   = (): SessionsStreamPump   | undefined =&gt; ctx.get('sessions')    // :76
const workspaces = (): WorkspacesStreamPump | undefined =&gt; ctx.get('workspaces')  // :77
ctx.inject(['sessions', 'workspaces'], () =&gt; {                       // :81
  loop ??= connection.start({
    onMuxEnvelope:  e =&gt; { sessions()?.handleMuxEnvelope(e) },        // :83-85
    onHostEnvelope: e =&gt; { sessions()?.handleHostEnvelope(e)
                           workspaces()?.handleHostEnvelope(e)
                           if (e.payload.type === 'host/remote-event')
                             ctx.remote.$dispatch(e.payload.event, e.payload.args) },  // :86-95
    onConnected:    () =&gt; { sessions()?.handleConnected()
                            workspaces()?.handleConnected()
                            ctx.emit('connection/reset') },          // :96-100
    onStateChange:  s  =&gt; { if (s === 'reconnecting') sessions()?.handleDisconnected() }, // :101-108
  })
})
```

Pumps are resolved **per frame** (late-bound) so a domain reload does not strand the loop (`:73-75`).

**The actual pump face types** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/stream-pumps.ts`:

```ts
/** The sessions service's stream entry points (`ISessions` deliberately omits them). */
export interface SessionsStreamPump {                                    // :14
  handleMuxEnvelope(envelope: RpcRequest&lt;MuxFrame&gt;): void                 // :19
  handleHostEnvelope(envelope: RpcRequest&lt;HostFrame&gt;): void               // :24
  /** Rebuild the Session baseline and every opened window after connection. */
  handleConnected(): void                                                 // :26
  /** Drop generation-scoped live interaction state the moment a generation dies. */
  handleDisconnected(): void                                              // :28
}

/** The workspaces service's stream entry points (`IWorkspaces` deliberately omits them). */
export interface WorkspacesStreamPump {                                   // :32
  handleHostEnvelope(envelope: RpcRequest&lt;HostFrame&gt;): void               // :37
  /** Rebuild the Workspace baseline after connection. */
  handleConnected(): void                                                 // :39
}
```

Module header (`:1-9`): "`ConnectionHandle.start` is one-shot: the Host stream has exactly one owner for the page's lifetime, and that owner is this generic layer. It addresses the domain services by name and narrows them to these faces, so no domain type crosses into the generic layer."

**The renderer feed faces** — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/host-feeds.ts`:

```ts
/** What `ctx.sessions` supplies to the renderer host (`ISessions` satisfies it). */

  readonly list: SlotRendererHost['sessions']['list']
  readonly currentProvideInfo: SlotRendererHost['sessions']['provideInfo']
}

/** What `ctx.workspaces` supplies to the renderer host (`IWorkspaces` satisfies it). */

  /** Workspace list source backing the useWorkspaces standard hook. */

```

Consumed in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:387-421` (`hostFace()`: `ctx.get('workspaces') as WorkspacesHostFeed | undefined`, throws if absent at `:396-399`, injected into the renderer host at `:420`).

Both faces are structural — neither domain package imports the other, and `runtime` imports neither.

## 2. SESSIONS, in brief

**Frames on the connection stream** — both unions declared in one file, `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api/events.ts`:

- `MuxFrame` `:69-108`: `session/event`, `session/subscribed`, `approval/requested|resolved`, `question/requested|resolved`, `session/queue`, `session/jobs`, `session/projection`, `stream/error`.
- `HostFrame` `:127-155`: `host/session-added`, `host/session-removed`, `host/session-status`, `host/agent-error`, `host/workspace-changed`, `host/workspace-removed`, `host/workspace-order-changed`, `host/archived-sessions-changed`, `host/remote-event`, `stream/error`.
- Stream openers `EventsApi.mux` / `EventsApi.host`: `:47-63`.
- Runtime validators (browser parses every frame): `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api/events.schema.ts` — `muxFrameSchema` ends `:67`, `hostFrameSchema` `:70-93`.

**Host emitters**: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:3327` `events: {`, `mux(...)` above, `host(_request, signal)` at `:3432`. The host stream's disposer list `:3443-3532` binds `session/created`, `session/disposed`, `agent/status`, `agent/error`, `domain/changed` (`:3464`, workspace frames `:3479/:3483/:3491/:3501/:3510`), and the forwarded-event loop `:3518-3531`.

**Client side**: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/manager.ts` — `handleMuxEnvelope` `:683-789`, `handleHostEnvelope` `:795-876`, `handleDisconnected` `:887-899`, `handleConnected` `:902-909` (`refreshList()` + `session.resync()` per opened window + subagent catalog refreshes). Service wrapper `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:452-472`; provided at `:348` `rootCtx.reflect.provide('sessions', this, undefined)`.

**How the BFF decides which host events forward to the client** — two distinct mechanisms:

1. **Hand-written frames**: each `HostFrame` variant is an explicit `ctx.on(...)` → `queue.push(frame(...))` in `api-proxy.ts:3443-3514`. Adding one means editing `events.ts`, `events.schema.ts`, and `api-proxy.ts`.
2. **Verbatim forwarding allowlist**: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts:17-29` `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` — a `const` array of 11 cordis event names. `api-proxy.ts:3518` maps it into `ctx.on(name, …)` handlers that wrap each emission as `{ type: 'host/remote-event', event, args }`. Type projection at `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/src/types.ts:15-19` (fills the `TypertRemoteEventSelection` seat). A compile-time shape gate rejects a name that isn't a declared event, binds an `AgentScope`, or isn't one-way: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts:41` `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS satisfies readonly TypertForwardableEvent[]`. Delivery lands on `ctx.remote.$on`, not on a frame variant — dispatched from the runtime loop at `packages/client/runtime/src/client/index.ts:94`.

**Transport**: unary is HTTP `POST /api/&lt;method&gt;`; both streams are **downlink-only WebSockets** at `/api/events.mux` and `/api/events.host` — paths in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/connection/src/api-path.ts:8-14`; browser reader `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/connection/src/client/web-api-client.ts:21-31`, `:35-93`; host pump `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/connection/src/websocket-downlink.ts:51-137` (client→server messages close the socket with 1008 at `:109-111`).

## 3. `packages/api` layout and where a new remote service must be registered

### Layout

```
packages/api/
  gateway/   — @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway    (host: ctx.typertGateway | client: ctx.remote)
  remotes/   — @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-remotes    (no service; host = identity policy + event allowlist,
                                                client = the contribution assembly)
```

`remotes` is the **only** package in the repo with split TypeScript faces (`tsconfig.host.json` + `tsconfig.client.json` under the package, root `tsconfig.json` is a solution only) — rationale in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/README.md` ("Build boundary" section) and `docs/api-gateway.md:101`. `src/remote-events.ts` and `src/types.ts` are deliberately listed in **both** faces' `files`.

Files: `remotes/src/index.ts` (host, 44 lines), `remotes/src/client/index.ts` (assembly, 131 lines), `remotes/src/remote-events.ts`, `remotes/src/types.ts`, `remotes/src/agent-lookup.ts` (211 lines, `createApiRemoteAgentResolver`), `gateway/src/index.ts` (685), `gateway/src/client/index.ts` (633), `gateway/src/types.ts`.

### Every registration point for a hypothetical new host service reachable from the browser

**Path A — Typert Remote (the modern one).** In order:

| # | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the service source | extend `TypertRemoteService` (`packages/typert/protocol/src/index.ts:147`) or `bindTypertRemote`; mark methods `@Remote` / `@RemoteScope` |
| 2 | the package's `package.json` | add `exports["./typert"]` → `./lib/typert.host.{d.ts,js}` **and** `exports["./remote"]` → `./lib/typert.remote-client.{d.ts,js}`, plus all four files in `files[]`. Exact shape enforced by `packages/typert/generator/src/workspace.ts:74-125`. Model: `packages/host/plugin-inventory/package.json:15-49` |
| 3 | **typert type graph** = `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.host.json` | `{ "path": "./packages/&lt;group&gt;/&lt;pkg&gt;" }` in `references` — the Host aggregate is the generator's *only* `ts.Program` seed (`tsdown.config.ts:28`; `docs/api-gateway.md:97`). A package absent here is never analyzed |
| 4 | `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/src/client/index.ts` | value import of `'&lt;pkg&gt;/remote'` (`:4-10`), matching `export type {} from '&lt;pkg&gt;/remote'` (`:15-20`), and an entry in the `$mount` array at `:116-119`. Any client-safe payload types re-exported here too (`:55-96`) |
| 5 | `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.client.json` | `references` entry for the *consuming* client package (not the host package) |
| 6 | a bundle `cordis.patch.yml` | host row mounting the service, e.g. `packages/bundle/app-settings/cordis.patch.yml:11-12` for `plugin-inventory`; the client-side consumer row in `app-chat`/`app-settings`/`web-platform` |
| 7 | that bundle's `package.json` | dependency on the row's package (see `packages/client/AGENTS.md:137`) |
| 8 | the consuming client package | `export const inject = ['remote', 'remote.&lt;namespace&gt;']` — `packages/client/ui-settings-plugin-inventory/src/client/index.ts:23` |
| 9 | (only if a Host object crosses the wire) | a `TypertLookupMap` declaration + a runtime provider on `ctx.typert.lookups`; app-wide `agent`/`session` policy is `packages/api/remotes/src/agent-lookup.ts` |
| 10 | (only if new host events must reach the browser) | `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` in `packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts:17` |

There is **no** gateway allowlist for methods. `TypertGatewayService.claimsEndpoint` (`packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts:114-137`) accepts any two-segment endpoint backed by a strict descriptor or a live SRC marker. The nearest thing to an allowlist is `PRIVILEGED_METHODS` in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/connection/src/index.ts:89-119`, which is a **loopback pin for legacy apiproxy method names only** — the Typert channel is registered wholesale as `{ authority: 'trusted-host' }` (`gateway/src/index.ts:109`).

### `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts` — role: **none** in this path

## 4. `packages/typert`: what it generates, when, from what

Four packages (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/README.md`):

| Package | Role | ctx key |
|---|---|---|
| `registry/` | stores runtime reflection + schemas + lookups | `ctx.typert` |
| `loader/` | discovers Loader entries, registers generated host artifacts | consumes `ctx.loader`, `ctx.typert` |
| `generator/` | build-time library (analyzer → model → emitter → renderer) | none |
| `protocol/` | decorators, bindings, merge-extensible protocol maps | none |

**What it generates** (per contributing package, into `&lt;pkg&gt;/lib/`): `typert.host.js`, `typert.host.d.ts`, and — when the package has Remote methods — `typert.remote-client.js`, `typert.remote-client.d.ts`, `typert.remote-client.d.ts.map`. Written by `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/typert/generator/src/tsdown-plugin.ts:103-124`; the same function *deletes* stale `typert.remote-client.*` when a host artifact no longer has Remote methods (`:117-123`). Table of consumers: `docs/api-gateway.md:105-111`.

**When gen runs / the gate**:

## Surface-health subscription mechanism

`DesktopRoot` uses two `useSyncExternalStore` pairs closed over once per fiber: `ctx.desktop.state.subscribe/getSnapshot` for the Desktop, and `ctx.slots.subscribe('desktop.window.surface', fn)` + `ctx.slots.getVersion('desktop.window.surface')` for the ledger — the same per-key version channel the renderer's own outlets use, which the core bumps for registrations, withdrawals *and* crash-abdications. Health itself is read during render via `ctx.slots.entriesOfSlot(key)` (the shadowing projection: one live winner per key) plus `ctx.desktop.surfaces()` for `pluginName`; it is not a uSES snapshot because a freshly built object fails the identity check.

One in-memory Desktop `fx-desktop` at revision 1 holding one `chat` Window (`launchSchemaVersion: 1`), one chat `SurfaceDescriptor`. `resolve` always answers with that Desktop (its id is authoritative — a stale client id gets this one back and stores it). `openWindow`/`closeWindow` go through a shared guard: wrong `desktopId` → `rejected missing-desktop`; repeated `mutationId` → `committed` with the current revision, no write; stale `expectedRevision` → `conflict` with the authoritative snapshot; then unknown surface → `rejected unknown-surface`, duplicate caller-minted window id → `conflict`, missing window → `rejected missing-window`. # Phase 2 adversarial review — findings

## REAL — should block

### 1. Retention prunes by `updatedAt`, which a reopen never touches, so the most-reopened Desktop is deleted first — MAJOR
`packages/desktop/desktop-domain/src/index.ts:405` sorts prune candidates by ascending `updatedAt`. That field has exactly two writers: `create()` at `:255` and `mutate()` at `:349`. `_resolve` (`:182-189`) reads and returns the record without touching it.

Phase 2 seeds the single Window at creation and ships **no launcher UI**, so an ordinary user never issues a mutation. Every Desktop's `updatedAt` is therefore frozen at its creation instant forever.

Failure: a user's daily-driver Desktop created 2026-06-01 and reopened every day since. Fifty throwaway Desktops accumulate from new tabs and cleared `sessionStorage`. The 51st creation calls `prune()`; the daily Desktop has the oldest `updatedAt` and is deleted first. The next load resolves a missing id and silently swaps in a fresh Desktop. The durable Window record — the entire point of the phase — is gone, and the most-used Desktop is precisely the one retention targets.

The Config JSDoc at `:35-38` claims "Fifty covers the reopen history a person accumulates," but the metric does not track reopens.

*Remedy: stamp a `lastResolvedAt` (or bump `updatedAt`) on a successful `_resolve` and sort retention on that.*

### 2. `?desktop=` plus a missing record creates a new Desktop on every reconnect — MAJOR
`packages/client/desktop-runtime/src/client/identity.ts:26-39` returns the URL parameter unconditionally, ahead of `sessionStorage`. `service.ts:71-81` re-reads it on every resolve and writes only the *answer* to storage — which the parameter then keeps overriding. `src/client/index.ts:47-50` calls `refresh()` on every `connection/reset`.

Failure: a user has `?desktop=D1` bookmarked and D1 was pruned (finding 1) or the storage root was reset. Load → resolve(D1) missing → create D2. A flaky connection fires `connection/reset` → resolve(**D1** again) → missing → create D3. `installBaseline` (`manager.ts:60-62`) installs an unfamiliar id unconditionally, so any Window the user opened on D2 vanishes. This repeats per reconnect and burns a retention slot each cycle, accelerating finding 1.

Note the e2e never exercises this: launches 2 and 3 use `?desktop=` against a record that *exists*.

*Remedy: once a resolve answers with an id different from the one requested, stop offering the URL parameter and prefer the remembered id.*

### 3. An event arriving during the first baseline resolve is dropped, then a stale baseline installs over it — MAJOR
`manager.ts:76` drops any update whose id does not match the held Desktop — which is true for *every* event while the mirror is still `LOADING` (`desktopId: null`). `manager.ts:59-65` then installs the older baseline.

Failure: two tabs on one Desktop via `?desktop=X`. Tab A boots; its resolve reads X@5. Before the response lands, tab B opens a Window → X@6 → forwarded to A → **dropped** (A holds no Desktop yet). A's baseline installs X@5. A never shows B's Window until the next commit on X or the next `connection/reset`.

`mirror.client.spec.ts:51` pins the drop as correct behavior; nothing covers the stale-baseline consequence. The apply guard is strictly-greater for events and equal-replace for baselines on switch, which is right for switch — the hole is specifically the null-to-first-baseline window.

*Remedy: retain the highest snapshot seen per desktop id while a resolve is in flight, and re-apply it after the baseline installs.*

### 4. A `connection/reset` during an in-flight resolve is coalesced into the doomed request and never retried — MAJOR (narrow)
`service.ts:64-68`: `refresh()` joins `inflightResolve` and issues nothing new. `packages/client/runtime/src/client/index.ts:96-100`: `connection/reset` fires from `onConnected` — once per established generation, so no further reset arrives while the connection stays healthy.

Failure: the resolve's HTTP request black-holes on a host restart (long timeout). The stream reconnects at t=1s → `connection/reset` → `refresh()` coalesces into the hung request. At t=30s it fails → `markUnavailable()`. The connection is now healthy, but no further reset will fire — the shell renders empty until the next disconnect.

The `refresh()` JSDoc at `:60-61` ("A call after settlement resolves anew, which is what a reconnect needs") names the gap without owning the consequence. Single-flight itself is correct and load-bearing — it prevents the first-visit double-create, and `.finally` at `:66` clears on both success and rejection.

*Remedy: set a "reset arrived while in flight" flag and re-resolve once on settlement.*

Client-side filtering is not isolation. The note lists several deferred items and does not list this one.

*Remedy: scope the desktop forward per connection, or record it as a deferred item with a named owner before Phase 3 lands session ids in launch state.*

## BENIGN — candidates I killed, and where the code handles them

- **Idempotency's single `lastMutationId` slot.** At-most-once *is* preserved, by CAS (`:341`), not by the slot. Revision is monotonic, so a replay after an intervening commit can never match a stale `expectedRevision`. Exact guarantee delivered: at-most-once holds for any retry that keeps its **original** `expectedRevision`; a client re-sending the same `mutationId` at a *newer* expectedRevision after an intervening commit would double-apply — the client never does that (`service.ts:112-118,127-132` mint a fresh id per intent and never retry). Note line 44 and the Definition JSDoc (`desktop/src/index.ts:100-106`, "already produced *the current revision*") both state this precisely. No overclaim.
- **Two concurrent `resolve({id:X})` for a missing X.** No double-create under one id, no corruption: each `create()` mints its own `desktop-${randomUUID()}` (`:252`). They diverge into two Desktops, which is documented D7 behavior. The tail map does not cover resolve-create, but nothing needs it to.
- **Storage write rejection leaving tails/memory inconsistent.** It does not. `records.set` runs only *after* the medium write (`domain.ts:308-312`), so a failed put leaves memory at the old revision; the tail swallows the rejection (`:363`) and `finally` cleans the map (`:365-367`). Pinned by `durability.spec.ts:104`.
- **Publish-at-commit ordering.** `put` writes medium → memory → resolves, so `getSnapshot` already sees the committed revision when `desktop/changed` fires. The invariant's relation holds.
- **Invariant reading `held.revision` after `fail(held === undefined)`.** Safe: `InvariantFailure` is `(message: string) =&gt; never` and genuinely throws, so TypeScript narrows correctly.
- **Crash-abdication bumping the subscribed version.** `reportEntryError` calls `markDirty` (`ui-slots:1156-1160`) and `entriesOfSlot` skips abdicated entries (`:1000`), so the tile appears with no user interaction.
- **Shadowing (a compatible entry behind an incompatible winner).** `readSurfaceHealth` (`DesktopRoot.tsx:32-33`) and the renderer (`scoped-slots.tsx:768`) use the *same* `entriesOfSlot(...).find(key===)` projection, so the health read always describes the entry that would actually render. **Host forwarding loop** — `packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:3519-3535`, inside `events.host(_request, signal)` `:3436-3538`:

```ts
...API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS.map(name =&gt; ctx.on(
  name,
  ((...args: unknown[]) =&gt; {
    queue.push(frame({ type: 'host/remote-event', event: name, args: assertJsonArgs(name, args) }))

```

Per-connection mechanics:
- **What identifies a connection:** nothing but the stream call itself. `events.host` receives a freshly minted `rpcId` and an empty payload — `fetch/handler.ts:257-259` (SSE GET) and `websocket-downlink.ts:77-82` (WS upgrade) both synthesize `{ rpcId: RpcId(randomUUID()), payload: {} }`. There is no connection id, cookie, or client id anywhere on this path.
- **What state each host-stream subscriber holds:** a private `FrameQueue&lt;RpcRequest&lt;HostFrame&gt;&gt;` `:3437` (class at `:359-390`), plus per-connection dedup baselines `committedWorkspaceIds` `:3439`, `committedWorkspaceOrder` `:3442`, `archivedSessionIds` `:3446`, and a `disposers` array `:3447-3536` torn down by `queue.iterate(signal, …)` `:3537`. The host stream, unlike the mux, is **not** kept in a registry set — each closure is fully self-contained.
- **Where a per-connection filter could attach:** inside that same closure, beside `committedWorkspaceIds`. The forwarding listener is a per-connection closure already; a mutable `heldDesktopId` in scope, read at `:3529` before `queue.push`, is structurally identical to how `committedWorkspaceIds` gates `host/workspace-changed` at `:3511-3517`.

**Mux precedent (per-connection subscription state, but not selective):** `mux(_request, signal)` `:3332-3434` mints its own queue `:3333`, adds it to the module-level `muxQueues` set `:3334` (declared `:1077`), and then subscribes **every** session unconditionally:

```ts

```

`subscribeSession` `:425-427` pushes `{ type: 'session/subscribed', sessionId, lastSeq: session.seq - 1 }`. `ctx.on('session/created', …)` `:3397-3407` subscribes late-born sessions to the same queue. So the "subscribed" flow is **per-connection state, all-sessions scope** — the connection holds a `session/subscribed` baseline frame per session and a per-connection `openCalls: Map&lt;SessionId, Map&lt;string, …&gt;&gt;` `:3375`, but it never chose a subset. There is no existing selective per-connection subscription anywhere in the proxy to mirror.

**Client** — `packages/client/runtime/src/client/index.ts:94`: `if (frame.type === 'host/remote-event') ctx.remote.$dispatch(frame.event, frame.args)`. Note the loop is gated on both `sessions` and `workspaces` at `:81`.

**Gateway client** — `packages/api/gateway/src/client/index.ts`: `subscriptions = new Map&lt;string, RemoteEventSubscription[]&gt;()` `:99`; `$on` `:118-136` pushes a `{ listener }` identity record inside `this.ctx.effect(…)` so the subscription unwinds with the *calling* fiber (`:88-90` explains identity-by-registration); `$dispatch(event, args)` `:143-164` snapshots the listener array `:148` and contains sync throws and rejected promises `:149-162`. `$dispatch` takes a bare string — no filtering hook, no envelope.

**Desktop consumer** — `packages/client/desktop-runtime/src/client/index.ts:42` `ctx.remote.$on('desktop/changed', (payload) =&gt; { desktop.receive(payload.snapshot) })`; `:43` for `surfaces-changed` → `refreshSurfaces()`. The drop is done client-side in `service.ts:151-162` ("Changes to another browser's Desktop reach this client too and the mirror drops them") and `manager.ts:74-79` (`if (current.desktopId !== snapshot.id || snapshot.revision &lt;= current.revision) return false`).

**What the Host knows about which Desktop a connection holds: nothing.** `desktop.resolve` arrives through the Typert gateway (`packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts:104-111` registers an `/api` interceptor; `invoke` `:145-…` sees only `namespace`, `method`, `args`, `signal`). The connection RPC handler signature `packages/client/connection/src/rpc.ts:15-19` is `(endpoint, payload, signal) =&gt; Promise&lt;RpcResult&lt;unknown&gt;&gt;` — no connection handle. The unary call and the host stream share no identity, so correlating them requires either a new subscribe unary carrying a `desktopId` or a connection identity threaded through both. The phase-2 note flags this explicitly as owed: *"per-connection scoping is owed before Phase 3 puts Session ids into launch state (owner: Phase 3)"* (`.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-28-durable-desktop-window-record.md`, Consequences).

## 4. The SurfaceDefinition launch resolver

`packages/desktop/surface-chat/src/index.ts` is 51 lines and contains **only** the registration. `CHAT_LAUNCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` `:26`, `name = 'surface-chat'` `:29`, `inject = ['desktop']` `:32`, and `apply` `:38-51` calling `ctx.effect(() =&gt; ctx.desktop.registerSurface({ id: SurfaceId('chat'), pluginName, label: 'Chat', launchSchemaVersion, launchSchema: windowLaunchState, defaultLaunchState: {}, defaultPlacement: 'full' }))`. `:45-46` records why the schema is the record schema rather than `{}`: "a Window's launch state is stored and replayed, so accepting any JSON object keeps a Window that a later Chat release opens with real launch keys readable at this version." No resolver, no host-service reach, no other exports. `invariant.ts` is a justified empty installer.

**What it could reach.** `package.json` peerDeps are exactly `dsh-desktop`, `dsh-invariants`, `cordis`; `tsconfig.json` references only `vendor/cordis`, `../desktop`, `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`. It is a plain host-plane function plugin loaded as a bundle row (`packages/bundle/app-chat/cordis.patch.yml:41-45`), so `inject` may name any host service and `ctx.get('sessions')` / `ctx.get('workspaceRegistry')` are reachable with a tsconfig reference + peerDep added — there is no plane obstacle on this side.

**The plane rule the package exists to satisfy** is the *client* direction, stated at `src/index.ts:1-9` and in the phase-2 note's alternatives: `ui-chat-surface` compiles in the Client face, and a host-half import of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop` there would put both planes' `Context.desktop` declaration merges into one program. That constrains where the definition lives, not what host services the definition may inject. The counter-pressure on injecting `sessions` into `SurfaceDefinition` is the packages-level rule "Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers" — `SurfaceDefinition` today is a pure data record that `desktop-domain` copies field-by-field in `describe()` (`desktop-domain/src/index.ts:83-92`) and validates via `surfaceDescriptor.parse` (`:162`); a callable member would be the first non-data field besides `launchSchema`.

## 5. Store-scope / duplicate-surface collision

**The rejection** — `desktop-domain/src/index.ts:222-229`:

```ts
// One Window per Surface while a Surface's browser state is keyed by
// Surface id alone: a second Window would draw the first one's state.
if (current.windows.some(window =&gt; window.surfaceId === request.surfaceId)) {
  return settled(rejected(
    'duplicate-surface',
    `desktop "${current.id}" already holds a window of surface "${request.surfaceId}"`,
  ))
}
```

Contract restatements: `desktop/src/index.ts:103-105`, `types.ts:193-197`. Test: `desktop-domain/tests/mutations.spec.ts:207`. Wire fixture mirror: `packages/client/connection/src/client/fixture.ts:3218-3223`.

**The actual collision, in two parts.**

*(a) Store instance keying.* `ui-desktop` declares `'desktop.window.surface': { kind: 'keyed'; scope: 'root'; owner: WindowSurfaceOwnerProps; meta: { launchSchemaVersion: number } }` (`packages/client/ui-desktop/src/client/index.ts:54-59`, register at `:116`). `ui-chat-surface` registers under `key: 'chat'` with an exclusive store factory (`packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/index.ts:127-149`, `store: createLayoutStore` `:142`). The renderer resolves a store per render at `packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/scoped-slots.tsx:417-419` → `host.storeOf(entry, info?.sessionId)` → `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:429-442`:

```ts
const key = record.scope === 'root' ? ROOT_INSTANCE_KEY : sessionId    // :432
...
instance = record.scope === 'root' ? handle.create() : handle.create(key)   // :438
record.instances.set(key, instance)
```

`ROOT_INSTANCE_KEY = 'root'` (`:50`). Two Windows of one Surface hit the same `StoredEntry` (keyed dispatch resolves by `entryKey: record.surfaceId`, `DesktopFrame.tsx:102`), therefore the same handle, therefore the literal same `StoreInstanceLike` — one sidebar width, one details-collapsed bit, shared. The only available discriminator today is `sessionId`, and the phase-2 note rejects reaching for it: *"Scoping `desktop.window.surface` per session. Rejected … non-root store resolution keys by session, which would fragment layout state and remount windows on session switches."*

*(b) Singleton service + global session selection.* `ctx.layout` is provided once per plugin fiber (`ui-chat-surface/src/client/index.ts:150`, `layout.attachPanels(actions)` at `:145-148`), not once per Window. And `ChatSurface` ignores its owner share entirely — module doc `:3-5` "a Chat Window carries no launch state, and the surface renders the globally selected Session exactly as before Windows existed" — reading the current session from the global feed at `ChatSurface.tsx:96-99` (`useSessions(s =&gt; s.current …)`), which reaches it through `SlotRegistry.hostFace()`'s `sessions.provideInfo = sessions.currentProvideInfo` (`slots.ts:418-421`). So even with per-Window stores, two Chat Windows would still show the same conversation until launch state carries a Session id.

## 6. Bounds semantics and the `'full'` blast radius

**Typed:** `types.ts:67-72` (`WindowBounds`), `:89` (`bounds: WindowBounds | null`), `:91` (`mode: 'full'`), `:179` (`SurfaceDescriptor.defaultPlacement: 'full'`), `index.ts:81` (`SurfaceDefinition.defaultPlacement: 'full'`).

**Validated:** `records.ts:48-53` (`windowBounds`), `:61` (`bounds: z.union([windowBounds, z.null()])`), `:62` (`mode: z.literal('full')`), `:117` (`defaultPlacement: z.literal('full')`). These schemas are simultaneously the durable boundary — `desktop-domain/src/spec.ts:17-23` builds domain `desktop` **v0** with `domainTable&lt;DesktopId, DesktopSnapshot&gt;(desktopSnapshot)`, so a records change is a stored-format change.

**Defaulted:** `desktop-domain/src/index.ts:337-338` — `bounds: null`, `mode: definition.defaultPlacement`. Nothing else ever writes either field; there is no update-bounds mutation, no focus concept, and no `zOrder` mutation (`nextZOrder` `:78-80` and the seed `zOrder: 0` `:307` are the only writers).

# Phase 3 surface inventory — page-wide Session selection in `packages/client/session-runtime` and consumers

## 1. The global selection surface

### 1a. `SessionListState.current` — defined `packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:80-98` (field at `:85`)

It rides the *same* snapshot as the list rows on purpose (`service.ts:76-79`: "arbitrated: the single useSessions standard hook reads list and selection together — sidebar highlighting and SessionProvider share one fact source").

Backing state, all in `SessionRuntime`:
- `service.ts:257` `private readonly selection: SnapshotStore&lt;SessionSelection&gt;` — persisted cell, `localStorage` key `dsh.sessions.current` (`service.ts:284-286`). Shape at `service.ts:101-104`: `{ sessionId?, subagentAddress? }` (the address persists so subagent breadcrumb routes survive reload).
- `manager.ts:151` `private selected: SessionId | undefined` — the wire-truth authority. The store is its projection.
- `service.ts:268` `private watched` — the "staged" id, a *separate* variable that follows `current` but holds its last defined value across masked gaps.
- `service.ts:270` `deferredRemovals` — teardowns parked behind the staged occupant.

The projection masks an absent selection rather than pruning it (`manager.ts:1061-1064`): `current` is `selected` only when `selected` is in `items` **or** in `this.addresses`; otherwise `undefined`. `service.ts:717-731` then wipes the persisted cell whenever `current` is `undefined`, and writes it when a listed `current` differs from the persisted pair.

| Site | What it reads it for |

### 1b. `currentProvideInfo`

- Declared on the outward face: `packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/contract/sessions.ts:29`.
- Implemented `service.ts:247` + `:328`, delegated to `SessionProvideChannel` (`packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/provide.ts:44, 58-64`).
- Republished by `SessionProvideChannel.publishCurrent()` (`provide.ts:106-120`) on **two** axes: every `list` write (`service.ts:316-319`) and every roster change (`provide.ts:168-172`). Identity comparison dedupes.
- Consumed at exactly one place in production: `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:418-421` puts it on the renderer host as `host.sessions.provideInfo`. Narrowed contract: `packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/host-feeds.ts:17`, `packages/client/ui-slots/src/renderer.ts:163-174`.
- Test double: `packages/test-support/client-runtime/src/sessions.ts:180, 217`.

### 1c. `sessions.open()` — what it actually does

Contract `contract/sessions.ts:36-40`; impl `service.ts:372-374` → `SessionManager.select()` (`manager.ts:185-202`). `select()` is **pure selection bookkeeping plus one navigation-shaped side effect chain**:

1. throws on an unknown id (`manager.ts:187-189`) — "must exist in the list; unknown ids fail loud";
2. retains/installs a subagent address and calls `session.configureSubagent(...)` (`manager.ts:190-196`) — which can trigger `resync()` if the address changed (`session.ts:544-552`);
3. `this.selected = sessionId`;
4. **clears the completion reminder** — "Looking at the session consumes its completion reminder" (`manager.ts:198-199`);
5. `void this.refreshSubagents(sessionId)` — a subagent-catalog RPC;
6. `notifyNow()`.

It does **not** open the event window directly. The window opens as a *consequence*: `list.subscribe` → `SessionRuntime.followCurrent()` (`service.ts:606-623`) → `record.session.open()` + `this.manager.refreshSubagents(current)`.

Sibling entry points: `openSubagent()` (`service.ts:380-382` → `manager.ts:208-220`, validates the child is a healthy catalog entry), `clear()` (`service.ts:422-424` → `manager.ts:223-226`).

**Callers of `open()`/`clear()`/`openSubagent()`:**
- `packages/client/workspace-runtime/src/client/service.ts:148` (initial selection), `:189` (`startSession` result), `:185` + `:343` (`clear()`)
- `packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/index.ts:77` (row click), `:90` (open the fork child)
- `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts:231` (workspace switch lands a new session), `:268` (header `open`), `:420` (`forkAt` child)
- `packages/client/ui-workflow-run/src/client/index.ts:30` (`openSession` from a workflow node)
- `packages/client/ui-subagent/src/client/index.ts:50` (`openSubagent`)

### 1d. The implicit-current `SessionProvider`

`packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/session-provider.tsx:150-160`. It takes **no id**: it reads `host.sessions.provideInfo`, keys the subtree `key={id}`, renders `empty()` when `sessionId === undefined`. The renderer hands it to any entry declaring a `scope: 'session'` child (`scoped-slots.tsx:436-438`; type seat `ui-slots/src/index.ts:384-388`, `SessionAreaProps` at `:339-344`).

**No shipped registrant calls it.** The only `SessionProvider(...)` invocations are in tests (`packages/test-support/client-runtime/tests/runtime.client.spec.tsx:36`, `packages/client/ui-trajectory/tests/views.client.spec.tsx:268,284`, `ui-renderer/tests/scoped-slots.client.spec.tsx:685,727`). In the shipped tree the id reaches components through the *root* provider instead — see §2.

### 1e. Invariants tying these together

- **One staged session at a time.** `service.ts:1-15` and `README.md:79`: "Scope teardown is stage-driven, single-occupant today — the staged session follows `list.current` exactly (staging is the open signal: the event window opens ⟺ the session is on stage)… The staged state can widen to a multi-pane list when concurrent panes land."
- **One session id in the render tree at a time.** There is exactly one `BindingContext.Provider` at the root (`scoped-slots.tsx:907`), so every `scope: 'session'` and `'session-maybe'` outlet in the page resolves the *same* id.
- **Stage move is the only sweep trigger.** `followCurrent` calls `sweepDeferred()` (`service.ts:614`, `:769-790`); a removed-while-staged session's scope survives frozen until the stage moves.
- **Selection survives transient absence** (`service.ts:250-256`, `manager.ts:1061-1064`) so reconnect re-pulls do not destroy the staged scope.

## 2. The session-scope machinery in the renderer

### How a scoped slot resolves *which* session

`packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/scoped-slots.tsx`:

1. `createSlotRenderer().renderRoot` (`:902-914`) wraps the whole tree in **one** `&lt;SessionMaybeProvider&gt;`.
2. `SessionMaybeProvider` (`session-provider.tsx:125-133`) subscribes `host.sessions.provideInfo` and puts the resulting `SessionMaybeProvideInfo` into a module-level React context (`session-provider.tsx:31` `BindingContext`).
3. Every outlet reads it: `SlotOutlet` (`scoped-slots.tsx:668`) calls `useSessionMaybeProvideInfo()`.
4. Dispatch (`renderOutletContent`, `:683-755`):
   - `spec.scope === 'session'` and `sessionInfo.sessionId === undefined` → `strictSessionAbsent` (`:695`), render the owner's fallback (`:696-698`) and skip election entirely (`:701`).
   - `scope: 'session'` → `&lt;StrictSessionEntry&gt;` (`:618-644`), which returns `null` with no session and otherwise remounts under `key={info.sessionId}`.
   - `scope: 'session-maybe'` → `&lt;SessionMaybeEntry&gt;` (`:547-591`), the *adoption* machine: born blank it adopts the first id without remounting; a later switch or loss bumps `epoch` and remounts (doc `:534-546`).
   - `scope: 'root'` → `&lt;RootEntry&gt;` (`:603-616`).

**The mechanism in one sentence:** the "current" session id enters the render tree at exactly one point — `SessionMaybeProvider` subscribing the runtime's `currentProvideInfo` observable — and everything downstream reads it from React context.

### What a "provide bundle" / `provideInfo` is

`SessionMaybeProvideInfo` — `packages/client/ui-slots/src/renderer.ts:62-83`:
```ts
{ sessionId: string | undefined
  hooks: Record&lt;string, HostObservable&lt;unknown&gt; | undefined&gt;   // static roster; values absent with the session
  props: Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;
  projections?: { faceOf(key: string): HostObservable&lt;unknown&gt; } }
```
`SessionProvideInfo` (`renderer.ts:85-90`) narrows `sessionId: string` and all hooks defined.

Materialized in `SessionProvideChannel.materializeInfo(binding)` (`provide.ts:128-165`) from a roster of `SessionProvideDescriptor`s (`service.ts:219-226`). The runtime contributes the first one itself — `'session'` → `useSession` (`provide.ts:52-55`), "no renderer special case". Fail-loud on undeclared/missing/duplicate members. The no-session static twin is `materializeMaybeInfo()` (`provide.ts:175-189`): same key roster, all values `undefined`, no `projections` face.

One bundle per **scope record**, stored at `service.ts:203` (`ScopeRecord.provideInfo`), minted in `resolve()` (`service.ts:647`) and re-minted wholesale on roster change (`service.ts:321-325`).

Bundle identity is the renderer's cache axis: `sessionInjectCache` / `sessionMaybeInjectCache` / `standardPropsCache` are all `WeakMap&lt;entry, WeakMap&lt;info, …&gt;&gt;` (`scoped-slots.tsx:96-98, 335-341`).

### `SessionStandardProps` — the merge

Declared empty in `packages/client/ui-slots/src/index.ts:205,212,219`; merged with real members by the sessions domain at `packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/index.ts:99-125`:
```ts
SessionStandardProps      = { useSession: SnapshotSelectorHook&lt;ConversationSnapshot&gt;; sessionId: SessionId; useProjection: UseProjection }
SessionMaybeStandardProps = { useSession: Maybe…; sessionId: SessionId | undefined; useProjection: UseProjection }
GlobalStandardProps       = { useSessions: SnapshotSelectorHook&lt;SessionListState&gt; }
```
plus `ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts:280-292` which merges `useInput` / `inputActions` into the same seats.

Assembly happens in `standardProps()` (`scoped-slots.tsx:344-381`): `useSessions`/`useWorkspaces` from `cache.root`, then each `info.hooks` source bound to `use&lt;Name&gt;` (strict → `observableHook`, maybe → `maybeObservableHook`), `info.props` spread, then `standard['sessionId'] = info.sessionId` (`:377`) and `standard['useProjection'] = projectionHook(info)` (`:378`).

Also entering per-session: `host.storeOf(entry, info?.sessionId)` (`scoped-slots.tsx:417-425`) → `SlotRegistry.resolveStore` (`slots.ts:437-452`) keyed per `(handle, sessionId)`; and `inject` receives `info.sessionId` as its first positional argument (`scoped-slots.tsx:102-111`; typed at `ui-slots/src/index.ts:487-495`).

### Is there already an explicit-id boundary?

**No production one.** What exists:
- `SessionRuntime.provideInfo(id)` — `service.ts:587-589` — resolves a bundle for an arbitrary id, explicitly documented as pure/render-safe ("no staging, no window side effects (StrictMode double-invokes and concurrent discarded passes must stay free)"). It is **private**.
- `SessionRuntime.binding(id)` (`service.ts:576-578`) and `scope(id)` (`service.ts:539-541`) are public explicit-id resolvers, but they hand back business objects, not render bundles.
- `TestSessions.provideInfo(id)` / `maybeProvideInfo(id)` — `packages/test-support/client-runtime/src/sessions.ts:334-348` — public, bench-only, described as "legacy provideInfo/maybeProvideInfo lookups" (`sessions.ts:169`).
- `BindingContext` is a plain React context whose provider is a module-level component; `SessionProvider` (`session-provider.tsx:150-160`) already writes it with `key={id}` — but sources `id` from `host.sessions.provideInfo`, not from props.

So the pieces for an explicit-id boundary (per-id bundle materialization, an id-keyed context, per-id store resolution) all exist; the only missing link is a public `provideInfo(id)` on `ISessions` and a provider component that takes the id as a prop.

## 3. The Session object model

### Identity

One `Session` per id, held in `SessionManager.sessions: Map&lt;SessionId, Session&gt;` (`manager.ts:107`). `get(id)` (`manager.ts:272-306`) is the sole lazy constructor; it also replays the pre-instantiation buffer and syncs blank/running from the list row. `drop(id)` (`manager.ts:262-264`) deletes it.

Identity is stable **while the id is eligible**. `SessionRuntime.resolve()` (`service.ts:631-651`) mints one `ScopeRecord` per id — `{ fiber, ctx, binding, session, provideInfo }` — and `session.bindScope(ctx)` throws on a second bind (`session.ts:172-175`). `eligible()` (`service.ts:654-657`) = `current === id || ids.includes(id)`.

### Event-window lifecycle

- Opened by `Session.open()` (`session.ts:369-378`): idempotent — `'open'` returns resolved, an in-flight open returns the same promise. Pulls the tail page (`doOpen`, `session.ts:618-648`).
- Called only from `SessionRuntime.followCurrent()` (`service.ts:620`). **Nothing else opens a window.**
- `resync()` (`session.ts:420-442`): bumps `openGeneration`, resets window/pending/liveBuffer, re-opens. Called by `SessionManager.handleConnected()` for **every resident instance** (`manager.ts:908`) and by `configureSubagent` on an address change (`session.ts:550`).
- Closed: never explicitly. There is no `close()`. The window dies with the instance via `dropScope` (`service.ts:757-766`) → `fiber.dispose()`, `session.unbindScope()`, `slots.pruneStoreScope(id)`, `manager.drop(id)`.
- `Session.dispose()` is a no-op (`session.ts:593-594`) — "No-op because session instances remain resident."

### Refcounts

**None on the session axis.** The only refcount in the client runtime is on the *slot store handle* axis: `SlotRegistry._acquire/_release` (`packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:98, 377, 384, 445-461`), counting registrations of a store handle, not viewers of a session.

### View-specific vs. list/background

Module header, `session.ts:1`: **"Sessions remain resident after creation so they continue consuming mux frames off-screen."**

**Page-wide, arrives for every session regardless of viewing:**
- The mux stream is a *single* per-connection stream: `packages/client/connection/src/client/connection.ts:128` `this.api.events.mux({}, …)` — no session argument. Host side `packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:3332-3340` subscribes **every** session in `ctx.sessions.list()` at stream open, plus pending-question/approval replay, queue baselines, and job baselines for all sessions; `session/created` subscribes newcomers (`:3396-3399`).
- Frames therefore land in `SessionManager.handleMuxEnvelope` (`manager.ts:683`) for all sessions. Manager-level, session-instance-independent state: `projectionStores` (`manager.ts:129`, applied at `:701-703` for uninstantiated sessions too), `jobsBySession` (`:707-713`), `pendingInteractions` (the sidebar amber dot — `:112-116`, "Manager-owned rather than read off Session instances because the sidebar must light up for sessions never instantiated"), `pendingBuffers` (`:111`), `completedNotifications` (`:117-122`).
- Frames carrying a `sessionId` reach a `Session` only when instantiated (`manager.ts:751-788`): "no lazy build; non-pending frames for uninstantiated sessions drop — history backfills them on open."
- `session/subscribed` (`manager.ts:714-734`, `session.ts:482-490`) is the per-session mux-generation baseline: truncates projections past `lastSeq`, clears the jobs and queue mirrors, sets `subscribedLastSeq` for gap detection.
- Host-stream frames (running/removed/agent-error/added) go through `handleHostEnvelope` (`manager.ts:790+`) for all sessions.

**View-specific (created on staging, destroyed with the scope):**
- The history event window itself (`session.history` RPC; `Session.events`/`views`/`baseSeq`/`hasMore`) and the `ConversationNodeAssembler` fold built over it (`session.ts:87, 151-156`).
- The Agent scope fiber + tagged `AgentContext` (`scope.ts:57-68`) and everything registered on it — input shell listeners (`ui-conversation/src/client/input/hub.ts:103-111`), slash controller, popups.
- The provide bundle (`ScopeRecord.provideInfo`).
- Per-session slot store instances (`slots.ts:437-452`, pruned by `pruneStoreScope`, `slots.ts:275-282` — which also **clears persisted storage**).
- The subagent catalog pull `refreshSubagents(current)` (`service.ts:621`, `manager.ts:200`).

### Zero / two viewers today

- **Zero viewers, session stays current:** the window stays open. Nothing observes mount/unmount; `followCurrent` keys off `current`, not renders. `strictSessionAbsent` outlets rendering nothing does not close anything.
- **Zero viewers because `current` moved:** `followCurrent` moves `watched`, sweeps deferrals, opens the new one. The previous session's scope is **not** torn down — only ineligibility (leaving the list) tears down, via `pruneScopes` (`service.ts:737-748`).
- **Two components viewing one session:** they both resolve the same `ScopeRecord` → same `Session`, same `provideInfo`, same per-`(handle, id)` store instance. `Session.open()` is idempotent. There is no duplicate stream work today — but there is also no mechanism to *have* two different sessions, because there is one `BindingContext` value.

## 5. `ui-chat-sidebar` list actions

`ui-chat-sidebar` itself owns *no* list. `SidebarRoot.tsx:42-49` receives only `startSession` and `toggleSidebar` (contract `contract/slots.ts:92-101`), wired at `ui-chat-sidebar/src/client/index.ts:34-39`:
```ts
startSession: (workspaceId) =&gt; { ctx.workspaces.startSession(workspaceId) },
toggleSidebar: () =&gt; { ctx.layout.toggleSidebar() },
```
It declares five holes (`index.ts:47-53`); the browsing region `chat.sidebar.workspaces` (`scope: 'root'`) is filled by `ui-workspace`.

- **New Session button** — `SidebarRoot.tsx:179-188` (and the brand row at `:131-156`) → `startSession()` → `WorkspaceRuntime.startSession()` (`workspace-runtime/src/client/service.ts:181-196`): resolve target workspace (explicit → current session's workspace → `recentWorkspaceId`); with none, `this.sessions.clear()`; otherwise `connectWorkspace(target)` then `this.sessions.open(sessionId)`.
- **Blank-session creation path (client)** — `connectWorkspace` (`workspace-runtime/service.ts:~95-116`): scan `sessions.list` for an existing `blank &amp;&amp; cwd === workspace.path &amp;&amp; workspace.sessionIds.includes(id) &amp;&amp; !archived`; reuse it, else `this.sessions.create({ workspaceId })` → `SessionRuntime.create()` (`service.ts:485-490`) → `manager.create()` + a synchronous `projectList()` so the id is addressable before the promise resolves. Single-flight per workspace via `this.connecting`.
- **Blank-session creation path (host)** — the `session.create` RPC in `packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts`; the client holds no pre-entity session state (`session-runtime/README.md:5`).
- **Row click** — `ui-workspace/WorkspaceBrowser.tsx:519, 635, 713` pass `onOpen={open}`; `open` is injected at `ui-workspace/src/client/index.ts:77` as `ctx.sessions.open(sessionId)`. Row rename → `sessions.binding(id)?.session.rename` (`:83-87`); fork → `sessions.fork(...)` then `sessions.open(childId)` (`:89-93`); archive → `ctx.workspaces.archiveSession`.
- **Workspace switcher interplay** — group actions pass an explicit `workspaceId` into `startSession`; `ConversationRoot`'s hero picker routes through `ui-conversation/apply.ts:213-232` (`selectWorkspace`), which migrates the draft + image attachments into the new session's input shell, then `sessions.open(nextId)`. Archiving the current session clears it (`workspace-runtime/service.ts:342-344`).
- **No-session page** — `sessions.clear()` blanks `current`, wipes the persisted cell (`service.ts:720-722`); `chat.conversation` is `session-maybe` so `ConversationRoot` renders the hero (`ConversationRoot.tsx:79-81`); `chat.details` is strict so it renders its fallback and elects nothing (`scoped-slots.tsx:695-701`).
- **Deep links: none.** There is no session/window routing at all. The only URL parameters in the client are `?desktop=` (`packages/client/desktop-runtime/src/client/identity.ts:71`) and `?fixture` (`packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts:111`). Startup restore is entirely the persisted `dsh.sessions.current` cell plus `WorkspaceRuntime.startInitialSelection()` (`workspace-runtime/service.ts:126-164`, mounted at `workspace-runtime/src/client/index.ts:46`), which selects a default exactly once and defers to a restored `current`.

## 6. Lease / refcount precedents, and narrow mode

### Acquire/release precedents in the client runtime

1. **Slot store handle refcount** — `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:98` (`{ scope, refs, instances }`), `:377` `_acquire`, `:384` `_release`, `:445-461`. Registration-axis, not viewing: last unregister drops the record and its instances.
2. **Explicit open/close viewing flag** — `sessions.setSubagentCatalogOpen(parentSessionId, open)` (`contract/sessions.ts:52-57`, `service.ts:399-401`, `manager.ts:422-434`). This is the closest existing "a UI surface declares it is consuming live updates" lease: `openCatalogs` gates membership-frame refresh (`manager.ts:811`) and reconnect refresh (`manager.ts:907`); close clears the debounce timer. It is a boolean set, not a count — two menus on one parent would collide on close.
3. **Single-flight promise sharing** — `catalogInflight` (`manager.ts:348-350`), `listInflight` (`manager.ts:135`), `WorkspaceRuntime.connecting`, `DesktopRuntime.inflightResolve` (`desktop-runtime/src/client/service.ts:38-53`). Share-and-join, no counting.
4. **Idempotent open with generation fence** — `Session.open()` / `openGeneration` (`session.ts:369-378, 618-648`). An open is joinable by identity; a `resync` invalidates in-flight passes.
5. **Deferred teardown behind an occupant** — `deferredRemovals` + `sweepDeferred` (`service.ts:270, 769-790`). Structurally a 1-slot lease.
6. **Cordis fibers as the disposal unit** — `createScope` (`scope.ts:57-68`), `ctx.effect`, `slots.inject`. Every per-session resource already hangs off one fiber, so a lease release maps onto `fiber.dispose()`.

### Narrow-mode flag and the three-column layout

State lives in the Chat frame's own layout store, `packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/stores.ts:23`:
```ts
type LayoutState = { sidebar: number; details: number; narrow: boolean; narrowExpanded: boolean }
```
- `narrow` (`stores.ts:62-66`, `setNarrow`) mirrors the frame's breakpoint reading so `toggleSidebar` can pick semantics; crossing in either direction resets `narrowExpanded = false`.
- `narrowExpanded` (`stores.ts:56-60`) is the manual override — under narrow, `toggleSidebar` flips it instead of writing the width preference, so the wide preference survives.
- Store is registered exclusively on the `chat` Window entry (`ui-chat-surface/src/client/index.ts` `store: createLayoutStore`), so it is per-Window already.

The frame (`ChatSurface.tsx`):
- Tracks its **own box**, not the window: rAF-throttled `ResizeObserver` on `frameRef` (`:113-130`).
- `const narrow = viewport &lt; SIDEBAR_AUTO_COLLAPSE` (`:138`), where `SIDEBAR_AUTO_COLLAPSE = 1024` (`columns.ts:33`); `useEffect(() =&gt; actions.setNarrow(narrow))` (`:139`).
- `sidebarCollapsed = narrow ? !panels.narrowExpanded : panels.sidebar === 0` (`:140`) — narrow auto-collapses the sidebar to the 56px rail (`SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED`, `columns.ts:29`).
- Widths solved by `computeColumns(viewport, sidebarPreference, details)` (`columns.ts:62-71`), a breakpoint-free concession chain honoring `CENTER_MIN = 640`, `SIDEBAR_MIN/MAX = 264/420`, `DETAILS_MIN/MAX = 300/520`.
- Grid is a single row: `gridTemplateColumns: ${cols.sidebar}px minmax(0, 1fr) ${cols.details}px` (`:170`). Columns never unmount — details at width 0 keeps the subtree mounted (`ChatSurface.tsx:36`).
- Details width forced to 0 when `detailsSession === undefined` (`:144`), and `closeDetails()` fires on a session change (`:103-110`).

There is **no narrow-mode fallback at the Desktop level** — `DesktopFrame` (`ui-desktop/src/client/DesktopFrame.tsx:107-121`) draws every Window absolutely at `zIndex: record.zOrder` with `active: true` always (`ui-desktop/src/client/index.ts:78-84`: "Always true this release: `full` is the only placement").

---

### Two structural notes for Phase 3

- `desktop.window.surface` is declared `scope: 'root'` (`ui-desktop/src/client/index.ts:56-60`), and `ChatSurface` reads the session through `useSessions(s =&gt; s.current)` (`ChatSurface.tsx:96-97`) — its module doc states it plainly: *"It ignores its Window's owner share this release: a Chat Window carries no launch state, and the surface renders the globally selected Session exactly as before Windows existed."* The Host side matches: `CHAT_LAUNCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` with `defaultLaunchState: {}` (`packages/desktop/surface-chat/src/index.ts:24-48`), whose comment already anticipates real launch keys at a later version.
- `SessionRuntime`'s own module doc already names the widening: *"the window opens ⟺ the session is on stage (today the stage is `current`; the staged state can widen to a multi-pane list later)"* (`service.ts:11-13`).</result>
