## 3. Pointer drag/resize precedents

**`packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/ChatSurface.tsx` — `DragHandle` (`:42-86`)**
- `:50-57` `onPointerDown`: `preventDefault()`, `e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)`, record `origin.current = e.clientX`, call `onStart()`, `setDragging(true)`.
- `:58-65` `onPointerMove`: `:59` bails unless `e.currentTarget.hasPointerCapture(e.pointerId)`; `:61-65` `frame.current ??= requestAnimationFrame(...)` — one `onDrag(latest - origin)` per frame.
- `:66-73` `onPointerUp`: same capture guard, `releasePointerCapture`, `cancelAnimationFrame` any pending frame, **one final `onDrag(latest - origin)`**, then `setDragging(false)` and `onEnd()`.
- Commit semantics: **writes land continuously**, not at pointerup — `:159-164` `onSidebarDrag`/`onDetailsDrag` call `actions.setSidebar/​setDetails` directly on every rAF tick; `stores.ts:52-53` clamps into the contract range. `:151-158` the drag base is the **rendered** width captured at `onStart` (`colsRef.current.sidebar`), frozen for the gesture so deltas don't compound.
- `:76-84` markup: `className={css.handle}`, `style={{ left }}`, **`data-side={props.side}`** (`'sidebar'|'details'`), **`data-dragging={dragging || undefined}`**.
- `:196-197` placement — sidebar handle rendered only when `!sidebarCollapsed`, details handle only when `cols.details &gt; 0`.
- `ChatSurface.module.css:54-66` `.handle` (8px strip, `margin-left:-4px`, `cursor: col-resize`, `z-index: 2`, `touch-action: none`); `:68-70` `.frame[data-dragging] .handle { transition: none }`; `:15-17` same for the grid tracks; `:19-23`/`:72-76` `prefers-reduced-motion` guards; `:78-108` details-only `::after` pill with hover reveal.
- Solver: `columns.ts:62-77` `computeColumns(viewport, sidebar, details)` — pure, no hysteresis, three-step concession chain; constants at `:21-39`.

**Other pointer-capture usage** (only two other packages): `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTimeline.tsx:435-436` and `:451-452` (guarded by `typeof … === 'function'`, dual right-button pan + left-button range drag, `dragRef`/`panRef`, `MINIMUM_DRAG_PX` threshold, commit via `onRangeChange`); `TrajectoryTable.tsx:2566`/`:2585` (column resize). CSS `touch-action: none` also at `TrajectoryTimeline.module.css:57`, `TrajectoryTable.module.css:888`.

**rAF batching in the store engine** — `packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/store.ts:54-71` `rafBatch()` (falls back to `queueMicrotask` where rAF is absent); `:86-117` `createSnapshotStore(init, { flush?: 'raf'|'sync', persist? })`, `:95-103` the raf-mode fan-out. **Default is `'sync'`, and `defineStore` (`:205-240`) never passes `flush`** — so every slot store, including the layout store, notifies synchronously; the rAF throttle in `DragHandle` is hand-rolled at the component.

**The `handles.expected.md` golden** — `apps/web/tests/snapshots/details-session-lifecycle/handles.expected.md` (7 lines) captures a single section, `## sidebar`, with `hit strip present: true`, `cursor: col-resize`, `pill generated: false`. Generator: `apps/web/tests/details-session-lifecycle.e2e.ts:46-65` `handleSnapshot()` — queries `[class*="handle"]`, emits `data-side`, computed `cursor`, and whether `getComputedStyle(el,'::after').content !== 'none'`; deliberately platform-coordinate-free. Only the sidebar handle appears because details is closed (`detailsTrack === 0`) at capture time. The e2e drives a real drag at `:104-113` via `page.locator('[data-side="sidebar"]')` + `mouse.down/move(+70, {steps:6})/up`, then asserts `sidebarTrack === sidebarBefore + 70`. `:150` `assertFixtureInventory(SNAPSHOT_DIR, ['handles.expected.md'])` pins the snapshot directory contents.

## 6. Narrow viewport

- Store: `packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/stores.ts:16-23` — `narrow` "mirrors ChatSurface's breakpoint reading"; `narrowExpanded` is the manual re-expand override. `:56-59` `toggleSidebar` flips `narrowExpanded` when `narrow`, else flips the width preference; `:62-66` `setNarrow` is a no-op on equal value and **drops the override on every crossing**.
- Who sets it: `ChatSurface.tsx:113-130` — a **`ResizeObserver` on the frame's own box** (`frameRef`), rAF-throttled, `setViewport(width)` when `&gt; 0`; **not** a media query and not `window.resize`. Initial value is `useState(() =&gt; window.innerWidth)` at `:101`. `:138-139` `const narrow = viewport &lt; SIDEBAR_AUTO_COLLAPSE` then `useEffect(() =&gt; { actions.setNarrow(narrow) }, [actions, narrow])`.
- Breakpoint: `columns.ts:30-33` `SIDEBAR_AUTO_COLLAPSE = 1024` (deepsuite LG); `:29` `SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED = 56`. The solver itself is breakpoint-free (`:10-13`).
- Visual result: `ChatSurface.tsx:140-144` `sidebarCollapsed = narrow ? !panels.narrowExpanded : panels.sidebar === 0`; the effective preference passed to `computeColumns` is `0` (rail) or the stored width, or `SIDEBAR_DEFAULT` when the wide preference was closed. `:171-173` sets `data-sidebar-collapsed`, `data-details-collapsed`, `data-dragging` on the frame; `:196` **no sidebar drag handle while collapsed**. The sidebar occupant re-renders as a rail via the owner share (`collapsed`, `width`) — `ui-chat-sidebar/SidebarRoot.tsx:27` `COLLAPSE_SETTLE_MS = 150` crossfade, wide content unmounts at settle.

`packages/client/runtime/src/client/index.ts` — exact current shape:

- `:78-110` the gate:
  ```
  ctx.inject(['sessions', 'workspaces'], () =&gt; {
    loop ??= connection.start({
      onMuxEnvelope: …  sessions()?.handleMuxEnvelope(envelope)
      onHostEnvelope: …  sessions()?.handleHostEnvelope(); workspaces()?.handleHostEnvelope();
                         if (frame.type === 'host/remote-event') ctx.remote.$dispatch(frame.event, frame.args)
      onConnected: …     sessions()?.handleConnected(); workspaces()?.handleConnected(); ctx.emit('connection/reset')
      onStateChange: …   if (state === 'reconnecting') sessions()?.handleDisconnected()
    })
  })
  ```

## Lease semantics as built

`ISessions.acquireView(sessionId): () =&gt; void` in `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts`:

- **State**: one `viewHolds: Map&lt;SessionId, number&gt;` where *an entry exists ⟺ the session is STAGED*, and the value counts live holds. A **zero value is the release grace**. Plus `releaseTimers: Map&lt;SessionId, Timeout&gt;`.
- **Acquire**: rejects unless `addressable(id)` (host-listed, or a durable child whose address `configureSubagentView` retained) — fail-loud like `open()` was. Cancels any pending sweep, increments; on the 0→1 edge `stageView` resolves the scope, `session.open()` (idempotent), `refreshSubagents(id)`, and `manager.stage(id)` which consumes the completion reminder. Further leases share that one staged session — no second `session.history`.
- **Release**: the returned disposer latches (repeat calls release once). Above 1 it decrements; the last one sets the count to 0 and schedules `setTimeout(sweep)` — a **macrotask grace**. Re-acquire inside the grace clears the timer and re-enters `stageView`, which no-ops on the already-open window. This is what makes StrictMode acquire/release/acquire and A-closes-while-B-opens handoffs leave the scope untouched.
- **Sweep**: deletes the entry, `manager.unstage(id)`, then `pruneScopes()`.
- **Eligibility**: `eligible = viewHolds.has(id) || ids.includes(id)` — the exact structural mirror of the old `current === id || ids.includes(id)`. So a session that leaves the list while staged keeps its scope frozen until its last lease releases (D1's "still tears down immediately via pruneScopes", preserving today's staged-defers rule). `deferredRemovals`/`sweepDeferred` are **deleted as redundant** — `pruneScopes` at every projection and every sweep covers them.
- Manager: `selected` → a `staged` Set driving completion reminders (`!staged.has(id)`), the session-added catalog refresh, and `handleConnected` (now iterates the staged set). `SessionListSnapshot`/`SessionListState` lost `current`/`currentAddress`; breadcrumb ancestor rows are now projected per staged addressed child.

1. `configureSubagentView(parentSessionId, address)` takes a **required** address — the `| undefined` arm has no expressible target (there is no child id to clear) and no caller, so it would be uncovered fiction.
2. `workspace-runtime.startSession()` returns `Promise&lt;SessionId | undefined&gt;`, not `Promise&lt;SessionId&gt;` — `undefined` is the real "no Workspace exists to start one in" state that previously called `sessions.clear()`. ## (A) Session-maybe adoption path

Both branches (`empty()` and `children(id)`) sit *inside* the keyed element, so a change from `undefined` to a real id changes the key from `''` to `'s1'` and React unmounts + remounts everything below.
- The only production dispatch of the `session-maybe` `chat.conversation` slot is `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/ChatSurface.tsx:355-357` — `&lt;SessionProvider info={info} empty={() =&gt; sessionColumns}&gt;{() =&gt; sessionColumns}&lt;/SessionProvider&gt;`. The *same* `sessionColumns` element tree is used in both branches, i.e. without the key nothing would remount; the key is the sole cause.
- Contracts now false: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/ConversationRoot.tsx:1-3` ("Hero chrome, composer positioning, the chain, AND the composer bar (session-maybe slot) stay mounted across no-session/session transitions"); `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/ConversationRoot.tsx:133-135` ("inert is a prop, not a different tree, so the textarea DOM survives the transition"); `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/slot-catalog.ts:87` and `:350` (same claim in the generated catalog).
- Before this diff the bundle came from a *keyless* root provider — `git show c94893a031:packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/session-provider.tsx` had `SessionMaybeProvider` wrapping the tree with no key at all, and `SessionProvider` used `key={id}` only on the branch where `id` was already defined (`if (id === undefined) return &lt;&gt;{empty?.()}&lt;/&gt;` before the provider).

Failure scenario: unbound Window shows the hero. User picks a workspace → `selectWorkspace()` resolves a blank session → `chatWindow.bind(connectedId)` → `boundSessionId` goes `undefined → S` → `info.sessionId` goes `undefined → S` → key flips `'' → 'S'` → the center and details columns are torn down and rebuilt. `ConversationRoot`'s local `pendingWorkspaceId` and `pickerOpen` (`ConversationRoot.tsx:30-31`) are discarded, so the optimistic workspace chip reverts to the "Choose workspace" placeholder and the hero flashes at the single most common transition in the app.

## (B) Deleted deferred sweep

Old code for reference: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-repos-deepseek-harness/2821d33d-4056-4b0b-a667-30e526437804/scratchpad/old-service.ts` (from `git show c94893a031:…/service.ts`).

- **(iii) Ordering between list projection and scope disposal.** Old and new both call `pruneScopes()` *after* `this.list.set(...)` (`service.ts:736-737`), so the snapshot React reads never advertises a session whose scope was already dropped in that pass. Preserved.
- **(ii) Synchronous teardown inside a store notification.** Old code did exactly that: `this.list.subscribe(() =&gt; { this.followCurrent(); … })` ran `sweepDeferred()` → `dropScope()` synchronously inside the list notify. That subscription is **deleted**; staging now runs from `acquireView` (a React effect) and teardown from a `setTimeout` macrotask. This is an improvement, not a regression.

**4. MAJOR — Scope disposal now publishes nothing, so a surface still holding the bundle is never told its scope died.**

Evidence: `sweepView` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:633-638`) calls `manager.unstage()` → `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/manager.ts:201-203`, which only does `this.staged.delete(sessionId)` — **no `notifyNow()`**, unlike its twin `stage()` at `manager.ts:190-194` which does call `notifyNow()`. Then `pruneScopes()` → `dropScope()` → `manager.drop()` (`manager.ts:259-261`), which only does `this.sessions.delete(sessionId)` — also no notification. In the old design the equivalent teardown ran inside the `list.subscribe` notify, so React was re-rendered by the very notification that carried it.

Failure scenario: a Window bound to session S; S is deleted host-side. `boundListed` flips false, the lease effect cleanup releases (`ChatSurface.tsx:218-227`), the macrotask sweep disposes S's scope fiber and its Session instance. No store notification fires. The Window is still rendering `info = provideInfo(boundSessionId)` (`ChatSurface.tsx:254`) from the *previous* render's bundle, now backed by a disposed fiber, and only recovers when the async "unbind on removal" desktop mutation (`ChatSurface.tsx:231-237`) round-trips through the host and republishes launch state. Until then the column renders against a dead scope.

Remedy: make `unstage()` symmetric with `stage()` (call `this.notifier.notifyNow()`), or have `sweepView` re-project the list after `pruneScopes()`.

**5. MAJOR — Stale breadcrumb rows survive their last viewer, because the projection that produces them is only driven by manager notifications and the sweep raises none.**

Evidence: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:707-734` derives breadcrumb `byId` rows by iterating `this.viewHolds.keys()`. `sweepView` (`service.ts:633-638`) deletes the hold but, per finding 4, triggers no re-projection. Same root cause, distinct symptom: an addressed subagent child keeps a list row after its last viewer let go, until some unrelated manager notify happens. It also means rows are contributed for grace-period (0-count) holds.

Remedy: same as finding 4.

**6. MAJOR — `acquireView` throws for unknown ids and is called from a React passive effect, turning a benign concurrent delete into an unmount.**

Evidence: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/session-runtime/src/client/service.ts:339-341` throws when `!addressable()`; `addressable()` (`service.ts:673-675`) reads the **live** `this.list.getSnapshot().ids`. ## (D) Cross-desktop privacy

**12. MAJOR (BLOCKER if a per-desktop boundary is intended) — `resolve()` serves any stored Desktop to any caller, and `desktop/changed` broadcasts every Desktop's id to every browser, so slimming the payload moved the leak one RPC hop instead of closing it.**

Evidence:

The request type carries only an optional id: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/desktop/desktop/src/types.ts:154-156`.
- The returned `DesktopSnapshot` carries the contents in question: `windows[].launchState` (which is where session ids live), `focusedWindowId`, bounds, modes — `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/desktop/desktop/src/types.ts:83-146`.
- Every desktop id is broadcast to every browser: `desktop/changed` is in `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts:27`), and the client acknowledges it: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/desktop-runtime/src/client/service.ts:144-145` — "Changes to another browser's Desktop reach this client too and are dropped." The type's own JSDoc states it: `types.ts:282-283`, "every browser sees every Desktop's ids and revisions and nothing else."
- The id is the only thing separating desktops, and it is attacker-supplyable from the URL: `/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/client/desktop-runtime/src/client/identity.ts:26-31` — `readDesktopId()` prefers `readLocationDesktopId()` over `sessionStorage`.

Failure scenario: browser B observes `desktop/changed { desktopId: D_A, revision }` for another browser's Desktop, then loads the app with `D_A` in the location (or calls `remote.resolve({ desktopId: D_A })` directly) and receives A's complete window list — every open session id, launch state, mode, and which window A is focused on.

**Second, independent content-carrying path — MAJOR:** the mutation results also return full aggregates with no ownership check. `DesktopMutationResult` is `{ status: 'conflict'; snapshot: DesktopSnapshot }` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/desktop/desktop/src/types.ts:268-271`), and `focusWindow`/`updateWindow`/`closeWindow`/`openWindow` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/desktop/desktop/src/index.ts:166-217`) accept any `desktopId`. A caller can send a deliberately-stale `expectedRevision` against a foreign desktop and read its whole aggregate back through the conflict branch — and, with a correct revision, *mutate* another desktop's windows.

**Killed candidates:** `listSurfaces` (`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/packages/desktop/desktop-domain/src/index.ts:243-245`) returns only the registered `SurfaceDescriptor` set — composition-global, no per-desktop content. `desktop/surfaces-changed` carries only `{ surfaceId, change }` (`types.ts:300-303`). Rejection messages name only the surface id and the request's own inputs (e.g. `index.ts:251-254`), never another desktop's contents. The `desktop/changed` payload itself is genuinely slimmed to `{ desktopId, revision }` (`types.ts:287-290`, emitted at `desktop-domain/src/index.ts:549-552`) — its residual leak is metadata (existence, id, and activity rate of other desktops), not contents.

Remedy: bind Desktop ownership to a caller identity (the anonymous identity/connection already exists) and reject `resolve` and every mutation for a Desktop the caller does not own; until then, do not forward `desktop/changed` for Desktops the receiving connection does not hold.</result>

**Output declaration**: `output: { schema, render }` — `:409-425`, `:472-488`, `:529-559` (the last uses a `oneOf` of two closed objects discriminated by a `const` `scope`). `render: (_args, value) =&gt; [{ type: 'text', text: ... }]` is a pure projection; the prose builders are separate module functions: `:209-213 renderDispatchState`, `:222-231 renderRules`, `:239-246 renderRuns`, `:253-257 renderAutomationState`. Record→listing projections: `:173-184 listedRule`, `:191-201 listedRun` (a zero-valued diagnostic counter is omitted rather than emitted).

**Render intent declaration**: all three tools return the *generic* card, via one shared helper — `:265-267`:
```ts
function presentAutomationCall(title: string, rawInput?: unknown): GenericCallView {
  return { card: 'generic', title, kind: 'other', ...rawInput === undefined ? {} : { rawInput } }
}
```
`presentCall` at `:452`, `:508`, `:580-585`. No `presentResult`, no `presentationMeta`, no `locations` — the tools touch no file. Per `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:71-90` the three call cards are `generic` (with optional `kind` icon and `locations: [{ path, line? }]`), `terminal` (tool-bash), and `diff` (tool-fs write/edit); result cards add `search`, `read`, `web`. The hard rules at `:86-88`: **purity** (presenters run on live streaming *and* session-log replay — no I/O, no session state, no clock/random), **UI-only formatting stays out of the model result**, and `defineTool` soft-validates the display path so malformed older logged args return `undefined` (generic fallback) instead of crashing replay. `locations` is what a capable editor follows — a desktop/notes tool has no file path, so `generic` is the correct card, matching automation.

**Presentation as a pure function of args** is directly asserted: `tests/tool-automation.spec.ts:513-520` and `:600-613` call `ctx.tools.get('automation_list')?.presentCall?.({...})` and compare the exact object.

**Config bounds pattern**: `src/index.ts:24-41`
```ts
export interface Config { maxListedRules?: number; maxListedRuns?: number }
export const Config: z&lt;Config&gt; = z.object({
  maxListedRules: z.number().step(1).min(1).default(20),
  maxListedRuns: z.number().step(1).min(1).default(20),
})
```
Each field carries a JSDoc justifying the number ("Twenty rules fit a listing the model can act on without spending a turn's context on inventory"). Enforcement is on the **emitted array**, not on the service call — `:495` and `:501`: `Math.min(requested ?? maxRules, maxRules)`, then `.slice(0, ruleLimit)` *after* the registry call, with the comment "a registry that ignores `limit` cannot widen a listing past its configured cap". Tests: `:233-237` (defaults + rejection of `0` / `1.5`), `:239-246` (a row configuring nothing still gets 20), `:496-511` (larger request reduced, smaller honored).

**Invariant companion** (`src/invariant.ts`, mandatory per `packages/CLAUDE.md`): `:6` `/* jscpd:ignore-start */`, `:10 PACKAGE_NAME`, `:13` `export const name = 'tool-automation-invariant'`, `:15` `export const inject = ['invariants']`, `:17-24` an empty installer whose JSDoc **must** start with `No runtime invariant:` and give a package-specific reason ("this package is a model-facing adapter over `ctx.automations`… the rule-to-run relation belongs to the companion in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-automation`"), `:31-32` `apply` returning `ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install)`. Gate: `scripts/verify-package-invariants.ts` → `scripts/package-invariants.ts:38` globs `packages/*/*/package.json`, `:50` requires `src/invariant.ts`, `:85-92` requires `exports["./invariant"]` → `./lib/types/invariant.d.ts` + `./lib/invariant.js`.

**package.json** invariants (`packages/automation/tool-automation/package.json`): `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` in `dependencies`; `dsh-agent`, `dsh-automation`, `dsh-invariants`, `dsh-session`, `dsh-tools`, `cordis` in **both** `peerDependencies` and `devDependencies` (plus `dsh-llm`, `dsh-system-prompt` dev-only for tests); `files: ["lib/index.js", "lib/invariant.js", "lib/types/**/*.d.ts"]`; `exports` for `.`, `./invariant`, `./src/*`, `./package.json`. `version` must match the root `package.json` (`scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts`).

**tsconfig.json**: `extends ../../../tsconfig.base.json`, `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, `references` = `vendor/cosmokit`, `vendor/cordis`, `vendor/schemastery`, `../automation`, `../../core/agent`, `../../core/session`, `../../core/tools`, `../../runtime-diagnostics/invariants`.

**Tests** (`tests/tool-automation.spec.ts`, 633 lines):
- `:26-95` a `StubAutomationRegistry extends AutomationRegistry` implementing the Service-Definition semantics (provenance, revision bump, contributed-rule refusal, most-recent-first `listRuns`), documented at `:18-25`.
- `:124-131 setup()` composes `SystemPrompt` → `ToolRuntime` → stub registry → the tool plugin on a bare `new Context()`.
- `:139-148 call()` drives the **real** `ctx.tools.execute({ signal, callId, name, arguments, agent? })`, never the raw `execute` callback.
- `:150-157` `text()` / `value()` helpers over `ToolExecutionResult`.
- Coverage classes: exact tool-name list + fiber disposal (`:200-211`), model-visible description text pinned verbatim (`:213-218`), required-key shape of the generated parameters (`:220-231`), Config defaults (`:233-246`), value + rendered text + committed record per tool, owner attribution (`:274-284`), every error path asserting `isError` plus message substring, `presentCall` purity, and the HMR/disposal proof for contributed rules at `:620-633`.
- The **non-unit REAL-composition** requirement (`packages/CLAUDE.md`) is satisfied by the headless keyless snapshot, not this file (see §3).

**Every mechanical registration a new tool package needs:**

**README Model Experience — tool-automation's exact structure** (`packages/automation/tool-automation/README.md:22-50`). The verifier (`scripts/verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts:13-18`) requires exactly `## Model Experience`, then one H3 per model-context entry, each with the three ordered H4s `#### What the model sees`, `#### Token effect`, `#### KV Cache effect`, one prose paragraph each, blank lines between, and no cross-links between local subsections (`:505`); `:533` requires at least one entry grounded by inline code, a nested ```` ```markdown ```` block, or an **anchored tool-catalog link** whose fragment must exist in `docs/tool-catalog.md` (`:254-263`). tool-automation's two entries:

- `### Tool schemas` → *What the model sees*: "The generated [`automation_create_rule`, `automation_list`, and `automation_set_enabled` schemas](../../../docs/tool-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-tool-automation) while this tool set is visible." → *Token effect*: "Fixed schema cost on each request where the tools are visible." → *KV Cache effect*: "Prefix-stable while tool definitions and visibility are unchanged. Registration lifecycle or scoped restrictions may invalidate reuse from the first changed schema token."
- `### Results` → *What the model sees* quotes the exact acknowledgement strings and both empty-listing sentinels and states that invalid input returns an `isError` result quoting the zod issue path → *Token effect*: "Results remain in history until compaction; listings are bounded by `maxListedRules` and `maxListedRuns` after any model-supplied `limit`." → *KV Cache effect*: "Append-only; newly visible content follows the reusable request prefix and does not invalidate existing KV-cache entries."

Then `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work` (`:52-56`) with three bolded gaps (edit-by-replacement, no pagination beyond caps, no delete tool + why). Preceding sections: a one-paragraph intro naming the seam and stating what it does *not* do ("registers no prompt section and appends no session events of its own"), a `## Tools` bullet per tool with its signature and result grammar, and a `## Config` table (`key | default | meaning`). Canonical format spec: `docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:73-107`.

**Translation pairing**: `README.zh.md` plus `README.i18n.yaml` recording both git blob hashes; re-record with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write &lt;path&gt;`. Full doc-sync gate list at `scripts/run-gates.ts:651-685`.

## 2. Runtime flow of a tool call

**Registry → prompt.** `ToolRuntime`'s constructor wires the assembly once: `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:832` — `ctx.systemPrompt.tools(context =&gt; this.wireSchemas(context.scope))`. Schemas flow in automatically; nothing per-tool is registered with the prompt. `schemas(scope?)` whitelists only name/description/parameters (`:251`). Under `mode: code`/`both` the constructor also adds `tools:code-only` and `tools:sdk` sections (`:833-836`), so a new tool is reachable as `await tools.&lt;name&gt;(args)` for free (`docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:61-65`).

**Execution waterfall.** `ctx.tools.execute(exec)` → lossless-snapshot + freeze `arguments`, mint an opaque `exec.token` → `tools/pre-execute` waterfall (`:1476`) → `ask` resolution through the approval seam (`:1679-1726`) → monotonic `ctx.tools.guard()` denials → `tools/execute` around-wrapper → the definition's `execute(args, exec)` → `tools/post-execute` → definition-owned `finalizeContent` → observe-only `tools/result`. The generated diagram is `docs/tool-execution-pipeline.md`. The durable `tool/call` event is logged *before* execution and `tool/result` *after*; `tools/result` (live) and `tool/result` (durable) are distinct (`packages/core/tools/README.md:37-39`).

**Approvals / permission.** The registry consumes the approval seam **opportunistically** — `ctx.get('approval')`, no static inject (`packages/core/tools/README.md:31`, code at `:1693-1697`): absent approval turns `ask` into deny with `tool "&lt;name&gt;" requires approval (not yet supported)`; an `ask` with no `exec.agent` denies at `:1702`. What *decides* a tool needs approval is a `tools/pre-execute` listener returning `{ kind: 'ask' }` — the only shipped producers are the hook bridges (`packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:242`, `packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:225`) and the sandbox escalation closure (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:12`). **No `tool-*` package declares approval rows, and `tool-automation` needs none**: the permission plugin's config selects *sandbox mode + approval policy* bundles, not per-tool gates. `packages/interaction/permission-presets/README.md:5-9` — each preset name bundles `sandbox/mode` with `approval/policy`; `custom` is derived-only.

**Where those rows live.** `packages/bundle/agent-standard/cordis.patch.yml:30-46` inserts `approval` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval`, policy `ask` unless `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access`) and `permission` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets` with the `read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access` table) in the *same insert* as the tool rows. `packages/bundle/app-chat/cordis.patch.yml` disables ~23 of agent-standard's **tool** rows (`:156-272`) so the per-session preset owns them, but leaves `approval` and `permission` untouched — they stay host-plane.

**What a tool returns.** `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:556-580`:
```ts
ToolExecutionSuccess { isError: false; value: JsonValue; content: ContentBlock[]; meta?; additionalContexts?; concludesTurn? }
ToolExecutionFailure { isError: true;  error: ToolFailure;  content: ContentBlock[]; meta?; additionalContexts? }
```
`execute` returns **only** the canonical JSON value declared by `output.schema`; the registry snapshots it as lossless JSON (`:544-553`), validates, freezes, and hands it to `output.render(args, value)`. Throwing, or returning a value that fails the schema/renderer/metadata projector, becomes `isError` (`docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:46`). Wire form (from the recorded transcript): `{"type":"tool-result","toolCallId":"…","content":[{"type":"text","text":"…"}],"isError":false}`.

**Bounded-output conventions.** Three layers exist and a Notes/desktop tool should pick from them: (a) tool-owned Config caps applied to the emitted array (tool-automation `maxListed*`); (b) `finalizeContent` byte trimming against a deployment limit — `packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:185,233-256` caches `visibleOutputLimit(ctx, exec)` in a `tools/pre-execute` prepend listener and trims in `finalizeContent`; (c) the optional `ctx.spillStore` backend for capped results with a follow-up-readable locator (tool-fs-search). `packages/CLAUDE.md`: "Apply bounds to the complete result… test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits."

## 3. The keyless snapshot anatomy for a tool package

Five files plus one test block:

1. **`examples/headless-agent/automation.cordis.yml`** — the *runnable* overlay. `cordis-plugin-include` over `./cordis.yml` with one `insert` list: `storage`, `storage-json` (root `./.storage`), `storage-domain` (backend json), `agent-default-model` (needed because a `start` rule has no session-specific model selection), `automation-domain`, `tool-automation` (`:29`). **Yes — the example lane must mount the tool's backing service.** A `notes.cordis.yml` mirrors this with `storage*` + `note-domain` + `tool-note`; a desktop one with `desktop-domain` + `tool-desktop` (and, for a launchable Surface, a `SurfaceDefinition` row — `surface-chat` is the precedent, `packages/bundle/app-chat/cordis.patch.yml:41-44`).

2. **`examples/headless-agent/automation.cordis.snapshot.yml`** — the replay twin. It re-includes `./cordis.yml` directly (header comment `:1-4`: "a config patch cannot target an entry behind a nested include"), disables `llm-deepseek` (`:8-10`), restates the whole overlay, and appends `llm-replay` (`:33-34`) plus the fence plugin as a top-level row (`:39-40`, `name: './tests/fixtures/automation-dispatch-fence.ts'`).

3. **`examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/automation-rule/`** — four files, **no `session.jsonl`**:
   - `input.json` — `{ "steps": [{ "op": "prompt", "text": "…" }] }`; read by `scenarioPrompt()` (`headless.snapshot.ts:207-214`) so the spec and fixture cannot drift.
   - `replay.override.json` — a **bare `ReplayEntry[]`**, i.e. a whole-script replacement, so `deriveScriptFromFile` is never reached and the missing `session.jsonl` is fine (`packages/test-support/llm-replay/src/index.ts:509-531`). Three entries, one per model call: (1) `block-start`/`tool-call-delta`/`block-end` for `automation_create_rule` with the full JSON argument string, `usage`, `finish {kind:'tool-calls'}`; (2) the same shape for `todo_write`; (3) a text block `"AUTOMATION RULE READY"` with `finish {kind:'stop'}`. **This is how a replayed model emits a tool call** — the `tool-call` block's `id` (`call_automation_create`) is what assertions correlate on.
   - `session.1.jsonl` — the **child** script for the session the rule *starts*, supplied via `DSH_SNAPSHOT_CHILD_FILES` (the primary sidecar replaces only the primary script).
   - `stream-json.expected.jsonl` — the pinned transcript: every `session_event` record plus a terminal `result` record, normalized with `{{sessionId}}`/`{{cwd}}`/`{{system}}`/`{{tools}}` tokens. This is where the model-visible result text is pinned verbatim (`"Created automation rule rule-{{sessionId}}: \"review finished todo work\" acts on tools/result and is on now (revision 0)."`).

4. **The block in `examples/headless-agent/tests/headless.snapshot.ts:810-899`** — `it('starts an automation session from a matched tool result')`. Consts at `:35-36`. It calls `runLoaderSmoke({ label, tempDirPrefix, binScript, libBinScript, configPath, binArgs: [configPath, prompt], tsconfigPath, env: { DSH_SNAPSHOT: 'replay', DSH_SNAPSHOT_FILE, DSH_SNAPSHOT_OVERRIDE, DSH_SNAPSHOT_CHILD_FILES, NODE_OPTIONS }, prepare, inspect })`. The `inspect` callback (`:833-893`) reads persisted logs and asserts: both sessions persisted with the same cwd (`:834-841`); the ordered `tool/call` names `['automation_create_rule','todo_write']` (`:844-846`); the create result located by `message.source.callId` (`:847-856`); the started session's trigger `user/message` source `{ kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'automation', form: 'notice' }` and its text shape (`:858-865`); and the **durable domain file** `.storage/automation.json` — rule fields, owner `{ kind:'agent', sessionId: prompted.header.id }`, and one run with `outcome: 'completed'` (`:870-891`). Finally `:895-899` normalizes stdout and compares against `stream-json.expected.jsonl`, writing it back under `DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh`.

5. **The fence fixture** — `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/automation-dispatch-fence.ts`. Loader plugin, `inject = ['automations']`, registered in `knip.json:42` as an entry. It listens on `tools/result` to capture the triggering agent id, on `domain/changed` to detect a non-`started` run outcome, and wraps `agent/pre-step` to hold the triggering agent until the caused run settles. Its JSDoc is explicit that it pins **process lifetime, not dispatch behavior**. A Notes/desktop scenario whose tool call is synchronous within one turn needs no fence; one that starts a second agent does.

Runner: `pnpm run test:snapshot` (`vitest.snapshot.config.ts:47-54` includes `examples/*/tests/**/*.snapshot.ts`), refresh with `test:snapshot:refresh`.

## 4. Driving a REAL tool call through the web UI replay lane

`/Users/ren/repos/deepseek-harness/apps/web/tests/cordis-tool-round.e2e.ts` (185 lines) is the model-authored probe. Anatomy:

- **Fixture**: `apps/web/tests/snapshots/cordis-tool-round/session.jsonl` + `ui.expected.md` (`:23-24`). Unlike the headless lane this is a **real recorded session log**, not an override sidecar; `installLlmReplay` derives the script from it (`scaffold.ts:631-641`).
- **Scaffold**: `launchWebScaffold({ cordisTools: true, ...(MODE === 'record' ? {} : { replayFixture: FIXTURE, paceMs: 15 }) })` (`:74-77`). `cordisTools: true` is a bespoke patch at `scaffold.ts:525-529` inserting `{ id: 'tool-cordis', name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-cordis' }` into the shipped tree — a Phase-4 e2e needs the equivalent flag (or an `extraOverlayPath` overlay, `scaffold.ts:212-217`, the pattern used by `goal-bar.overlay.yml` / `desktop-recovery.overlay.yml`).
- **Fixture↔script coupling**: `:95` asserts `fixtureUserPrompts(await readFile(FIXTURE,'utf8'))` equals the exact prompts the spec types, so the drive script cannot drift from the recording (`scaffold.ts:762-768`).
- **Drive**: fill the `textarea`, press Enter, await `scaffold.whenTurnSettled()` (`:97-101`), which resolves on the in-process `turn/end` after `ctx.sessions.flush(session)` (`scaffold.ts:676-695`).
- **Real execution under replay**: `:1-10` states the contract — *the fixture pins only what the MODEL said; the tools execute for real*. The approval is the test's own click (`:105-115`), and the DOM probe `[data-snapshot-probe]` is asserted absent before and present after (`:110`, `:116`), proving the side effect really happened. This is exactly the lever a Phase-4 e2e needs: the Notes window can be asserted to show the **committed revision** the tool actually wrote.
- **Durable-log assertions**: `assertCompleteCordisLifecycle` (`:45-64`) filters the harvested `SessionEvent[]` (collected via `scaffold.ctx.on('session/event', …)` at `:78`) for `turn/end` reason `{kind:'completed'}`, the exact ordered `tool/call` names, and one non-`isError` `tool/result` per `callId`.
- **UI-tool card assertions** (`:137-167`): rows are located by `page.locator('[data-tool="&lt;tool_name&gt;"]')` — emitted by `packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/components/ToolRow.tsx:195` as `data-variant` / `data-tool` / `data-state`. A tool with **no** keyed toolview renders the generic card whose accessible name is `Tool call &lt;name&gt; · &lt;args&gt;` (see `ui.expected.md` line for `cordis_inspect_self`); a package that registers a keyed toolview replaces it (`:145-148`). `data-state` is asserted `'ok'` at `:164`. The whole row is the expand toggle: `row.locator('[aria-expanded]').first().click()` (`:152`).
- **Aria golden**: `captureStableAria(page, '[class*="centerCol"]', scaffold.workspaceCwd)` + `compareOrRefreshGolden(UI_EXPECTED, snapshot, MODE)` (`:169-179`).
- **Cleanliness**: `watchConsole(page)` tripwire asserting zero `pageErrors`/`warnings` (`:181-184`); teardown asserts the replay fixture was fully consumed (`scaffold.ts:702-708`).

Config: `vitest.web.config.ts:26-27` includes `apps/web/tests/**/*.e2e.ts`; run with `pnpm run test:web` (builds first) or `test:web:refresh`. Window-level helpers for the desktop half live in `apps/web/tests/desktop-windows.ts` (`WINDOW`, `TASKBAR`, `openWindowFromLauncher`, `desktopRecord(scaffold, page)` returning the host `DesktopSnapshot`, `boundSessions`).

## 5. Tool naming conventions and multi-action modeling

**Verb placement.** Two families coexist; the newer, subsystem-owned packages use `&lt;singular_subsystem&gt;_&lt;verb&gt;`:

- `automation_create_rule`, `automation_list`, `automation_set_enabled`
- `schedule_create`, `schedule_delete`, `schedule_list`
- `terminal_open`, `terminal_close`, `terminal_list`, `terminal_read`, `terminal_send`, `terminal_signal`
- `job_kill`, `job_list`, `job_output` — **singular** `job_`, though the package is `tool-jobs` and the service is `ctx.jobs`
- `session_search`, `session_trace`, `session_event_read`, `session_event_search`, `session_event_trace`
- `team_task_create`, `team_task_get`, `team_task_list`, `team_task_update`
- `cordis_define`, `cordis_undefine`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, `cordis_inspect_self`, `cordis_inspect_list`, `cordis_inspect_query`
- `todo_write`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `read_image`

The older verb-first names are `create_goal`, `get_goal`, `update_goal`, `list_agents`, `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, `wait_agent`, `spawn_teammate`, `exit_plan_mode`, `ask_user_question`, `run_code`. Bare single-tool names carry no prefix: `bash`, `pwsh`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `lsp`, `skill`, `subagent`, `workflow`, `ralph`, `report`, `str_replace_editor`. **Plural prefixes are never used.** Full inventory: `docs/tool-catalog.md:18-44`.

**Parameter case.** Top-level model-facing parameters are `snake_case` (`rule_id`, `include_runs`, `kill_switch`, `run_in_background`, `file_path`, `session_id`), while nested objects that mirror a durable record keep the record's `camelCase` (`target.presetId`, `target.sessionId`, `budget.maxTurns`, `rateLimit.maxPerMinute`, `causal.agentEvents`) — `packages/automation/tool-automation/README.md:9` says this is deliberate: "mirrors the `AutomationRuleInput` record field-for-field (camelCase), so a zod rejection quotes the exact parameter path the model supplied."

**Multi-action modeling — both patterns ship, chosen by whether the actions share a subject and argument shape.**
- *Single tool + action enum*: `lsp` with `operation: enum['goToDefinition','findReferences','goToImplementation','hover']` over one identical `(file_path, line, character)` cursor (`docs/tool-catalog.md:1166+`); `str_replace_editor` with `command: enum['view','create','str_replace','insert']` over one `path` (`:563+`); `cordis_inspect_*` splits into three tools but the *scope* is the discriminator, not an enum.
- *Many tools*: `terminal_*` (six, distinct arguments and lifecycles), `job_*` (three), `schedule_*` (three), `automation_*` (three).
- *Hybrid — one tool, a boolean discriminator, and a `oneOf` output*: `automation_set_enabled(enabled, rule_id? | kill_switch?)`, whose cross-field rule is enforced inside `execute` (`src/index.ts:561-570`) and whose output is a two-arm `oneOf` discriminated by a `const` `scope` (`:529-559`). This is the closest precedent for "one desktop tool that minimizes/restores/closes" versus separate tools.

There are **three** composition points, and which one applies depends on whether the agent is process-wide or per-session:

## The face as shipped

`ctx.notes` (`packages/client/ui-note/src/client/contract/notes.ts`) — `state: SnapshotStore&lt;NotesViewState{phase,summaries}&gt;`, `note(id): ObservableSnapshot&lt;NoteDetailState&gt;`, `create(init?)`, `update(id, expectedRevision, set)`, `remove(id, expectedRevision)`, `refresh()`.

Four firmings of the spec'd face, each deliberate:

- **`NoteDetailState` is a discriminated union** (`{phase:'loading'} | {phase:'ready';record} | {phase:'missing'}`), not `{phase, record?}`. With `record?` every reader needs a narrowing check that nothing can make fail — unreachable branches that the 100% per-file gate cannot pass.
- **Outcomes alias the Host unions**: `NoteWriteOutcome = NoteMutationResult | NoteUnreachable`, `NoteDeleteOutcome = NoteDeletionResult | NoteUnreachable`. They cannot drift from the seam, and the one added arm is honest — a carrier failure reached *no* Host verdict, so the caller says "not saved" rather than naming a refusal the Host never made.
- **`create` returns the full outcome**, not `NoteRecord | undefined`. Collapsing `note-limit` into `undefined` means pressing New note does nothing with no explanation; the list pane now shows the Host's own message.
- **`expectedRevision` is the caller's and is never re-derived at send time.** This is the crux: re-reading the held revision when the write leaves *is* the silent overwrite the no-retry rule exists to prevent. The chain still serializes writes per Note so answers install in order. Double-click protection lives where it belongs — the editor disables Save while one is in flight.

Conflicts are installed (so the editor can show what it is up against) and returned unretried. Live: `note/changed` re-reads the list always and the Note only when held-and-behind; `note/deleted` settles a held cell without a read; `connection/reset` → `reload()` re-reads the list and every held cell.

**Detail cells are marked `missing`, never pruned** — an open editor is subscribed to that exact store, and a Note recreated under the same id must be able to come back. Install ordering is guarded by a per-cell generation counter rather than revision comparison, because a deleted Note has no revision and a recreated one restarts at 0. Growth bound documented honestly in the README.

## UI structure

`NoteSurface.tsx` reads `launchState.noteId` and renders either `NoteList.tsx` (rows as a semantic `&lt;ul&gt;` of buttons — a listbox option cannot contain the row's own menu control) or `NoteEditor.tsx`. Row menu via ui-primitives `Menu`; delete confirm via `Modal` (not `RiskConfirmation`, which demands an acknowledgement checkbox — over-heavy for deleting your own note).

The conflict banner covers **both** ways of learning the Note moved: a save that came back `conflict`, and a Note that advanced under an unsaved draft (tracked by `baseRevision`). While it stands, plain Save is disabled — otherwise Save would carry the draft onto the very revision the banner warns about. Reload discards the draft; Overwrite resends at `banner.revision`. The per-Window draft is tagged with its Note (`subject`), so a Window switching notes can never leak one draft onto another.

Two deviations from D10's parentheticals: the bound view **replaces** the list with a header Back control rather than collapsing it to a sidebar rail (a rail duplicating a list the Back button already reaches earns nothing at v1), and the deleted-notice offers Close-window only, since Back is already in the header.

# Phase 4 review — Notes vertical slice + desktop tools

**What I ran:** focused suites for note/desktop/ui-note/tool/bundle packages — **308 tests, 23 files, pass**; the two headless scenarios via `test:snapshot` — **18 tests pass, keyless, exit 0**; `npm run typecheck` — **exit 0**; scoped coverage on the new packages — **100% (678/678 stmts, 324/324 branches)**; `duplication` — **green (0 TS clones)**; `verify-cordis-config` — **142 files pass**; `verify-client-domain-graph` — exit 1, 17 violations, **zero in ui-note**.
**Not run:** the two web lanes (need an official build) — those findings are a static audit and are labelled as such.

---

## VERDICT Q1 — host-plane rows are correct; the preset alternative is structurally unavailable

**The alternative fails hard, and the repo already pins it.** `mountPreset` does not tolerate a pending row:

- `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:295` — `Object.keys(fiber.inject).filter(name =&gt; fiber.ctx.get(name) === undefined)`
- `mount.ts:357-359` — throws `N row(s) did not activate:\n…waiting for &lt;name&gt;`
- `mount.ts:369-380` — the catch disposes the whole subtree and rethrows `PresetMountError`

The repo's own tests pin both halves: `tests/mount.spec.ts:251-254` rejects with `/waiting for serviceThatDoesNotExist/`, and `:236-241` proves full rollback — `ctx.agents.get(...)` is `undefined`. So the answer to the directed sub-question is: **not a warning, not "session works minus the tool" — the agent is never created.**

`tool-note` and `tool-desktop` declare `inject = ['tools','notes']` / `['tools','desktop']` (`src/index.ts:21` each). `vendor/cordis/src/registry.ts:71-77` shows the array form normalizes to **required** keys. My probe confirms empirically:

```
row applied?      false
fiber.inject keys = ["tools","notes"]
inactiveRows() reports = waiting for tools, notes
```

And the preset is genuinely shared: `HOST_PROFILE_BUNDLES` (which carries `agent-standard`) is in **every** profile — `PROFILE_TEMPLATES.web`, `.headless`, and `DEFAULT_PROFILE_BUNDLES` (`profile.ts:114-158`). A `tool-note` row in `standard/agent.cordis.yml` would therefore break **every CLI and headless session**, not just deny a tool.

The one escape hatch is real but wrong to take: `disabled: !!js` evaluates against the entry's Context (`vendor/loader/src/config/entry.ts:104-111` → `evaluate(this.ctx, expr)` → `with (ctx) { eval(expr) }`), and `inactiveRows` skips disabled entries (`mount.ts:286`), so `disabled: !!js !get('notes')` would work. But every existing use is a static process fact (`process.platform`), the expression is read at entry init with no re-evaluation when a service arrives later, and it would make a preset's tool list depend on host composition order. Not a safe swap.

**Verdict: keep the host-plane bundle rows.** The rewritten pin's reasoning is sound — these tools mutate deployment-owned durable records not keyed by session, and ship in the same bundle as the surfaces drawing them.

**What must change anyway:** the consequence was not followed through. `minimal/preset.yml` still says *"仅提供持久 bash 与 str_replace_editor 的双工具编码 Agent"* (a two-tool agent), and `minimal/agent.cordis.yml:1` still says *"a fixed-prompt, two-tool coding-agent composition"*. In the web profile both are now false — it is ten. Fix the two descriptions, and record the global-layer decision in an Agent Note (see finding 15). If `minimal` is meant to hold an exactly-closed catalog, that needs a per-preset opt-out in the tool registry — a follow-up, not this PR.

---

## VERDICT Q2 — placement belongs host-side, in `desktop-domain._openWindow`

Only one of four callers places anything. `DesktopRoot.onOpenSurface` (`DesktopRoot.tsx:103-120`) opens, diffs the window set, then issues a **second** mutation `updateWindow(opened.id, {mode:'floating', bounds: cascadeBounds(before.length)})`, skipping when `before.length === 0`. The other three do a bare open:

- `packages/client/ui-note/src/client/index.ts:158` (new)
- `packages/client/ui-chat-surface/src/client/index.ts:283` (pre-existing — not in this diff)
- `packages/desktop/tool-desktop/src/index.ts:470` — **the tool, which has no client at all**

**Put it in the host.** Five reasons, each with evidence:

1. **The tool cannot be reached by client policy.** `desktop_open_window` will always full-screen over the user's work — precisely the Phase-4 exit-criterion scenario, a Notes window open beside Chat.
2. **The host already owns every input.** `_openWindow` holds `current.windows` at the commit point and already computes `nextZOrder(current.windows)` (`desktop-domain/src/index.ts:288`); `buildWindow` already applies `mode: definition.defaultPlacement` (`:439`). Placement for the *first* window is already a host decision.
3. **The host already owns the geometry.** `DEFAULT_FLOATING_BOUNDS` lives at `desktop-domain/src/index.ts:57`, and `chrome.ts:66-73` documents its client copy as a mirror *"never to decide what gets stored."*
4. **Atomicity.** The two-step bumps two revisions per open, flashes a full-screen window, and leaves it permanently `full` if the second call is lost to a disconnect or conflict.
5. **Reload determinism.** Placement decided once at commit means the stored record is right the first time, not contingent on a client that may never run the follow-up.

**D8 survives exactly:** `current.windows.length === 0` → keep `definition.defaultPlacement`. Identical predicate to `before.length === 0`.

**Minimal change:** move `CASCADE_STEP`/`CASCADE_WRAP`/`cascadeBounds` into desktop-domain beside `DEFAULT_FLOATING_BOUNDS`; in `_openWindow`, when `current.windows.length &gt; 0`, build with `mode:'floating'` and `bounds: cascadeBounds(current.windows.length)`; delete `DesktopRoot.tsx:112-118`. `ui-note` and `ui-chat-surface` then need **no change** and get correct placement for free.

The one counter-argument — the host is viewport-blind — does not introduce a new class of problem: it is already viewport-blind for `DEFAULT_FLOATING_BOUNDS`, and `chrome.ts:53-58,112-115` draws one window full-bleed on a narrow frame regardless of the recorded rectangle.

## Findings

**1. BLOCKER — the conflict lane's post-Reload assertions run against the wrong Window.**
`apps/web/tests/notes-window.e2e.ts:245` caches Window B from `windowAtOrigin`, then clicks Reload at `:268`. B is not focused (A was raised at `:214`; `.fill()` does not raise — the only trigger is `onPointerDownCapture`, `DesktopWindow.tsx:83`). The click fires `onFocus` → `focusWindow` → `DesktopFrame` re-sorts by `zOrder` (`DesktopFrame.tsx:113`) and React reorders the keyed nodes. `windowAtOrigin` returns `windows.nth(index)` — **positional** (`desktop-windows.ts:349`) — so `other` silently re-points at Window A, where all four assertions at `:269-273` pass vacuously. A Reload that left B's banner up, kept B's draft, or restored the wrong text still goes green. Because the reorder lands on an RPC reply, which Window gets asserted is a genuine race.
*Remedy:* re-resolve immediately before `:269` (`const resolved = await peer()`); never store a `windowAtOrigin` result across a click.

**2. MAJOR — `desktop_list` orders and cuts by array position, not `zOrder`; its own invariant comment is false.**
`tool-desktop/src/index.ts:417-419` does `snapshot.windows.slice(-limit)` and renders `"Windows, backmost first"` / `"the N frontmost of M open"` (`:301-304`). But `_focusWindow` raises `zOrder` **in place** via `.map()` (`desktop-domain/src/index.ts:344`), so array order stops tracking `zOrder` the moment any window is focused. The sibling client knows this and does the opposite: `DesktopFrame.placeWindows` sorts defensively — *"the record order is sorted by `zOrder` here rather than relied on"* (`DesktopFrame.tsx:102,113`).
Consequences: at default config the model is told a false stacking order on every session after the first focus; with `maxListedWindows` lowered, the comment's stated safety property (`:413-416`, "dropping the front would answer with a `focusedWindowId` naming a Window absent from the same result") **fails** — open W1,W2,W3, focus W1 (zOrder→3, array position unchanged), `slice(-2)` returns W2,W3 and omits the focused window.
The test masks it: `tests/tool-desktop.spec.ts:381-402` seeds via a loop so array order == `zOrder` order and never focuses anything — its own comment names the mechanism it does not exercise.
*Remedy:* `[...snapshot.windows].sort((l, r) =&gt; l.zOrder - r.zOrder).slice(-limit)`, and add a focus-then-list case.

**3. MAJOR — `windowAtOrigin` documents the opposite of what it returns.**
`apps/web/tests/desktop-windows.ts:334-353`: the JSDoc promises an origin "does not move when a Window is raised… Resolved on every call rather than cached for that same reason", but it hands back an index-bound locator that decays exactly as promised it would not. Root cause of finding 1, and invisible in review.
*Remedy:* return a locator that re-derives by origin, or state that the result must not outlive a click.

**4. MAJOR — the headless note scenario does not exercise the returned revision.**
`examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/note-tools/replay.override.json:36-37` scripts `"expected_revision":0` as a literal, while the scenario's own prompt (`input.json:5`) says *"at the revision you read"*. The note id on the same call **is** recovered via `{{fromRequest:}}`, so the honest form is available and already in use. A `note_read` reporting revision 7 over a store holding 0 would still let the update succeed. The CAS data path is real (`tool-note/src/index.ts:530,536-543`); it just isn't fed from the result.
*Remedy:* `"expected_revision":{{fromRequest:at revision ([0-9]+)\.}}`.

**5. MAJOR — `notes-window`'s cross-window propagation claim is not proven.**
`notes-window.e2e.ts:227-228` claims "the committed revision was published and it pulled the Note back", but both Windows read **one shared in-page cell** — `notes.note(noteId)` over a single `NotesMirror` (`ui-note/src/client/index.ts:86,131,151`), and A's own save installs the record directly via `installWritten` (`service.ts:275-282,310-315`). Deleting the `$on('note/changed')` wiring at `index.ts:134` leaves both tests green. The observable behaviour (two Windows agree, no reload) is genuinely proven; the stated mechanism is not.
*Remedy:* drive one propagation step from outside the browser (`scaffold.ctx.notes.update(...)`), or re-word the claim.
*Note:* `notes-agent-round` **is** honest here — the audit traced the only path to the new body as `note/changed → receiveChanged → isBehind(2&gt;1) → pull → read → install`, with one `page.goto` in `beforeAll` and no reload anywhere.

**6. MAJOR — the minimal preset's own copy is now false.** See Q1. `minimal/preset.yml` and `minimal/agent.cordis.yml:1` both still promise two tools.

**7. MAJOR — the eleventh list: nine prose spots still describe the web profile as seven bundles.**
`apps/cli/reference/README.md:11,13` (+ `.zh.md`), `docs/architecture.md:25` (+ `.zh.md`), `packages/bundle/README.md:17-19` (+ `.zh.md`, no `app-notes/` row), `packages/bundle/web-platform/README.md:5`, `packages/bundle/web-platform/cordis.patch.yml:6`. The CLI reference tells an operator the `web` profile has seven layers; a user who hand-writes that list gets silently rewritten to eight by `normalizeShippedProfile`, which will read as corruption.
*Remedy:* update all nine (both languages) and add the `app-notes/` bundle-table row.
**The other ten lists are VERIFIED CORRECT** and killed — profile.ts:128, scaffold.ts:106, assembled-boot.ts:52, verify-cordis-config.ts:143, built-bin.e2e.ts:749, lazy-search-startup:28, windows-shell:48, web-agent-presets:30, apps/cli package.json:31 + tsconfig:33, profile.spec.ts:178-215 — plus both extras (built-boot:131, smoke-real:148) and two more the sweep caught unprompted (shipped-composition:34-46, minimal-preset.snapshot:117-127).

**8. MINOR — `conflictMessage` embeds a raw epoch, contradicting the package's own rule 60 lines away.**
`tool-note/src/index.ts:230` renders `(last changed at ${record.updatedAt})` — e.g. `1756312800000`. `renderNotes` states the opposite rule at `:281-284`: *"no line spells out a wall-clock time the model would have to interpret; `updatedAt` stays in the value."* The retry is built from the revision alone; the epoch is unusable to the model and is a latent snapshot-flake vector. Not currently snapshotted (grep for `last changed at` across all goldens: no hits).
*Remedy:* drop the `(last changed at …)` clause.

**9. MINOR — `ui-note`'s Open-in-new-window has no placement step.** `ui-note/src/client/index.ts:158`. Replicates the pre-existing `ui-chat-surface:283` defect; fixed for free by the Q2 host-side change.

**10. MINOR — a dirty draft can silently overwrite a recreated same-id note.**
The mirror's generation counter guards the cell and explicitly reasons about recreation (`manager.ts:8-12`), but the window store's `baseRevision` is an untagged bare number (`stores.ts:39`). If a note is deleted while a draft is dirty and then recreated under the same id (reachable via the tool's client-chosen id) and reaches the *same* revision, `rebased` is false, the banner never appears, Save is enabled, and the host CAS passes — the old draft lands on an unrelated note. Narrow, but the generation counter exists for exactly this class.
*Remedy:* clear `subject`/draft when the cell transitions to `missing` (the draft is already unreachable in that phase), or tag `baseRevision` with the cell generation.

**11. MINOR — `{{fromRequest:}}` patterns are order-dependent and truncation-prone.**
`resolveFromRequest` takes the **last** corpus match (`llm-replay/src/index.ts:356-361`) while `desktop_list`/`note_list` render every record, so with two records `desktop-[0-9a-f-]+` silently resolves to the least-recently-opened one. Separately, `note-[0-9a-f-]+` matches the first hex run after any literal `note-`, and the `note_read` result embeds the **body** after the id in the same leaf — a body containing `note-abc` retargets the next call. Safe today only because each scenario runs in a fresh temp cwd with one record.
*Remedy:* anchor on the unique result sentence with a capture group, or pin the full UUID shape.

**12. MINOR — `seed-desktop.ts:27-29` sets its guard flag before the await**, so a second concurrent `agent/pre-step` would not wait. Unreachable in this single-agent scenario; the repo's fence fixtures use `Promise.withResolvers` correctly. *Remedy:* `seeded ??= ctx.desktop.resolve({}); await seeded`.

**13. MINOR — two e2e settle races.** `notes-window.e2e.ts:205-207` starts a move before the resize is proven committed and then calls a non-retrying `windowAtOrigin` (the mature `desktop-window-management.e2e.ts:144-151` polls after every drag); `notes-agent-round.e2e.ts:192` reads `data-state` one-shot before the settling polls.

**14. MINOR — `desktop.cordis.yml` is inert as shipped.** No seeder (correct — that is snapshot-only) plus a cwd-local `root: './.storage'` (`:16-17`) means a live run finds no Desktop and `desktop_list` returns `(no desktops)`, while the header comment advertises a shared storage root.

**15. INFO — the N6 documentation/generator backlog is real but correctly deferred.** Sequencing is N1→N2∥N3→N4→**N5 (this review)**→N6, so these are not defects yet — but the list is longer than D14 enumerates, and two items would be missed:
- Gate failures awaiting N6: `gen-doc-graphs` **crashes** (`SERVICE_ROLES` has no `notes` entry, `scripts/gen-doc-graphs.ts:665`); `gen-cordis-catalog` **crashes** (`docs/subsystems/note.md` mapped at `:75,:186` and 11 `LINK_MAP` rows, never created); `docs/module-graph.md`, `docs/config-catalog.md` and the generated client slot catalog are stale; `verify-translation-pairing` fails with 10 violations (seven new English-only READMEs; `docs/tool-catalog.zh.md` omits all eight new tools); `verify-md-links` fails with 2. Note `verify-module-graph` runs in **ci-static, ci-primary and ci-linux-primary**, not only doc-sync.
- **Not in D14, easy to miss:** `gen-doc-graphs.ts:517-523` — the `desktop` role entry omits `tool-desktop` and its `note` field still says the model-facing Consumer "is Phase 4 of the desktop plan", which this change shipped. And `packages/note/` has no group README triplet (every other group has one), plus `packages/client/README.md` has no `ui-note/` row and `packages/desktop/README.md` no `tool-desktop/` row.
- One genuine path bug already latent: `packages/client/ui-note/README.md:40` links `../../note-domain/README.md`; the correct path is `../../note/note-domain/README.md`.
- Also absent: the Phase-4 Agent Note (phases 2 and 3 each shipped one). The global-tool-layer decision currently lives only in a test comment.

INFO — the flagged duplication is correctly deferred.** `duplication` is green: the note-domain/desktop-domain tails are suppressed by `jscpd:ignore` with a written justification naming the right future owner (`note-domain/src/index.ts:323-329` — *"a common owner belongs in `dsh-storage-domain`… two providers do not yet establish the key and lifetime that owner would have to fit"*). The `genericCall` triplication carries an explicit `TODO(tools)` at both sites correctly scoping it as a change to `dsh-tools`' public API. Both judgements are right — extraction on two/three instances would be premature. Recommend revisiting the tails owner at a third provider.

## Candidates killed (verified, with handling code)

- **`empty-update` missing from `NoteMutationCode`** — deliberate and documented: the `.refine()` at `note/src/records.ts:80-83` refuses it at validation, and `types.ts:128-131` explains why contract-level bounds are not deployment codes. Better than the spec.
- **Create idempotency gap for server-minted ids** — honestly documented at `types.ts:70-74`; replay is impossible by construction without a caller id, and it says so.
- **Delete non-idempotency + the `note/deleted` invariant on replay** — documented at `note-domain/src/index.ts:230-235`; a replay after success reads `missing-note` via `onStoredNote`, so nothing announces a deletion that did not happen.
- **`note-limit` off-by-one** — `table.size &gt;= maxNotes` with `maxNotes:1` correctly admits exactly one.
- **UTF-8 body bounds** — `Buffer.byteLength(body,'utf8')` (`:253`).
- **`note_read` byte windows splitting code points** — `sliceBody` (`tool-note:188-202`) advances `start` off continuation bytes and backs `end` off them; `continuesCodePoint` is `(byte &amp; 0xc0) === 0x80`. The "first character larger than `max_bytes`" case returns empty **and** `truncated:true` rather than letting the model page over unseen text (`:174-182`, `renderWindow:307-311`). Bounds apply to emitted values only (`Math.min(requested ?? max, max)`).
- **`desktop_window` restore mirroring `chrome.ts`** — `restoredMode` (`tool-desktop:239-241`) is byte-equivalent to `restorePlacement` (`chrome.ts:192-195`), with the non-minimized no-op guard at `:566` and the mirror documented at `:229-235`.
- **Tails drain / publish containment / publish-at-commit** — admission closes before the drain, `enqueue`'s tail-identity guard is correct, both emits are try/caught after the durable write.
- **Fixture parity** — `fixture.ts:3420+` mirrors CAS, `lastMutationId` replay, `conflict`, and `missing-note`; the one omission (config-varying `note-limit`/`body-too-large`) is stated with its reason at `:3414-3418`.
- **N3's crux — no path re-derives `expectedRevision` at send.** `sendUpdate` passes the caller's value straight through (`service.ts:271-283`), and the editor's plain Save is provably equivalent to the draft base: Save is disabled whenever `banner !== null`, and `rebased` is true exactly when `current.revision !== win.baseRevision` (`NoteEditor.tsx:135,155`), so an enabled Save implies they are equal. *(Passing `win.baseRevision` directly would make this direct rather than inferred — worth a comment.)*
- **Overwrite** resends at `banner.revision` once (`:188`), guarded by `disabled={saving}` and, more importantly, by the host CAS — a double-click's second write conflicts rather than double-applying.

## Deviations from the spec, with rationale

1. **Two serialization lanes, one tail map.** Spec §3b puts `harness.storage` writes "under the plugin's operation tail". A host half that `await`s `harness.storage.get(...)` during activation would then deadlock against the transaction activating it. I kept one `operationTails` map and one `enqueue`, keyed by lane: `plugins:&lt;id&gt;` for registry transactions, `data:&lt;id&gt;` for that plugin's storage. `BOOT_READ_HOST` pins the case.
2. **Whole transaction inside the lane.** Rollback/enable/uninstall run load → candidate start → put → run swap inside the plugin lane; a promotion's candidate still starts outside it (the page handshake requires that), and only put → swap is in the lane. This removed an unreachable "record vanished mid-transaction" branch.
3. **A first install mints its `PersonalPluginId` when the request is armed**, not at commit (spec §3c COMMIT step 1). The candidate's host half — and its namespaced storage — runs before any record exists.
4. **`promotedAt: number`**, not `number | null`; the spec's own parenthetical says entries exist only for committed packages.
5. **`committed.runId` is `PersonalPluginRunId | null` with optional `diagnostics`** on both promotion and rollback: a commit whose Surface registration is refused installs the record but produces no run. Same for `PersonalPluginEnableResult`.
6. **`PromotionTargetView.existing.currentPackageId` is nullable** — a target can be uninstalled while its promotion is armed (tested; approving then reinstalls under the same id).
7. **`rollback` refuses a disabled plugin** (`code: 'disabled'`), so "prove the previous package comes up" stays meaningful.
8. **`setEnabled` is idempotent** — an unchanged request writes nothing and publishes nothing.
9. **`uninstall` publishes `personal-plugin/changed` at `revision + 1`** so a roster reconcile learns about removals without a third event; the invariant treats a removal as the one announcement with nothing to read back.
10. **Surfaces are registered from the service fiber with disposers held on the run**, not "on the candidate's fiber" — client-only packages have no fiber, and the run must own withdrawal deterministically either way.
11. **The one-pending-per-target check runs right after target resolution**, before the collision/bounds/store work.
12. **No own "package carries neither half" check** — the package store's artifact schema refuses it as `package-rejected`.
13. **`tsconfig.base.json` gained two `paths` entries** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-package-store/types`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-registry/types`). Required: the Typert generator refuses a Remote boundary type imported from a package root (`PluginPackageId must be exported from a public non-root type subpath`), and `types.ts` must stay client-plane-importable.
14. **Two `jscpd:ignore` fences** in `activation.ts` (`errorDetails`, `runHandle`): `cordis-host-runner` keeps its equivalents private, so `duplication` flagged them. Recorded as a README limitation.

2. **Rollback calls `rollbackForAgent(agent, pluginId)`** — the registry's in-process Agent-attributed entry point — not an optional-agent overload of `rollback`.
3. **Manifest validation is delegated.** The tool locally validates only the three id arguments it brands; `name`/`purpose`/`surfaces`/`storage_schema_version` go to the registry's zod `promotionManifestInput`, whose `invalid-manifest` refusal names the offending field. Duplicating those rules would let the two drift.
4. **`presentPluginCall` takes `kind`** (`read` for the two listings, `execute` for the two mutations), so it is not byte-identical to tool-note's `kind: 'other'` copy. It keeps the jscpd fence and the `TODO(tools)` marker, worded for this copy.
5. **`maxInspectBytes` bounds the complete emitted result**, measured on its JSON encoding, not the source alone. The record summary is never cut (small, and it is what the model acts on); the host half fills first, then the browser half. Truncation walks code points at their exact JSON-encoded cost, so a character is whole or absent.

## What was built

**`packages/plugin-runtime/personal-client-runner` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-personal-client-runner`)** — a two-entry client package modelled on `cordis-client-runner`:

- `src/index.ts` — node half, empty `apply` so the cordis.yml row exists.
- `src/invariant.ts` — explained empty installer (the owned relation spans a page and a host process; not observable from the node plane).
- `src/client/index.ts` — the plugin: `inject = ['loader','modules','slots','remote','remote.personalPlugins']`, the `RemoteResult`-unwrapping host seam, per-code teaching errors for `invoke` (a `Record` keyed by refusal code rather than an if-chain, so every arm is total and covered), the `ctx.personalPluginRunner` face declaration, and the event wiring (`personal-plugin/changed` → roster pull, `personal-plugin/promotion` → promotions pull, `connection/reset` and activation → both). Every verb reads `ctx.remote.personalPlugins` at call time; no client `timer` service is provided.
- `src/client/runner.ts` — one `DynamicCordisPackageRunner` with `modulePrefix: 'personal'`, the reconcile loop, and the approval orchestration.
- `tests/bench.client.ts` + `roster|routing|promotion.client.spec.ts` — 38 jsdom specs over a real `SlotRegistry`, real cordis fibers behind a stand-in loader, and a fake `personalPlugins` namespace.
- README trio, pairing recorded via `verify-translation-pairing --write`.

## Key design decisions

- **Mounts are keyed by `PersonalPluginId`, taken from `getClientCode`'s answer** (`PersonalPluginClientSource.pluginId`). The registry mints the id when it *arms* a request — even for a first install — so a candidate mounts under the id it will commit under and the post-commit reconcile is a no-op for both new installs and updates. No requestId-keyed provisional mounts, no remount after commit (both paths tested).
- **Convergence is by activation, serialized on one lane** (`lane.then(op)`), mirroring the engine's own per-package queue one level up: a roster pull arriving mid-approval runs *after* it, so no reconcile can unload an unsettled candidate. Public entry points enqueue; internal steps call `reconcile`/`pullPromotions` directly (no self-deadlock).
- **Failure unwinding rides convergence**: after `resolvePromotion(ok:false)` (or a non-committed answer to `ok:true`) the final reconcile sees a runId mismatch and re-mounts whatever the host still runs.
- **Brand seam**: the shared engine keys by the draft runtime's branded ids. The five crossings take plain `string` (a legal narrowing, no double assertion) and sit together in one commented block.
- Deviations worth naming: (1) `surfaceId` on a render report is the crashed entry's **slot**, because the supervision seam carries no registration key — documented in Known Limitations; (2) a roster-path mount failure has no host carrier (the registry only records client failures for an approval it awaits) — logged page-locally, retried on the next pull, documented.

## Files touched outside the package

`tsconfig.client.json` (project reference) and `tsconfig.base.json` (one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-personal-client-runner/client` paths entry — needed because only `packages/client/*` has a `/client` wildcard; the root and `/invariant` are covered by the existing `plugin-runtime/*` wildcards). No `vitest.config.ts` change was needed — the package reaches per-file 100% with no exclusion. No `scripts/verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts` allowlist entry either: the package authors genuinely model-visible text (the candidate-load message the registry steers to the asking Agent, and the render-failure text `plugin_inspect` shows), so the README carries two full structured Model Experience entries, matching `cordis-client-runner`'s classification.

# Agentic Web Desktop — Cordis Context Topology Map

## Headline finding

**There is no per-app and no per-window Cordis context anywhere.** The Desktop, Chat, Notes, Settings, and the Plugin Studio all live as *rows in one flat Host tree* and *rows in one flat Client tree*. The only real context nesting in the system is the **per-agent/per-session scope chain** (`dsh-scope` + preset standing mounts). "Apps" are a *composition-layer* concept (a bundle patch layer) plus a *runtime registry* concept (a `SurfaceDefinition` on `ctx.desktop` + a keyed slot registration in the browser) — not a context concept.

---

## (a) Runtime context topology

### Host process (one per `dsh --profile web`)

```
Context (root)                                    packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:764
├─ Loader                                         (ctx.plugin(Loader), :771)
└─ cordis:include root  →  the composed entry list (flat, ~150 rows)
   ├─ runtime-core rows        (session persistence, model route, storage, tools/systemPrompt registries…)
   ├─ agent-standard rows
   ├─ local-machine rows
   ├─ web-platform rows        (webserver, api-gateway, connection, client roster)
   ├─ desktop-shell rows       desktop-domain, tool-desktop, desktop-runtime, ui-desktop
   ├─ app-chat rows            surface-chat, workspace, session-*, ~30 ui-* rows, agent-presets
   ├─ app-settings rows
   ├─ app-notes rows           note-domain, surface-note, tool-note, ui-note
   └─ personal-plugin-runtime  plugin-package-store, plugin-registry, surface-plugin-studio,
                               plugin-mode-redirect, personal-client-runner, ui-plugin-studio
   ├─ [group fiber] "cordis-dynamic"    extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/index.ts:1245
   │     └─ one child fiber per *ephemeral draft* plugin host half
   └─ [group fiber] "personal-plugins"  plugin-runtime/plugin-registry/src/index.ts:1366
         └─ one child fiber per *installed durable* plugin host half

Per-preset standing scopes (siblings, minted lazily, one per preset id):
  createScope(agentPresetsCtx, {agentPreset:id})   preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts:515
    └─ PresetTree (an Include subtree of agent.cordis.yml)   preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:350
         └─ rows may declare `isolate:` realms via cordis:group

Per-session agent scopes (one per live Agent):
  createScope(loopCtx, agent)                      core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:94
  ctx = scope.ctx.extend({ agent })                                        :95
  scope key's *scope parent* = the standing preset key  (bindScopeParent)
     preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts:286 / :323 / :467
```

Crucially, the agent's scope **fiber** hangs off the agent-loop context, while its **preset composition** hangs off a *sibling* standing fiber. The two are joined only by the `dsh-scope` parent relation (`packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:39-102`), which is a `WeakMap`, not a Cordis fiber link. Registry views (`ScopedLayers.chainLayers`, `packages/core/scope/src/store.ts:192`) and event routing (`scopeTarget`, `:170`) walk that relation.

### Browser page (one per tab)

```
Context (root)                                    packages/client/web/src/boot.ts:70
├─ Loader over window.__DSH_BOOT__ roster (flat; every `dsh.client` row is one entry)
├─ ui-desktop → declares slot 'desktop.window.surface' (keyed, root-scope)
│                                    client/ui-desktop/src/client/DesktopRoot.tsx:24
├─ ui-chat-surface   → registers under key 'chat'
├─ ui-note           → registers under key 'note'
├─ ui-plugin-studio  → registers under key for the Studio surface
└─ personal-client-runner → creates *more loader entries* for installed plugins' browser halves
                            (plugin-runtime/personal-client-runner/src/client/runner.ts:391 via
                             extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/runtime.ts:391)

Per-session client scopes (identity-keyed, not object-keyed):
  createScope(rootCtx, sessionId)   client/session-runtime/src/client/scope.ts:55, service.ts:666
```

A **Window is not a context**. Per-window state rides an `instanceKey` axis on keyed slot dispatch, where the instance key *is the Window id*:
- `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:468-480` (store instance resolution: `record.scope === 'root' ? instanceKey ?? 'root' : sessionId`)
- `packages/client/runtime/src/client/slots.ts:306` `pruneStoreInstance(instanceKey)`, called from `DesktopRoot.tsx:124` when a Window leaves the Desktop
- `packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/scoped-slots.tsx:195-246` (per-instance inject-face caches)

| Plane | File | Defines |
|---|---|---|
| Profile template (what a `web` install composes) | `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts:114` (`HOST_PROFILE_BUNDLES`), `:121` (`PROFILE_TEMPLATES.web` = runtime-core, agent-standard, local-machine, web-platform, **desktop-shell, app-chat, app-settings, app-notes, personal-plugin-runtime**) | the nine ordered patch layers |

| Desktop | `packages/bundle/desktop-shell/cordis.patch.yml` — 4 rows: `desktop-domain` (:16), `tool-desktop` (:23), `desktop-runtime` (:26), `ui-desktop` (:29). Names **no** Surface. | |
